## Dental recall reminders: following up patients who don't book
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/dental-recall-follow-up/

Dental recall reminders tell a patient they are due their next check-up and ask them to book. Most practice software already sends the first reminder; the patients who slip away are the ones who ignore it. A simple follow-up sequence closes that gap: a second reminder, a different channel, and then a weekly list of overdue patients for a person at the front desk to call or close off.

Dental recall reminders usually work for the patients who were going to book anyway. The rest open the text, mean to call, and forget. Six months later they are a year overdue, and nobody at the practice noticed because the software sent its one reminder and moved on. This page is for small UK and US practices. It gives a recall follow-up sequence, messages to copy, and a clear split between what a system can send and what your team should handle. It doesn't tell you how often patients should come in: that's the dentist's call for each patient.

### Why recall reminders lose patients
- The software sends one reminder, sometimes two, then stops. Nobody owns the patients who didn't reply.
- Reminders go to an old mobile number or an email nobody reads, and the bounce is never checked.
- The patient replies "I'll call next week" to a no-reply address, and the reply goes nowhere.
- The overdue report exists, but it runs to hundreds of names, so nobody works through it.
- Families are split: one parent books for three children, and one child is quietly missed.

### Who sets the recall interval
The interval is a clinical decision, not an admin one. The NHS says the time between check-ups can vary from 3 months to 2 years, and up to 1 year if you're under 18, and that your dentist should suggest when your next check-up is (nhs.uk, page last reviewed April 2025). Outside the NHS, the dentist still sets it for each patient. So the automation never decides when someone is due. It reads the recall date the dentist set in your practice system and works from that. If the date is wrong or missing, the fix is at the chair, not in the reminders.

### A recall follow-up sequence
For illustration, this counts from the recall due date your dentist set. Change the gaps to suit your practice and your patients. Every step stops the moment the patient books.
| When | Channel | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 weeks before due | Text or email (your software's usual reminder) | You're due a check-up, here's how to book. |
| Due date, not booked | The other channel | A short second reminder with a direct booking link or phone number. |
| 2 weeks after due | Text | A friendly nudge that offers two or three real appointment slots. |
| 4 weeks after due | Front desk call list | The patient goes on this week's call list with their history, so a person can ring them. |
| After the call | Recorded by a person | Booked, will call back on a date, moved away, gone elsewhere or asked not to be contacted. The list updates. |
| 3 months after due, no answer | One last letter or email | A short note that you'd still like to see them. Then the patient is marked lapsed and leaves the active list. |

### Second reminder for a patient who hasn't booked
Text or email (edit the wording to suit your practice):
```
Hi [First name], this is [Practice name]. Our records show you're due your check-up with [Dentist name] and we haven't got you booked in yet.

You can book here: [booking link], or call us on [phone number].

If you've moved or now see another dentist, just reply and let us know so we can update your record.

Thanks,
[Practice name]
```

### Front desk call notes
A short script for the weekly call list:
```
"Hi, is that [First name]? It's [Your name] from [Practice name]. You're due a check-up with [Dentist name] and I wanted to see if we can find you a time. I've got [day and time] or [day and time], would either of those work?"

If no: "No problem. Would it help if I called you back in a couple of weeks, or would you rather book online when you're ready?"

Record one of: booked / call back on [date] / will book online / moved away / registered elsewhere / please don't contact.
```

### What to automate and what to keep with a person
1. Read recall dates from your practice system each week, never from a separate spreadsheet that drifts out of date. The same habit keeps [hearing care recall reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/hearing-care-recall-reminders/) accurate.
2. Send the second and third reminders on the right channel, and stop them as soon as a booking appears.
3. Catch bounced emails and failed texts, and put those patients straight on the call list with a note to update their details.
4. Build one short weekly call list, oldest overdue first, with family members grouped so one call covers the household. Patients with [unbooked treatment plans](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/dental-treatment-plan-follow-up/) can go on the same list, so one person works both.
5. Record every call outcome in the same place, so nobody is called twice and "please don't contact" is respected everywhere.
6. Keep these with a person: anything clinical, a patient who is anxious or unhappy, complaints, and any decision to mark someone lapsed.

### Keep messages short and private
Recall messages can be read by anyone who picks up the phone or opens a shared inbox. Keep them to the practice name, the fact that a check-up is due, and how to book. Leave out treatment details, outstanding balances and anything clinical. If a patient asks to be contacted a different way, or not at all, record it once and make sure every reminder follows it. Practice owners should check their own data protection and patient privacy obligations before changing how patients are contacted; this isn't legal advice.

### If your practice software already does recalls
Most dental practice systems have recall reminders built in. Switch them on and use them first. The gap is usually what happens after the second reminder: the overdue list nobody works through, the replies that land nowhere, and the patients with wrong contact details. Clinics see the same gap with [physio rebooking reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/physio-rebooking-reminders/), and opticians with [eye test recalls](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/optician-eye-test-recall/). That's the part worth building, the same way [vet vaccination reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/vet-practice-vaccination-reminders/) and [patient intake forms](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/physio-clinic-patient-intake-forms/) work best when the system does the sending and a person handles the exceptions.

### How Mike Automations builds it
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how recalls run at your practice today and where patients slip through. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example "every patient past their recall date gets two follow-ups, and the front desk gets one call list every Monday". It's built on the tools you already use (your practice software where it allows a connection, your email and text service, Google Sheets or Excel), so your team has nothing new to learn. It goes live in 2-3 days, costs [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it. A person at the practice approves the wording of every message before anything is sent.

### How often should patients be recalled?
That's the dentist's decision for each patient, based on their oral health. The NHS says the gap between check-ups can be anywhere from 3 months to 2 years, and up to 1 year for under 18s. The reminders simply follow the recall date the dentist sets in your practice system.

### Will patients find extra reminders annoying?
Each reminder stops as soon as the patient books, so people who book straight away hear from you once. Only patients who haven't booked get the follow-ups, and anyone who asks not to be contacted is taken off every list.

### Do we need new practice software?
No. The follow-up runs alongside the system you already have, reading recall dates from it where it allows a connection, or from a regular export where it doesn't.

### Can AI write the messages or make the calls?
AI can help draft message wording or summarise a patient's recall history for the call list, but a person at the practice approves every message, and the calls are made by your team.

## Chasing candidate compliance documents: a checklist and chase plan for agencies
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/candidate-compliance-document-chasing/

Chasing candidate compliance documents means getting every document a candidate needs before they can start, such as right to work evidence, references, a DBS certificate where the role is eligible and proof of qualifications, then tracking what expires. A recruitment agency can run it from one checklist per role: an automatic request when the candidate is registered, reminders until each item arrives, and an expiry list so follow-up checks happen on time. A consultant still checks every document before the candidate is cleared.

Chasing candidate compliance documents is the job that stands between a placement and a start date. The client wants someone on Monday, the candidate has sent a passport photo but no references, and the DBS certificate is somewhere in an email thread. Below: example checklists by role, a chase sequence, messages to copy and what to automate, for small UK and US agencies. It sits next to our guide on [timesheet chasing for recruitment agencies](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/recruitment-timesheet-chasing/), which covers the weekly side once people are working.

### What the rules ask agencies to hold
Right to work (UK): the Home Office Employer's guide to right to work checks (1 October 2026 version) says the check must be done before employment starts, and an employment business supplying temps is the employer for that check. eVisa holders prove their right to work with a share code. Copies are kept for the whole employment and two years after. For time-limited permission, a follow-up check is due on or before the date it ends. The civil penalty is up to £60,000 per illegal worker. Suitability (England, Wales and Scotland): regulation 19 of the Conduct of Employment Agencies and Employment Businesses Regulations 2003 says you must confirm the candidate's identity, and that they have the experience, training, qualifications and any authorisation the hirer, the law or a professional body requires. For roles working with vulnerable people, regulation 22 adds two references from people who aren't relatives and copies of relevant qualifications offered to the hirer. DBS: gov.uk says standard and enhanced checks can only be requested where the specific role is eligible. US: USCIS says Section 2 of Form I-9 must be completed within 3 business days of the hire date. This is a summary, not legal advice.

### Example checklists by role
For illustration only. Your own list depends on the client, the role, the sector's rules and your contracts. Home care agencies have their own list: see [carer compliance for home care agencies](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/home-care-agency-carer-compliance/). Agree it with your compliance lead, then let the system chase against it. Immigration firms work the same way with a [document checklist for each visa or case type](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/immigration-law-firm-document-checklists/).
| Document | Office temp (UK) | Warehouse or driver (UK) | Care or education role (UK) | US light industrial |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Identity and right to work | Yes, before start | Yes, before start | Yes, before start | Form I-9, Section 2 within 3 business days |
| Follow-up right to work date | If permission is time-limited | If permission is time-limited | If permission is time-limited | Reverify if work authorization expires |
| References | As the client asks | As the client asks | Two, from non-relatives | As the client asks |
| Criminal record check | Usually none | Basic, if the client asks | Enhanced DBS, if the role is eligible | As the client and state law allow |
| Qualifications or licences | If the role needs them | Driving licence, licence checks, tickets | Relevant qualifications, copies offered to the client | Forklift or other certificates the role needs |
| Client-specific items | Signed terms, induction | Site induction, safety boots | Training certificates | Site induction |

### A chase sequence that stops when documents arrive
| When | Who gets it | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On registration | Candidate | One message listing only the documents their role needs, with an upload link or reply address. |
| Day 2 | Candidate | Reminder listing only what is still missing, nothing they've already sent. |
| Day 4 | Candidate's referees | Reference request, sent once the candidate gives referee details. |
| Day 5 | Candidate and consultant | Third reminder, plus a note to the consultant to call. |
| Day 7 | Referees who haven't replied | Reminder, then the consultant is told which reference is holding things up. |
| Before start | Consultant | Clear-to-start list: complete, waiting on documents, waiting on a check. Nobody starts until a person clears them. |
| 60, 30 and 7 days before expiry | Consultant and worker | Follow-up right to work check and expiring certificates, so nothing lapses mid-assignment. |

### Request to the candidate
Email or text (edit the wording to suit your agency):
```
Hi [First name], it's [Your name] at [Agency].

To get you cleared for [role] at [client or sector], we still need:

[missing item 1]
[missing item 2]

You can upload them here: [secure link]. For right to work, if you have an eVisa, please send a share code from gov.uk (it starts with W).

Once these are in, we can confirm your start date. If anything is a problem, reply and tell me.

Thanks,
[Your name]
```

### Reference request
Email to a referee:
```
Hi [Referee name],

[Candidate name] has named you as a referee for a [role] position through [Agency], and agreed the reference may be shared with our client.

Could you confirm their dates of employment, their role, and whether you'd re-employ them? A short reply is fine, or use this form: [link]. A reply by [date] would really help.

Thanks,
[Your name], [Agency], [phone number]
```

### What to automate and what to keep with a person
1. Keep one checklist per role type, agreed with your compliance lead. Each new candidate gets the list that matches their role.
2. Send the first request automatically, then remind only about what is still missing.
3. Save each document against the right candidate with the date received and any expiry date.
4. Build a daily clear-to-start list and a monthly expiry list, so follow-up checks and renewals are booked ahead. Security firms keep the same expiry list for [SIA licences and shift confirmations](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/security-company-licence-and-shift-confirmations/).
5. Keep these with a person: checking that documents are genuine, running the online right to work check, deciding whether a DBS check is eligible, reading references, and clearing anyone to start.

### If you already use recruitment software
Many recruitment systems have compliance checklists and uploads. Use them first. The gap is the chasing around them: reminders that stop when a document arrives, silent referees, and an expiry list someone reads. It's the same pattern as [right to rent follow-up check reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/right-to-rent-follow-up-check-reminders/) for letting agents: the dates are known, so the reminders can be too.

### How Mike Automations builds it
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how documents reach you today and where candidates get stuck. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example "every new candidate gets their role's list on registration, reminders stop when each item arrives, and the team gets a clear-to-start list every morning". It's built on the tools you already use (your email, your recruitment system where it allows a connection, Google Drive or SharePoint, Google Sheets or Excel), so your team has nothing new to learn. It goes live in 2-3 days, costs [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it. Review the [GDPR checklist before automating client data](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gdpr-checklist-automating-client-data/) too: candidate documents are personal data.

### Can automation do the right to work check for us?
No. A person must do the check the way the Home Office guide sets out: a manual document check, the online check with a share code, or a certified identity service where that's allowed. Automation requests the documents or share code, saves the record with the date, and reminds you when a follow-up check is due.

### When is a follow-up right to work check needed?
The Home Office guide says that if a worker has time-limited permission, you must re-check on or before the date it ends if you want to keep employing them. If the first check showed settled status or status under the EU Settlement Scheme, no follow-up check is needed.

### What about candidates who send documents on WhatsApp?
It happens. A secure upload link is safer, so documents don't sit on personal phones. If a photo arrives anyway, a person files it to the right record and deletes it from the chat.

## Gym failed payment follow-up that keeps the member
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/gym-failed-payment-follow-up/

Gym failed payment follow-up is the sequence a gym or fitness studio runs when a membership payment is declined or a Direct Debit fails: let the payment provider retry, send the member a friendly message with a link to update their card or bank details, and have a person call if the money still hasn't come in after about two weeks. Done well, it recovers the payment without making the member feel chased.

Gym failed payment follow-up is mostly a timing problem. A card expires or a bank account is short on the 1st, and the member still wants to train. If nobody tells them for three weeks, they either lose access at the desk with no warning or keep training unpaid until the debt is awkward to raise. A clear sequence, run the same way every time, fixes both. It sits alongside your general [payment reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/), but the tone is different: this is a member you want to keep, not an invoice to close.

### What your payment provider already does
Check this first, because your follow-up should fit around it, not fight it.
- Card payments on Stripe: Stripe's documentation (2026) says Smart Retries is on by default for new accounts and retries a failed subscription payment up to 8 times within 2 weeks. It does not retry hard declines such as a lost or stolen card: those need new card details from the member.
- Card updates: Stripe says it automatically tries to update saved cards when a bank issues a new one. This is widely supported for cards issued in the United States, and support in other countries varies. So in the UK, an expired card is more likely to reach you as a failed payment.
- UK Direct Debit through GoCardless: GoCardless's help centre says a payment can be re-submitted at most three times. Its Success+ feature only retries failures caused by insufficient funds, while the mandate is still active. If the member cancelled the mandate at their bank, no retry will work: they need to set up a new one.
- Bacs Direct Debit through Stripe: Stripe lists up to 2 retries within 30 days, for insufficient funds only. US bank (ACH) debits through Stripe: up to 2 retries within 40 days, also for insufficient funds only.
- Your gym management software may have its own retry and email settings. Find out what it sends, so members don't get two different messages about the same payment.

### A dunning sequence for membership payments
Dunning just means the steps you take to collect a payment that failed. Adjust the days to your billing cycle. This assumes a monthly membership:
| When | Who or what | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Day 0: payment fails | Payment provider | Automatic retry starts (card) or a retry is scheduled (Direct Debit, insufficient funds only) |
| Day 0 | Email and text | Friendly notice: the payment didn't go through, nothing is wrong with the membership, here's a link to update card or bank details |
| Day 3 | Text | Short reminder with the same link, only if still unpaid |
| Day 7 | Email | Second notice: the amount, what happens next and the date access may be paused |
| Day 10-14 | Staff member | Phone call or a word at the front desk if they're still training. The member goes on a call list |
| Day 14-21 | Your decision | Pause, freeze or cancel the membership under your terms. One last message says what happened and how to restart |

### Message templates that keep goodwill
Assume an honest mistake. Most failed payments are an expired card or a bank account that was short for a day. The same tone suits [martial arts school memberships](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/martial-arts-school-memberships-and-gradings/), where the person paying may be a parent rather than the student.
First notice, the day the payment fails (email or text):
```
Hi [first name], your [gym name] membership payment of [amount] on [date] didn't go through. It happens, usually a new card or a timing thing with the bank.

You can update your details here in under a minute: [secure update link]

Your membership carries on as normal while you sort it. Any questions, just reply.

[your name], [gym name]
```

### The second notice, a week later
Second notice, day 7 (email):
```
Subject: Your [gym name] membership payment

Hi [first name],

We still haven't been able to collect your membership payment of [amount] from [date]. Our system has tried again, but it hasn't gone through.

To keep your membership active, please update your card or bank details here: [secure update link]. If we can't collect it by [date], we'll need to pause your access until it's sorted, as set out in your membership terms.

If something has changed and you'd like to freeze or change your membership instead, reply to this email and we'll help.

[your name], [gym name]
```

### When a person should call
Automated messages handle most cases. A person is better in these:
- The member is still checking in but hasn't paid after about 10 days. A quiet word at the desk is kinder than a blocked fob.
- The failure is a cancelled mandate or a card reported lost or stolen. Retries won't work, so ask directly whether they want to continue.
- The member replied to a message and mentioned money worries, illness or moving away. Offer a freeze or a change of plan, never more reminders.

### What an automated follow-up workflow does
1. Picks up each failed payment from Stripe, GoCardless or your gym software as soon as it's reported.
2. Sends the first notice with a secure link to update card or bank details, through the payment tool you already use.
3. Stops every message the moment the payment succeeds, so nobody is chased after they've paid.
4. Puts members who are still unpaid after 10 days, or whose mandate was cancelled, on a call list for the front desk or manager.
5. Gives you a weekly list: failed payments, recovered, still open and paused, so nothing sits in an inbox. Personal trainers billing monthly plans can pair this with [check-ins and package renewals](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/personal-trainer-client-check-ins/).

### If you change the amount or the date
If you collect by UK Direct Debit and you change the amount, the collection date or the frequency, the Direct Debit Guarantee says the member must be told in advance, normally 10 working days before. Collecting two months at once after a missed payment counts as a change of amount. When in doubt, take the missed amount separately with a one-off payment link instead. Your membership terms set out when access can be paused, so make sure the messages match them. Studios that sell intro offers and class packs rather than memberships have a different job: [following up trial clients before the offer runs out](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/fitness-studio-intro-offer-follow-up/).

Within 48 hours you get a [written plan with a fixed price](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/how-it-works/). It's built on the tools you already use (your gym software, Stripe or GoCardless, email and texting, where they allow a connection), so your team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days, for a one-off $2,000. You pay once it's running and you're happy with it. If AI drafts a reply to a member, a person always approves it before it's sent.

### Doesn't our gym software already chase failed payments?
Many systems retry the payment and send one email. The workflow adds the friendly first message, a person following up at the right time and one list of who still owes what.

### Should we block access straight away?
That's your decision, under your membership terms. A short grace period with clear messages usually keeps more goodwill than an instant block.

### Can a Direct Debit be retried if the member cancelled it?
No. GoCardless only retries failures for insufficient funds while the mandate is still active. If the mandate was cancelled, the member needs to set up a new one, so the workflow sends them to a person instead.

### Does it work for fitness studios and class packs?
Yes. Any recurring payment works the same way: a monthly membership, a class subscription or a personal training plan. Charities use the same steps for [failed regular donations](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/charity-gift-aid-declarations/), and [driving instructors](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/driving-instructor-lesson-bookings-and-test-reminders/) for pupils paying for blocks of lessons. For no-shows and late cancellations, see [salon cancellation policies and deposits](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/salon-cancellation-policy-and-deposits/), which works the same way for classes.

## Lawn care seasonal renewals and booking reminders, on autopilot
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/lawn-care-seasonal-renewals/

Lawn care seasonal renewals are the yearly job of asking last season's customers to sign up again for their lawn treatment programme or regular garden visits, before the first round of the new season. An automated workflow sends each customer their renewal, with the price and a link to confirm, in late winter, reminds the ones who haven't answered, books their first visit and puts anyone still undecided on a short call list.

Lawn care seasonal renewals decide how full your spring is. In the US this is usually a lawn care program of treatments through the year. In the UK it's more often called a gardening round or a lawn treatment programme, with regular cuts or feeds. Either way, the work is the same: every winter you go back to last year's customers, confirm who's staying, update prices and fill the calendar before the grass starts growing. Most small firms do it from a spreadsheet and a lot of phone calls, which is exactly the kind of repeat job a simple workflow handles well. [Pest control contracts](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pest-control-contract-visits-and-reports/) renew the same way.

### Where renewals go wrong
- Renewal letters go out late, after customers have already been leafleted by someone else
- One email is sent and nobody follows up the customers who didn't answer
- Price changes are buried in the email, so customers query them at the door on the first visit
- Confirmed customers aren't booked straight away, so the first round is planned by hand from a list

### A renewal timeline for the season
Work back from your first visit of the year. The Royal Horticultural Society's advice for UK lawns (2026) is to apply a spring feed in mid-spring, usually late March to April, so for many UK firms the first round falls then. In the US, the start date depends on your region and grass type, so set the dates from your own first round.
| When | Channel | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 8-10 weeks before the first round | Email | Renewal invitation: last year's service, this year's plan and price, a link to confirm |
| 6 weeks before | Text | Short reminder with the link, only to customers who haven't answered and have agreed to texts |
| 4 weeks before | Email | Last reminder: the date the first round starts and that places on the round are filling |
| 3 weeks before | Office list | Customers still undecided go on a call list for a personal phone call |
| On confirmation | Email or text | Thank you, the first visit date, and what they need to do (gate unlocked, pets in) |
| 2 days before each visit | Text | Visit reminder with the day and a way to tell you if it doesn't suit |
| After the first round | Email | One message to anyone who didn't renew: a link to restart, then no more automatic messages |

### Renewal email you can copy
Renewal invitation, 8-10 weeks before the first round:
```
Subject: Your [season] [lawn care programme / garden visits] with [company]

Hi [first name],

Thanks for having us look after [address] last year. We're planning [season] now and would love to keep you on the round.

This year: [plan name], [number of visits or treatments], starting from [first visit week]. The price is [price] [per visit / for the season]. [If the price has changed: That's up from [old price], because [one plain reason].]

To keep your place, confirm here: [confirm link]. It takes a minute, and you can pay [how you take payment].

Want something different this year, more visits or fewer? Just reply and tell us.

[your name], [company]
```

### Booking reminder and lapsed-customer messages
Visit reminder (text) and one follow-up for customers who didn't renew (email):
```
Visit reminder, 2 days before:
Hi [first name], [company] here. We're due at [address] on [day] for your [treatment / cut]. Please leave the side gate unlocked. If the day doesn't suit, reply and we'll move you.

One follow-up after the first round:
Subject: Still want help with the garden this year?

Hi [first name], our [season] round is now under way and we didn't hear back from you, which is completely fine. If you'd like to join later in the season, or try a lighter plan, reply to this email or book here: [link]. We won't keep emailing about it.

[your name], [company]
```

### What an automated renewal workflow does
1. Builds one customer list from last season: address, plan, number of visits, price paid and how they paid, from your spreadsheet or scheduling software. Carpet cleaners can build the same kind of list from [the date and rooms of each customer's last clean](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/carpet-cleaning-repeat-booking-reminders/).
2. Sends each customer their own renewal email with this year's plan and price, and a link to confirm and pay with the payment tool you already use.
3. Reminds only the customers who haven't answered, and stops the moment someone confirms or says no.
4. Books confirmed customers into the first round by area, so your rounds are planned from the list, not from memory.
5. Sends visit reminders before each round, and gives you a weekly list: renewed, undecided, declined and still to call. If you also service pools on a route, [reports from each pool visit](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pool-service-visit-reports/) work the same way.

### If your programme renews automatically
Some US lawn care companies run continuous service, where the program carries on each year until the customer cancels. Auto-renewal rules differ by state, and some states require an annual reminder (California is one example, covered on our [HVAC maintenance agreement renewals](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/hvac-maintenance-agreement-renewals/) page). Check your own state's rules with your attorney, then set the reminders to match. In the UK, tell customers about price changes clearly and before the season starts, so nobody is surprised by the first invoice. The workflow sends whatever notices you decide on, on time, and keeps a record that they went out.

## CIS monthly return: collecting subcontractor invoices before the 19th
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/cis-monthly-return-subcontractor-invoices/

A CIS monthly return lists every payment a contractor made to subcontractors in the tax month (the 6th of one month to the 5th of the next), and HMRC must receive it by the 19th. To file it on time you need each subcontractor's invoice, split into labour, materials and VAT, and their verification status before you pay. A collection workflow requests invoices before the 5th, checks what's missing, and gives you one list to finish the return.

The CIS monthly return itself takes minutes. Collecting subcontractor invoices for it is what takes the week. One sub sends a photo of a handwritten invoice, another forgets to split out materials, a new starter hasn't given you a UTR, and the 19th arrives before the paperwork does. This guide is for UK contractors, and the bookkeepers who run CIS for them, who want that collection to run on a fixed monthly rhythm instead of a scramble.

### The CIS dates every month
HMRC's guide "What you must do as a CIS contractor" (gov.uk, checked November 2026) sets these dates. A tax month runs from the 6th to the 5th, so the return for 6 November to 5 December must reach HMRC by 19 December. The same dates sit alongside payroll and VAT in our [UK accounting practice deadline calendar](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/uk-accounting-practice-deadline-calendar-2026-27/).
| When | What happens | What you need in hand |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6th | New tax month starts. Payments from today go on next month's return | A list of subs expected to invoice this month |
| Around the 1st | Ask every active sub for this month's invoice | Invoices split into labour, materials and VAT |
| Before any payment | Verify any new sub, or one not on a return in this or the last 2 tax years | UTR, plus NI number, company or partnership details |
| By the 5th | Last day of the tax month for payments | Every payment logged with gross amount and deduction |
| 6th to 12th | Check every payment has an invoice and a deduction rate | A short list of what is still missing |
| By the 19th | Return reaches HMRC, and each sub gets a payment and deduction statement | Monthly return, or a nil return if nobody was paid |
| By the 22nd | CIS deductions paid to HMRC (by the 19th if paying by post) | Total deductions from the return |

### What you need from each subcontractor
Before you can pay a new subcontractor, HMRC says you must verify them. It tells you whether they're registered and which rate to use: 20% for registered subcontractors, 30% for unregistered ones, or 0% if they have gross payment status. The details you give must exactly match what the subcontractor registered with, and you can't verify temporary NI numbers starting with "TN". If you verify more than 50 subcontractors you need commercial CIS software rather than HMRC's free online service.
- Sole traders: name, UTR and National Insurance number
- Limited companies: company name, company UTR and Companies House registration number
- Partnerships: nominated partner details, trading name and partnership UTR
- Every month: an invoice showing the gross amount, VAT, and what they paid for materials, plant hire, fuel (not for travel) and consumables, because the deduction is only taken from what's left
- Receipts for materials if you ask for them. HMRC says that without evidence you estimate the materials cost

### What a late or wrong return costs
HMRC charges £100 for a return 1 day late, £200 more at 2 months, and at 6 and 12 months £300 or 5% of the CIS deductions on the return, whichever is higher. Later than that, the extra penalty can be up to £3,000 or 100% of the deductions. Each month is a separate return, so one missed month can turn into several penalties. HMRC's April 2026 Employer Bulletin says that from April 2026 contractors must file every month again, including nil returns when no sub was paid (or send an inactivity request in advance), and that the full late-filing penalty regime is back. Giving the wrong employment status for a subcontractor can cost up to £3,000, and so can failing to show your CIS records when asked. HMRC says to keep them for at least 3 years after the end of the tax year.

### A request you can send to subcontractors
Monthly invoice request to a subcontractor (send around the 1st):
```
Subject: Your invoice for [month]: needed by [date before the 5th]

Hi [first name],

To pay you for [month] and include you on our CIS return, please send your invoice by [date].

Please show on the invoice:
1. The total for the work
2. VAT, if you're VAT registered
3. What you paid for materials, plant hire and fuel for this job (not travel)

We'll take CIS off the labour part only, at the rate HMRC gives us for you. You'll get your payment and deduction statement by the 19th.

If anything has changed (new company, new UTR, now VAT registered), please tell us before we pay.

You can reply with a photo or PDF, or upload it here: [upload link]

Thanks,
[your name]
[business name]
```

### What an automated collection workflow does
1. Keeps one list of subcontractors with their verification status, deduction rate and the date they were last on a return, so anyone who needs verifying again is flagged before payment.
2. Sends each active sub the invoice request around the 1st, by email or text, with an upload link.
3. Saves each invoice to the right month's folder and records the gross amount, materials and VAT for a person to check.
4. Reminds only the subs who haven't sent anything, and tells you on the 3rd who is still missing.
5. On the 6th, gives you a draft of the month: every payment, its deduction, and any gaps. If nobody was paid, it reminds you to file a nil return.
6. After you file, sends each sub their payment and deduction statement and reminds you to pay HMRC by the 22nd.

### If you're a bookkeeper running CIS for clients
The same rhythm works across a client list. Each contractor client gets the request on the same day, and you get one view on the 6th of which clients have everything and which are still waiting on a sub. It sits well next to your [bookkeeping document collection](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/bookkeeper-document-collection/), and the monthly statements it saves are the ones your subcontractor clients need at year end, as listed in our [Self Assessment records checklist](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/self-assessment-records-checklist-for-clients/).

### How Mike Automations would build this
We start with a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how invoices reach you today and who files the return. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example: every active sub is asked by the 1st, gaps are listed by the 6th, and statements go out after filing. It's built on the tools you already use (your email, a shared drive or spreadsheet, and your CIS or accounting software where it allows a connection). Live in 2-3 days, [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it. If you want to see where CIS fits among your other tasks first, try the [plan builder](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/).

### What stays with you
Verifying subcontractors, deciding employment status, checking the figures and submitting the return. The workflow requests, files and reminds. Nothing is sent to HMRC by the workflow, and anything sent to a subcontractor in your name uses wording you approved.

### When is the CIS monthly return due?
HMRC must receive it by the 19th of the month after the tax month ends. The tax month runs from the 6th to the 5th, so the return for 6 November to 5 December is due by 19 December.

### Do I need to file a CIS return if I paid no subcontractors?
Yes. HMRC's April 2026 Employer Bulletin says contractors must again file every month from April 2026, including a nil return, unless they told HMRC in advance with an inactivity request.

### What details do I need to verify a subcontractor?
Your own UTR, accounts office reference and employer reference, plus the sub's UTR and either their NI number (sole trader), company name, UTR and registration number (limited company), or partnership details. They must exactly match what the sub registered with.

White-label automation lets a marketing or web agency say yes when a client asks, "Can you automate our enquiries?" without hiring a developer. ### Data protection: put it in writing
In UK GDPR terms your client is usually the controller, your agency a processor, and Michael a sub-processor. The ICO's guidance (checked 11 November 2026) says a processor must not engage another processor without the controller's prior specific or general written authorisation, and must put a contract in place with that sub-processor offering the same protection as its own contract. So tell your client a specialist is building the workflow, and get their written OK. Michael works from Haifa, Israel, so include that when you describe where the work is done. US clients may have their own contract or state privacy terms; check those too.

## AI automation services for small business: what's real and who to hire
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/ai-automation-services-small-business/

AI automation services for small business build workflows where an AI model reads, sorts or drafts something (an email, a form, a PDF) inside your existing tools, and ordinary automation moves the result to the right place. What is real today is AI that prepares work for a person to approve: sorted enquiries, draft replies, data pulled from documents, summaries. Be wary of any provider promising an AI that runs your business on its own, replaces staff or guarantees income.

AI automation services for small business are now sold by agencies, freelancers, course sellers and one-person specialists, often with the same words and very different results. If you are searching for an AI automation agency or an AI expert to hire, this page helps you tell the useful work from the hype. It lists the jobs AI genuinely does well in a small service business, what to check before you hire anyone, a side-by-side of agency, freelancer, one-person specialist and DIY, what the AI tools themselves cost according to the vendors' own pricing pages, and the limits worth knowing before anything goes live.

### What AI automation actually means
Most of a good "AI automation" is ordinary automation: a trigger (a new email, a form, a file in a folder), fixed rules and actions in your tools. The AI part is one or two steps where reading or writing language is needed, such as working out what an email is about or drafting a reply. If the job follows the same rules every time, it usually needs no AI at all, and [the difference between AI and automation](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/ai-vs-automation-difference/) is worth knowing before you pay for either. An [AI agent](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/ai-agent-for-small-business/) goes a step further and chooses which tool to use next, which makes a person's approval step even more important.

### 8 jobs small businesses hire AI automation for
- Sorting new enquiries: reads each message or form, tags it (new job, quote request, complaint, spam) and puts urgent ones at the top of a list.
- Drafting replies: prepares a reply to each enquiry from your prices, services and tone, for a person to edit and send. Speed matters here, as [replying to new enquiries fast](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reply-to-new-enquiries-fast/) explains.
- Reading documents: pulls supplier, date, amount and VAT from invoices and receipts into a spreadsheet or accounting tool, flagging anything it is unsure of. More in [automating data entry from emails and PDFs](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/automate-data-entry-from-emails-and-pdfs/).
- Checking what clients sent: compares received files against a checklist and drafts a polite note listing only what is still missing.
- Summarising notes: turns rough job notes or a typed meeting note into a tidy summary on the client's record.
- Drafting quotes and proposals: fills a first draft from an enquiry form and your price list, for you to check and send.
- Answering staff questions: lets your team ask questions of your own documents, such as your policies or price list, with links to the source.
- Weekly summaries: writes a short plain-English summary of what your spreadsheet or job list shows, for the owner on Monday morning.

### What's real and what's hype
The US Federal Trade Commission ran a sweep called Operation AI Comply in September 2024 against deceptive AI claims, including "AI-powered" business-opportunity schemes that promised passive income and a service marketed as a "robot lawyer". The FTC's chair said there is no AI exemption from the laws on the books. Use the same test when you hire:
| Claim you might hear | What is usually true |
| --- | --- |
| "An AI agent will run your admin on its own" | AI can prepare most of the work. A person still checks anything that goes to a customer or moves money. |
| "Replace your receptionist or staff" | AI can take routine sorting and drafting off people. Judgement calls and unhappy customers still need a person. See the [pros and cons of an AI receptionist](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/ai-receptionist-small-business-pros-and-cons/). |
| "Guaranteed results or income" | No honest provider can guarantee results from AI. Ask for a written definition of "working" instead. |
| "Our own AI platform" | Often a monthly subscription to someone else's tool with new branding. Ask whose accounts it runs in and what happens if you stop paying. |
| "Fully accurate" | AI models make mistakes, including confident wrong answers. Good builds show where the AI is unsure and send those cases to a person. |

### Agency, freelancer, one-person specialist or DIY
The [consultant vs freelancer vs DIY comparison](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/automation-consultant-vs-freelancer-vs-diy/) goes deeper. For AI work specifically:
|  | AI automation agency | Freelancer | One-person specialist | Do it yourself |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Who you deal with | A salesperson, then a project team | The person who builds it | The same person maps, builds and supports it | You |
| Usual pricing | Project fee, often plus a monthly retainer | Hourly or per task | Fixed project fee, optional support | Tool subscriptions and your time |
| Strength | Capacity for big or several projects at once | Cheap for a clearly specified job | One person who knows your process end to end | Cheapest, and you learn the tools |
| Watch out for | Long discovery phases, retainers, builds in their own accounts | Nobody to call when it breaks | Holidays and capacity: ask who covers | AI steps that fail quietly with nobody checking |
| Best for | Larger firms with many processes | A one-page spec you already wrote | One process that touches clients or money | Internal tasks where a mistake is cheap |

### Checklist: questions to ask before hiring anyone
Copy these into your first call or email. The [full list of questions to ask an automation expert](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/questions-to-ask-before-hiring-an-automation-expert/) covers the general ones; these are the AI-specific ones.
AI automation hiring questions (copy and paste):
```
1. Which steps use AI, and which are ordinary rules?
2. Which AI model and provider will it use, and in whose account?
3. Is our data used to train the model? Where is it stored and for how long?
4. Where does a person approve the AI's work before it reaches a customer or moves money?
5. What happens when the AI is unsure or wrong? Who sees those cases?
6. Roughly what will the AI usage cost us each month, and who pays the bill?
7. What happens when the model we use is retired or changes?
8. Do we own everything you build, and can we see and change it after you leave?
9. What is the fixed price, and what does "working" mean in writing?
10. Who fixes it when it breaks, how fast, and what does that cost?
```

### What the AI tools themselves cost

- You also pay for the automation tool that runs the workflow, such as Zapier, Make or n8n. The [Zapier vs Make vs n8n comparison](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/zapier-vs-make-vs-n8n/) covers those plans.

Claude Team standard seat $25 per seat a month billed monthly ($20 billed annually) | People using AI by hand: drafting, summarising and [admin tasks in a chat window](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/chatgpt-for-small-business-admin/) |

| Batch API | Anthropic's docs list a 50 percent discount on input and output tokens for batch requests | Jobs that can wait, such as overnight document reading |

### Limits and gotchas from the official docs
- Training on your data: OpenAI's documentation says data sent to its API is not used to train its models unless you opt in, and that abuse-monitoring logs are kept for up to 30 days unless the law requires longer. Consumer chat apps can have different settings, so check the plan you actually use.
- Models are retired: Anthropic's pricing docs list older models as retired. A workflow built on one model needs updating when it goes, so ask who does that.
- Token counts change between models: Anthropic's docs say its newer tokenizer produces roughly 30 percent more tokens for the same text. A lower price per token does not always mean a lower bill.
- Data protection: the ICO's guidance on AI and data protection covers fairness, accuracy and automated decisions about people under UK GDPR. The ICO says the guidance is under review after the Data (Use and Access) Act, so check it again before you rely on it.
- Decisions about people: keep AI away from deciding on its own whether someone gets a job, a tenancy, credit or a service. Let it prepare, and let a person decide.

### What do AI automation services for small business actually do?
They connect an AI model to your existing tools so it can read, sort, summarise or draft things such as emails, forms and documents, with ordinary automation moving the results to the right place. The useful setups have a person approve the AI's work before it reaches customers.

### Should I hire an AI automation agency or a freelancer?
An agency suits a larger business with several processes and budget for a retainer. A freelancer suits a job you can specify on one page. A one-person specialist suits one process that touches clients or money and needs someone who maps, builds and supports it.

### How much does AI automation cost a small business?
Two parts: the build and the running costs. Running costs are the AI provider (a chat subscription per person, or pay-per-use API pricing) plus the automation tool. With Mike Automations, a workflow build is a fixed $2,000 ($1,500 for the first 3 clients), paid once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Is it safe to put client data through AI?
It can be, with the right account and settings. Check whether the provider trains on your data, how long it keeps logs and where it stores them, send only the data the job needs, and follow the ICO's guidance or your own regulator's. Keep a person approving the output.

### Do I need AI at all?
Often not. If a job follows the same rules every time, plain automation is cheaper and more reliable. AI earns its place when a step involves reading or writing language that varies, such as free-text emails or mixed documents.

Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/hubspot-automation-consultant/

A HubSpot automation consultant for a small business sets up the follow-ups, reminders and data syncs that HubSpot doesn't run on its own, either inside HubSpot on the right plan or with an outside tool that reads and updates your HubSpot records. On the free CRM, HubSpot automates one email per form, so most small businesses need either a paid plan or a connected automation. Before hiring anyone, check which of your triggers live inside HubSpot and which live in other tools, because that decides what the build needs.

A HubSpot automation consultant is who people look for when HubSpot holds their contacts and deals but nothing happens unless someone remembers to do it. - Sending reminders before a call or visit booked through HubSpot's meeting page.
- Keeping HubSpot and your invoicing tool in step: a won deal creates the invoice in Xero or QuickBooks, and paid or overdue status comes back to the contact. The [payment reminders guide](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) covers the chasing side.

| Plan | Price shown | Automation it lists |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0, for up to 2 users | One email after each form is submitted (HubSpot Knowledge Base) |

| Sales Hub Professional | $90 to $100 per seat per month, plus a required one-time $1,500 onboarding fee | Up to 300 fully customisable workflows |
| Sales Hub Enterprise | $150 per seat per month, plus a required one-time $3,500 onboarding fee | Up to 1,000 workflows |

### Limits and gotchas from HubSpot's own docs
- The free CRM allows up to two users and 1,000 contacts, with no expiry date, according to HubSpot's free CRM page.
- On the free tools, HubSpot's form automations article says you get one "Send an email after form submission" simple workflow per form, with one action. No second email, no task, no deal update.
- HubSpot's "Create workflows" help article lists the workflows tool for Professional and Enterprise, while the pricing page lists limited workflows on Sales Hub Starter. Check what your own account shows under Automation before you pay for an upgrade or a build.
- Pipeline stage automations (create a task, send an internal email notification or edit the record when a deal enters a stage) are listed for Sales Hub and Service Hub Starter, Professional and Enterprise. Not free.
- An outside tool can work with a free account. HubSpot's developer usage guidelines list 100 requests every 10 seconds per private app and 250,000 a day per account on Free and Starter, which is plenty for a small business.
- A HubSpot workflow only sees what's in HubSpot. If the trigger is an overdue invoice in Xero or a booking in another app, you need a connection either way. Our post on [HubSpot free CRM automation limits](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/hubspot-free-crm-automation-limits/) goes through this in detail.

### Do it yourself or hire help?
| Your situation | Usually best | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |

| Triggers in Xero, QuickBooks, a booking app or WhatsApp | Hire, or learn a tool like Zapier or n8n | It crosses tools, so someone has to connect, test and handle failures |
| You'd upgrade only to get one or two follow-ups | Price both | Per-seat upgrades are paid every month; a connected automation is built once |

## QuickBooks Online automation services for small business: what to hire help for
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/quickbooks-online-automation-services/

QuickBooks Online automation services set up the work around your books so it runs by itself: invoice reminders, bank rules, receipt chasing, approvals and moving data in from forms, email and payment tools. QuickBooks already does some of this on its own, such as up to three automatic reminders per invoice and bank rules with up to 5 conditions each, so good help starts with the built-in features and only builds what is missing. Everything should be set up in your own QuickBooks and email accounts, so you own it.

QuickBooks Online automation services are what small businesses and bookkeepers look for when QuickBooks is set up but the admin around it still eats the week: chasing receipts, typing in invoices, nudging late payers, copying data from one tool to another. If you've searched for a QuickBooks automation consultant or a QuickBooks expert, this page helps you decide what to hire for, what to check before you hire anyone, and what you can do yourself. The product facts come from Intuit's own help pages, checked on 11 November 2026.

### What small businesses usually hire QuickBooks automation help for
- Turning on and wording automatic invoice reminders, then adding the step QuickBooks doesn't take: telling a person when an invoice is badly overdue so someone calls
- Writing bank rules so regular payments (rent, fuel, software) are categorised the same way every month
- Chasing missing receipts: one email per client or per month listing the transactions still without one, instead of chasing each one by hand
- Creating invoices in QuickBooks from a booking, a signed quote, a job marked done or an online form, so nobody retypes them
- Getting supplier bills from an email inbox into QuickBooks for approval before they're paid
- Matching card or online payments from a payment tool to the right invoice
- A weekly email to the owner: what's overdue, what's due this week and what's still uncategorised
- Adding new customers to QuickBooks from a CRM or sign-up form with the right details and terms
- For bookkeepers and accountants: chasing documents that QuickBooks doesn't ask for, such as year-end records, payroll changes or W-9s

### What QuickBooks Online already does on its own
Before paying anyone, check whether the feature is built in. These come from Intuit's help articles (US versions, checked 11 November 2026):
- Invoice reminders: Intuit says you can send up to three automatic reminders per invoice, scheduled up to 90 days before or after the due date, and only for invoices you've already emailed. Our post on [QuickBooks Online client reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/quickbooks-client-reminders/) covers the settings.
- Bank rules: each rule can have up to 5 conditions, and Intuit says QuickBooks can only apply one rule per transaction, in priority order. Rules can auto-post without review, which Intuit says to use with caution.
- Workflows: Intuit says these are in QuickBooks Online Advanced and Intuit Enterprise Suite only. They can send reminders and approval requests to your team or customers when conditions you set are met.
- Requests: you can ask a client for details or a file about a specific transaction, and they get a weekly reminder. Intuit says Requests are on all QuickBooks Online plans except Solopreneur.

### What QuickBooks Online costs
Intuit's US pricing page, checked on 11 November 2026, lists these monthly prices before any introductory discount (it was offering 50% off for 3 months to new customers). Prices differ by country and change, so check the page for your country before you decide.

| --- | --- | --- |
| Simple Start | $38 | 1 |
| Essentials | $85 | 3 |
| Plus | $140 | 5 |
| Advanced | $340 | 25 |

A rough guide. For a broader view, [automation consultant vs freelancer vs DIY](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/automation-consultant-vs-freelancer-vs-diy/) sets out the trade-offs, and connector tools such as Zapier, Make and n8n are compared in [Zapier vs Make vs n8n](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/zapier-vs-make-vs-n8n/).


### Gotchas from Intuit's own documentation
- Only one bank rule applies to a transaction. Two overlapping rules don't combine: the higher one in the list wins.
- Auto-posted rules skip your review. Keep them for simple, regular costs.
- Automatic reminders only go for invoices emailed from QuickBooks. Invoices printed or sent another way are not chased.
- Workflows need Advanced. On other plans, approvals and escalations need another tool or a manual step.
- Users count towards your plan's limit, though Intuit says some roles, such as reports only, don't. Deleting a user is permanent, but their history stays in the audit log.

## Xero automation services for small business: what to hire help for, and what to check first
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/xero-automation-services/

Xero automation services are paid help to connect Xero to the rest of a business, so invoices, bills, client questions and reminders move without someone copying them by hand. Xero already automates bank feeds, bank rules, repeating invoices and invoice reminders, so good help starts by switching those on and only builds what Xero can't do, such as chasing clients for missing information or getting bills approved before they're entered. The work should be built in the business's own accounts, so the owner keeps it if the helper leaves.

Xero automation services are what people look for when they know Xero could do more but don't have the time to work out how. Maybe invoices are still typed in from a spreadsheet, bills arrive in five inboxes, or the month end depends on one person remembering to chase. Looking for a Xero automation consultant? This page covers the jobs small businesses and practices usually hire help for, what Xero does on its own, what it costs according to Xero's own pricing pages, the limits worth knowing, and the questions to ask anyone before you let them into your books.

### What small businesses hire Xero automation help for
These are the jobs that come up most. Each one sits between Xero and something else: your inbox, a form, a job system or your clients.
- Creating invoices in Xero from a finished job, a signed quote or a row in a spreadsheet, instead of retyping them
- Getting supplier bills from email into Xero with a person approving them first, covered in [supplier invoice approval](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/supplier-invoice-approval-workflow/)
- Chasing overdue invoices beyond Xero's own reminders: a call list for the ones still unpaid, or a text as well as an email, as in [invoice payment reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/)
- Sending clients one list of bank lines to explain each month and collecting the answers in one place
- Chasing missing receipts and statements before month end or a VAT or sales tax return, the core of [bookkeeper document collection](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/bookkeeper-document-collection/)
- Setting up a new client or customer: the contact in Xero, a folder, a welcome email and the first requests
- Keeping a simple status sheet of who is ready for month end, built from Xero and your own notes
- Sending the owner a weekly email of overdue invoices, so nobody has to log in to check

### What Xero already does on its own
Before paying anyone, make sure these are switched on. Xero's UK invoicing page says Xero can send automatic reminders before or after the due date, and that it checks the bank feed so it only chases invoices that are still unpaid. It can also create and send repeating invoices, and add a pay now button through Stripe or GoCardless (fees apply). Bank rules and auto-reconcile handle bank lines that repeat. Hubdoc, which captures bills and receipts, is included in Xero's current UK plans when it's connected to Xero. Anyone who builds an automation for one of these jobs without checking first is selling you something you already pay for. A longer list of ideas for practices is in [Xero automation ideas for small accounting practices](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/xero-practice-automation-ideas/).

### What Xero costs, from Xero's pricing pages
Checked on 11 November 2026. Xero often runs introductory discounts for new customers, and prices change, so check the page for your country before you decide. These are the regular monthly prices.
| Plan (country) | Regular monthly price | Limits that matter for automation |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ignite (UK) | £18 excl. VAT | Quotes and 20 invoices, 10 bills, no automated bill entry, auto-reconcile is a £3.50 add-on |
| Grow (UK) | £39 excl. VAT | Invoices and bills included, automated bill entry, auto-reconcile included |
| Comprehensive (UK) | £55 excl. VAT | As Grow, plus multi-currency and expenses for 5 users |
| Ultimate (UK) | £70 excl. VAT | As Comprehensive, plus projects for 10 users |
| Early (US) | $27 | 20 invoices, 5 bills, no automated bill entry, auto-reconcile is a $5 add-on |
| Growing (US) | $59 | Invoices and bills included, automated bill entry |
| Established (US) | $97 | As Growing, plus multi-currency and projects |

### Limits and gotchas worth knowing
- Plan caps: on Ignite (UK) or Early (US), an automation that creates invoices or bills will fail once the plan's limit is reached. Check the plan before building anything that writes to Xero.
- API limits: Xero's developer FAQ says each connected organisation allows 60 API calls a minute, 5,000 a day and 5 at the same time, and that the limits are the same for every app. A small business rarely gets near them, but a badly built sync that checks every few seconds can.
- Who connects it: connect apps from an admin login the business controls, not a helper's personal one, so access never depends on someone who might leave. Keep a list of which apps are connected to Xero.
- Posting without review: nothing should post to the ledger, approve a bill or send a payment without a person checking it first.
- Country differences: plan names, limits and features differ between the UK, the US, Australia and other regions, so something that works for one business may not work for another.

### Do it yourself or hire help?
| Situation | Do it yourself | Hire help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A feature Xero already has (reminders, repeating invoices, bank rules) | Yes, follow Xero's own help pages | Not needed |
| One simple link, such as a form that creates a contact | Yes, with Zapier or Make and an afternoon | Only if you don't have the afternoon |
| Several steps with approvals, reminders and exceptions | Possible, but it tends to break quietly | Usually worth it |
| Client data, chasing and a deadline that matters | Risky without testing | Yes, with a written definition of "working" |
| Nobody in the business wants to own it | No | Yes, with optional support |

## Airtable consultant for small business: what to hire for and what to check
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/airtable-consultant-small-business/

An Airtable consultant for a small business designs the base (the tables, linked records, views and forms), moves data in from spreadsheets, and sets up the automations and connections that keep it up to date, inside the business's own Airtable account. Hire one when your data is several linked things, such as customers, jobs and invoices, and the build needs more than an afternoon; stay DIY for one simple list. Airtable itself costs $20 per editing seat per month on the Team plan billed annually, and its Free plan stops at 1,000 records per base (Airtable, November 2026).

An Airtable consultant for small business is usually who you look for when a base you started yourself has grown messy, or when you know your spreadsheet should be a proper database but don't want to spend weeks learning how. Looking for an Airtable expert? This page sets out the jobs small businesses typically hire help for, a checklist of questions to ask anyone before you hire, when to do it yourself, what Airtable costs and where its limits catch people out, all checked against Airtable's own pages in November 2026. To be clear from the start: Mike Automations isn't an Airtable partner and doesn't resell licences. The advice is about your work, not a product.

### What small businesses hire Airtable help for
- Turning a spreadsheet into a base: customers, jobs, quotes and invoices as separate tables that link to each other, so a phone number changes in one place. If you're not sure you need this, read [Airtable vs Google Sheets](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/airtable-vs-google-sheets-small-business/) first.
- Cleaning and importing old data: one customer per row, consistent dates, duplicates merged, before anything is linked.
- Forms that feed the right table: enquiries, job requests or onboarding details landing as proper records, with attachments.
- Interfaces and views per person: the office sees every open job, a field worker sees only today's list on their phone.
- Built-in automations: an email when a record reaches a stage, a reminder when a quote has had no reply, a task when a form arrives.
- Connecting Airtable to other tools: Gmail or Outlook, your accounting software, a booking app or e-signatures, through Zapier, Make, n8n or Airtable's API. Our comparison of [Zapier, Make and n8n](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/zapier-vs-make-vs-n8n/) explains the options.
- Fixing a base that has outgrown itself: too many fields, broken lookups, automations nobody understands or that use up the monthly allowance.
- Adding AI with a person in charge: drafting replies or summarising notes for someone to approve before anything is sent. See [AI agents for small business](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/ai-agent-for-small-business/).
- Handover: written notes on how the base works, so you aren't tied to whoever built it.

### DIY or hire: a decision table
| Your situation | Do it yourself | Hire help |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One list (leads, stock, a price list) | Yes, Airtable's templates are enough | Rarely worth it |
| Customers, jobs and invoices that link to each other | Possible if you have time to learn linked records | Yes, the table design is the hard part |
| Data in several messy spreadsheets | Slow and easy to get wrong | Yes, cleaning first saves rebuilding later |
| Simple status emails inside Airtable | Yes, built-in automations handle this | Not needed |
| Airtable must talk to email, accounts or bookings | Possible with Zapier or Make | Yes, if it must be reliable and watched |
| Field staff or clients need their own view | Possible with interfaces | Yes, if permissions matter |
| You aren't sure Airtable is the right tool | Try the Free plan on a copy of your data | A short call is cheaper than a wrong build |

### What Airtable costs in November 2026
Airtable charges per seat. Its pricing page says that on Team and Business plans you pay for everyone with edit permissions on at least one base, while read-only collaborators, form submissions and share links are free. Airtable's plans help article also lists commenters as billable on the Team plan, so check who counts before you invite your whole team. Figures from airtable.com/pricing and Airtable's plans overview, checked 11 November 2026:
| Plan | Price per seat | Records per base | Automation runs per workspace per month | API calls per month |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Free | $0 (up to 5 editors) | 1,000 | 100 | 1,000 |
| Team | $20 a month billed annually, $24 billed monthly | 50,000 | 25,000 | 100,000 |
| Business | $45 a month billed annually, $54 billed monthly | 125,000 | 100,000 | No monthly cap |
| Enterprise Scale | Custom, through Airtable's sales team | Ask Airtable | 500,000 | No monthly cap |

### Limits and gotchas from Airtable's own docs
- Record limits are per base and add up across tables. Airtable's plans article says a base with two tables of 25,000 records is at the Team plan's limit. When you hit it, you keep your data but can't add records until you upgrade.
- Every automation trigger counts as a run, including failed and cancelled runs. Run limits reset on the first day of each month, not on your billing date, and unused runs don't carry over.
- On the Free plan the "Run a script" action isn't available, and "Send email" can only email people who are collaborators on the base. Team can email 100 unique non-collaborator addresses a day; Business 1,000.
- An automation can't trigger in one base and act in another, so the base design decides what can be automated.
- Turning on a new automation doesn't run it for existing records, only for new or updated ones.
- Triggers on formula fields check about every 5 minutes while someone has the base open, and once an hour otherwise, so they aren't instant.
- The API allows 5 requests per second per base. On Team, going over 100,000 calls in a month slows calls to 2 per second until the month resets.
- Business and Enterprise Scale plans need a private email domain, so a Gmail or Yahoo address can't upgrade to them.
- Exports are CSV, one table at a time. You can't export a whole base as one file, so keep that in mind for backups.

### Questions to ask any Airtable consultant before you hire
Copy this list into an email or keep it next to you on the call. More on this in [questions to ask before hiring an automation expert](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/questions-to-ask-before-hiring-an-automation-expert/), and if you're still weighing up who to hire, [consultant vs freelancer vs DIY](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/automation-consultant-vs-freelancer-vs-diy/).
Airtable consultant checklist (copy and paste):
```
[ ] Will the base be built in our own Airtable account and workspace, so we own it?
[ ] Which Airtable plan will we need, and how many paid seats? Who only needs read-only access?
[ ] How many records and automation runs a month do you expect, and how close is that to the plan limit?
[ ] What other tools (Zapier, Make, n8n, scripts) will it depend on, and who pays for them?
[ ] Will you clean our data before importing it?
[ ] Is the price fixed, and what exactly counts as "working" before we pay?
[ ] What happens when an automation fails? Who gets told?
[ ] Does anything send messages to customers without a person approving it?
[ ] What written handover do we get, and can someone else take over the base later?
[ ] What does support cost after it goes live, and can we stop it?
```

## Google Workspace automation services for small business: what to hire for, what it costs, what to check
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/google-workspace-automation-services/

Google Workspace automation services for small business means someone builds workflows inside the Gmail, Google Sheets, Forms, Drive, Calendar and Apps Script your business already pays for, so enquiries, reminders, documents and reports run on their own. Most small jobs need no extra software: Apps Script is included with a Google account, though Google sets daily limits such as 1,500 script email recipients a day on a Workspace account. A good provider builds everything in your own account, so you own it and it keeps working if they disappear.

Google Workspace automation services are what you look for when your business runs on Gmail and Google Sheets and the copying, chasing and filing has started to eat your week. Maybe you're searching for a Google Apps Script developer, a Google Sheets automation expert or someone to connect your Google Forms to everything else. This page covers the jobs small businesses usually hire help for, what Google charges and the limits it publishes, what to check before you hire anyone, and when doing it yourself is the better choice.

### What small businesses usually hire help for
These are the Google Workspace jobs that come up again and again in small service businesses. Each one stays inside tools you already have:
- A Google Form (enquiry, intake, booking request) that adds a row to a tracker sheet, creates a client folder in Drive and emails you a summary.
- Overdue invoice reminders drafted in Gmail from a sheet of unpaid invoices, for a person to check and send. The full workflow is on the [invoice payment reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) page.
- Document chasing: each client gets a list of what's still missing and polite reminders until it arrives, with uploads filed in the right Drive folder.
- Quotes, welcome letters or job sheets made from a Google Docs template, filled from a row in a sheet and saved as PDF.
- Calendar events created from a list of booked jobs, with a reminder email to the customer the day before.
- A Monday morning summary email: open jobs, overdue items, who hasn't replied, built from your tracker sheet.
- Gmail labels and drafts for repeat enquiries, so a person approves a reply instead of writing it from scratch. Our post on [Gmail automation](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gmail-automation-for-accountants/) covers what Gmail does on its own.
- Connecting Google to the rest of your tools (Xero, QuickBooks, Stripe, a booking app) through their APIs or a connector such as Zapier or Make.
- Fixing a script someone else wrote that stopped working when they left the business.

### What Google Workspace itself costs
Google's help page on Business edition pricing (last updated 26 October 2026) lists these US prices per user per month. Google's pricing page shows different prices in different countries, and promotional discounts come and go, so check workspace.google.com/pricing for yours. Google says the Business plans can be bought for up to 300 users. Apps Script has no separate charge.
| Plan | Flexible plan (monthly) | Annual plan |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Business Starter | $8.40 | $7.00 |
| Business Standard | $16.80 | $14.00 |
| Business Plus | $26.40 | $22.00 |

### Google's limits that shape what gets built
A good provider designs around these before writing a line of code. All from Google's own documentation, checked 11 November 2026. Google says Apps Script quotas can change at any time without notice.
- Apps Script can email 1,500 recipients a day from a Workspace account and 100 from a free gmail.com account.
- One script run stops after 6 minutes. Triggered scripts get 6 hours of total runtime a day on Workspace and 90 minutes on gmail.com.
- Installable triggers always run under the account of the person who created them. If an employee sets one up and later leaves, the automation stops when their account is removed. Set triggers up from an account the business owns.
- A daily trigger set for 9 AM runs at a time Google picks between 9 and 10 AM, then keeps that time. Fine for reminders, not for anything that must happen to the minute.
- Gmail itself allows a paid Workspace user 2,000 messages a day (1,500 for mail merge). Free trial accounts have lower limits: 500 messages a day.

### Do it yourself or hire help?
| Situation | Usually better | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| One sheet, one simple reminder, you're comfortable editing a script | Do it yourself | Our [Google Apps Script guide](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/google-apps-script-for-small-business/) has a script to copy |
| Gmail filters, templates and scheduled send | Do it yourself | Built into Gmail, no code |
| Form to sheet to folder to email, with several people involved | Hire help | Permissions, triggers and errors need care |
| Anything that emails clients automatically | Hire help, or test hard | A mistake reaches every client at once |
| Google plus Xero, QuickBooks or Stripe | Hire help | APIs, logins and error handling |
| A script nobody understands has stopped | Hire help | Finding the cause takes longer than writing it |
