To see the steps for your clinic first, [build your plan here](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=med-spa-consent-forms-and-aftercare). A physio clinic runs the same pattern: see [physio patient intake forms](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/physio-clinic-patient-intake-forms/).

### Can a consent form sent by email replace the consultation?
No. The form collects history and records that the client has read the information. Your practitioner still goes through the treatment, risks and consent with the client before treating, as their professional body and insurer require.

### Can the booking flow stop under-18s from booking Botox or filler?
It can ask for date of birth and stop the booking if the client is under 18. In England the Botulinum Toxin and Cosmetic Fillers (Children) Act 2021 makes giving these to under-18s an offence unless a doctor, or a regulated health professional on a doctor's directions, gives it. Check ID on the day if age is in doubt.

### Can aftercare messages answer client questions with AI?
We don't build that. Aftercare messages send the sheet your practitioner wrote. Any reply goes to a person, because a question after a treatment can be a clinical concern.

### Where are the forms stored?
In your clinic or booking software where it allows a connection, otherwise in a restricted folder you control. Health data is special category data under UK GDPR, so access is limited to the people who need it.

## Rental application document collection for property managers, without the inbox chase
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/rental-application-document-collection/

Rental application document collection is the step where a property manager gathers each applicant's photo ID, proof of income such as pay stubs, and landlord or employer references before deciding on the application. A simple workflow sends every applicant the same checklist, files each upload against the application, reminds them about anything missing and tells you when the file is complete. A person always makes the decision, and the same written criteria apply to every applicant.

Rental application document collection is where good applicants get lost. The listing gets ten inquiries, six people apply, and then the paperwork arrives in pieces: an ID photo by text, two pay stubs by email, a reference contact on a sticky note. By the time one file is complete, a faster manager has signed the lease. This page gives you a checklist, a request message and a reminder schedule you can copy, plus the FTC and HUD points to keep in mind.

### The documents to ask for, and why it should be one list
Decide what you need once, write it down and send the same list to every applicant for the same unit. A consistent list is faster, and it's also fairer: HUD says the Fair Housing Act prohibits discrimination in housing because of race, color, national origin, religion, sex, familial status and disability, and asking different applicants for different things is how unequal treatment creeps in. State and local rules can add more, so check yours. A typical list, for illustration:
| Document | What it shows | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Completed application form | Who will live there, contact details, rental history | One form per adult, online if possible |
| Government photo ID | The applicant is who they say they are | Ask only for what you need, and say how you store it |
| Proof of income | Ability to pay rent | For example, recent pay stubs, an offer letter or benefit letters, as your written criteria allow |
| Landlord reference contact | Past rent and tenancy record | Name, phone and email of the current or last landlord |
| Employer reference contact | Current employment | Only if your criteria use it |
| Signed permission for screening | Your right to run a credit or background check | The FTC says written permission helps show you have a permissible purpose |

### A document request message you can copy
Sent the moment an application comes in (edit the words in brackets):
```
Hi [first name], thanks for applying for [address, unit]. To review your application we need the items below from each adult who will live there:

1. Photo ID
2. Proof of income: [your accepted documents]
3. Current or last landlord: name, phone and email
4. The signed screening permission form: [link]

Upload everything here: [secure link]. Please don't send ID by text or email. We review complete applications in the order they're finished, using the same criteria for everyone: [link to criteria]. Questions? Reply to this message. [company name], [phone]
```

### How the workflow runs, step by step
1. An application arrives from your listing site, website form or property management software. The applicant gets the request above within minutes, with a secure upload link for their application.
2. Each upload is saved in the applicant's folder and ticked off the checklist. Nothing sits loose in someone's inbox.
3. Anything still missing after 24 hours gets a short reminder naming exactly what's missing. A second reminder goes after 48 hours, then the application is marked incomplete and you're told.
4. Reference requests go to the landlord and employer contacts with a short form to fill in, and one reminder if they don't reply.
5. When the checklist is complete, you get one message: application ready to review, with links to every document. If several people applied, you see them in the order their files were completed.
6. You review and decide. The workflow sends the approval with lease next steps, or the decline message you've approved, and logs the date and reason.
7. After the period you choose, documents from applicants who didn't rent are deleted, following your retention policy.

### If you use a screening report: the adverse action notice
The FTC says tenant background check reports, such as credit reports, eviction or rental history reports and screening scores, are consumer reports under the Fair Credit Reporting Act. If you deny an application, ask for a co-signer, or charge a bigger deposit or higher rent based even partly on one of those reports, you must give the applicant an adverse action notice. The FTC lists what it must include: the name, address and phone number of the screening company, a statement that the company didn't make the decision and can't give the reasons for it, and the applicant's right to dispute the report and to get a free copy if they ask within 60 days. If a credit score was used, the notice must also give the score and the key factors that hurt it. The FTC calls written notices best practice and says you must securely dispose of reports once you're done with them. A workflow can send your approved notice wording whenever a decision is logged with "screening report" as a reason. This isn't legal advice: check the wording with your attorney.

### Managing rentals in Canada
In Canada, landlords' handling of personal information falls under federal or provincial privacy law depending on the province, so check which applies to you. The Office of the Privacy Commissioner of Canada's tips for the rental housing sector say to explain why you collect each item, ask only for what's necessary, mark the Social Insurance Number as optional if you ask for it at all, get consent before reference or background checks, avoid using social media for background checks, and plan how you'll dispose of information from the start.

### Where application paperwork usually breaks
- ID and pay stubs arrive by text and email, and some never get saved to the file
- Nobody notices a missing document until the applicant calls to ask what's happening
- References are chased by phone between showings, and the notes live in one person's head
- Different staff ask for different documents, so there's no record that every applicant was treated the same
- Inquiries wait hours for a first reply. A fast [auto-reply to new inquiries](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reply-to-new-enquiries-fast/) fixes the step before this one

### What stays with you
Your screening criteria, the decision on every application, the wording of approval, decline and adverse action notices, and any call with an applicant. The workflow asks, files, reminds and logs. It doesn't score applicants or decide anything. If AI drafts a message, a person approves it before it's sent. More on this in [document requests without a client portal](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/document-requests-without-a-portal/). Once a tenant moves in, the same tools can book [move-in and routine inspections](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/property-inspection-scheduling/).

It's built on the tools you already use (your listing inbox, a form, Google Drive or OneDrive, email and texts, and your property management software where it allows a connection), so your team doesn't learn a new system. To see the steps for your rentals first, [build your plan here](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=rental-application-document-collection), or [try the demo](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/try/).

### What documents should a rental application include?
Usually a completed application for each adult, photo ID, proof of income such as recent pay stubs, landlord and employer reference contacts, and signed permission for any credit or background check. Ask every applicant for the same list, written down in advance.

### Is it safe to collect ID and pay stubs by email?
A secure upload link that saves each file to the applicant's folder is better, and you can ask applicants not to send ID by text or email. Limit who can open the folder, and delete files you no longer need.

### Do I have to send an adverse action notice?
The FTC says yes if you deny an application, ask for a co-signer, or charge more based even partly on a consumer report such as a credit or tenant screening report. The notice must name the screening company and explain the applicant's right to a free copy and to dispute it.

No. It collects documents, chases what's missing and tells you when a file is complete. You decide, using your own written criteria.

## Nursery waiting list and enrolment, from first enquiry to the first settling-in session
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/nursery-enrolment-and-waiting-list/

A nursery waiting list workflow keeps every family's enquiry, wanted start date and funding in one list, tells parents where they stand, and sends the enrolment pack the moment a place is accepted. In England, gov.uk says parents of children aged 9 months to 4 years can apply for 30 hours of free childcare a week, and must give the nursery an 11-digit code that they reconfirm every 3 months, so the workflow also asks for that code before the start date and reminds parents when it is due. The nursery manager still decides who is offered a place.

A nursery waiting list is often a spreadsheet, a notebook and a memory. A parent rings when they're pregnant, another emails about a September start, and by spring nobody is sure who was promised what. Then a place comes up and the enrolment paperwork starts: registration form, contract, allergies, emergency contacts, funding code, settling-in sessions. It is the same for every family, so it can run as one workflow while your staff look after the children. This page is for nurseries and pre-schools in England; Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland have their own funded childcare schemes.

### Where waiting lists and enrolment go wrong
- The list has no wanted start date, days or funding type, so you can't match a family to a place when one comes up
- A place is offered by phone, the parent says "probably", and nobody follows up for a week
- The funding code arrives on the first morning, or not at all, and the funded hours can't be claimed
- Parents forget to reconfirm their code every 3 months and nobody notices until it has lapsed

### The funded childcare dates your list needs to know (England)
These come from gov.uk, checked in November 2026. Gov.uk says parents of children aged 9 months to 4 years can get 30 hours of free childcare a week for 38 weeks of the year through Free Childcare for Working Parents. They can apply from when the child is 23 weeks old, and the hours start in the term after the child turns 9 months:
| Child turns 9 months between | Funded hours can start from | Parent's deadline to apply |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 September and 31 December | 1 January | 31 December |
| 1 January and 31 March | 1 April | 31 March |
| 1 April and 31 August | 1 September | 31 August |

### Other funding facts that shape your paperwork
- If a parent is approved, HMRC gives them an 11-digit code. Gov.uk tells parents to give it to their provider with their National Insurance number and the child's date of birth.
- Parents must sign in to their childcare account every 3 months to confirm their details are up to date. Your workflow can remind them a couple of weeks before their date.
- Every 3 and 4 year old in England can get 570 free hours a year, usually 15 hours a week for 38 weeks, from the term after their third birthday (1 January, 1 April or 1 September). It stops when the child starts in reception class.
- Gov.uk says you may charge for extras such as meals, nappies and trips, but parents can still get the free hours if they don't pay, and you should agree an alternative. Say so plainly in your enrolment pack.

### The waiting list and enrolment workflow
1. A parent enquires by your website form, email or a phone message. Within minutes they get a reply with your sessions, fees and a short form: child's name and date of birth, wanted start date, days, and whether they expect funded hours. Why speed matters: [replying to new enquiries fast](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reply-to-new-enquiries-fast/).
2. The answers go into one waiting list sheet, sorted by start date and days, with the funding term worked out from the child's date of birth using the gov.uk table.
3. Each term, waiting families get a short update asking if their dates have changed. Anyone who doesn't reply is marked for a call, not removed. Swim schools keep [a waiting list sorted by age and stage](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/swim-school-term-bookings-and-waiting-list/) on the same principle.
4. When a place comes up, the list shows the families whose days and start date fit. You choose who to offer it to.
5. The offer goes out with the start date, days, fees and a date to accept by, plus one reminder. If they decline or don't answer, you're told, and you pick the next family.
6. Once the place is accepted, the enrolment pack goes out: registration form, contract, extras and how to opt out of them, and your policies.
7. The returned form is checked against the EYFS list below, and only missing items are chased. If funded hours are expected, the parent is asked for the code, their National Insurance number and the child's date of birth well before the first session.
8. Settling-in sessions are booked, the parent gets the key person's name, and a member of staff checks the allergy and dietary details and shares them with the staff who need them.

### A place offer email you can copy
Place offer (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: A place for [child's first name] at [nursery name]

Hi [parent's first name],

Good news: we can offer [child's first name] a place starting on [start date], on [days and session times].

The fee is [fee] per [month or session], before any funded hours. If you're expecting funded hours, please have your 11-digit childcare code ready.

Please reply by [accept-by date] to let us know if you'd like the place. Once you accept, we'll send the registration form and contract and book settling-in sessions.

If the timing doesn't work, tell us and we'll keep you on the list.

[Your name]
[Nursery name], [phone]
```

### The enrolment checklist: what the EYFS says you must record
The EYFS statutory framework for group and school-based providers (in force from 1 September 2026) says you must record, for each child: their full name and date of birth; the name and address of every parent or carer known to you; anyone else with parental responsibility; which parent or carer the child normally lives with; and emergency contact details, ideally more than two numbers. It also says you must get details of special dietary requirements, food allergies and intolerances and any special health requirements before the child is admitted, and written permission from a parent before giving any medicine. Mark these fields as required on your registration form and the workflow knows what to chase. [Physio clinics run the same check on intake forms](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/physio-clinic-patient-intake-forms/).

### What stays with you
Who is offered a place, in what order and on what terms. Fees, funded hours claims and anything about a child's care, health or safeguarding. The workflow keeps the list, sends messages on time and tells you what is missing. It never decides on admissions or reads anything into a child's health information. Children's details are sensitive, so keep them in tools you control, limit who can see them and work through the [GDPR checklist for automating client data](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gdpr-checklist-automating-client-data/). If AI drafts a message, a person approves it before it's sent.

Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your nursery software's exports, a spreadsheet, email, online forms, texts), so your staff don't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. To see the steps for your nursery first, [build your plan here](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=nursery-enrolment-and-waiting-list). If you also bill termly, see how [tutoring centres send termly invoices](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/tutoring-centre-enrolment-and-termly-invoices/) and how to [chase unpaid invoices](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/).

### Can a waiting list workflow decide who gets a place?
No. It sorts the list by start date, days and funding and shows you who fits. You decide who is offered the place and in what order.

### When should we ask parents for their funding code?
As soon as the place is accepted, and well before the first session. Gov.uk tells parents to give the 11-digit code to their provider with their National Insurance number and the child's date of birth.

### Do parents have to reconfirm their code?
Yes. Gov.uk says parents must sign in to their childcare account every 3 months to confirm their details are up to date. A reminder before that date helps them keep the funded hours.

## Venue hire enquiry follow-up, from first reply to final payment
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/event-venue-enquiry-follow-up/

Venue hire enquiry follow-up is everything a venue sends between a new enquiry and a signed, paid booking: the first reply with availability and prices, a viewing invitation, the proposal, a provisional hold with an end date, the contract and the payment schedule. A workflow can send each step on time from one list of enquiries and dates, remind people before a hold lapses and chase each payment on its due date. The venue team still sets prices, runs viewings and decides which dates to hold or release.

Venue hire enquiry follow-up is where most venues lose bookings without noticing. An enquiry for a Saturday in June arrives at 10 PM through the website form. Someone replies two days later, the couple or the office manager has already booked a viewing elsewhere, and the date stays pencilled in your diary for a month because nobody released it. The steps after an enquiry are the same for every wedding, party or company event, so they can run on their own while your team focuses on viewings and the day itself. This page is for event venues, function rooms, hotels with event spaces and private hire rooms in the UK and the US (in the US you'll call it an inquiry; the steps are the same).

### Where venue enquiries go cold
- The first reply takes a day or more, because the person who knows the prices and availability is running an event
- Availability is checked in one diary and prices in another document, so every reply is written from scratch
- Provisional holds have no end date, so a date is blocked for weeks by someone who has gone quiet
- A second enquiry for a held date gets a flat no, instead of a note asking the first client to decide
- The contract goes out, and nobody notices it hasn't come back signed
- Balance payments and final numbers are chased from memory in the last few weeks

### The follow-up sequence, step by step
A starting point. The timings and the length of a hold are yours to set; what matters is that every step has a date and the next one starts on its own.
1. New enquiry: the form, email or phone note is logged with the date, event type, guest numbers and budget. Within minutes the enquirer gets a reply saying whether the date looks free, the room or package prices that fit, and a link to book a viewing. Speed matters most here: see [how to reply to new enquiries fast](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reply-to-new-enquiries-fast/).
2. Viewing booked: a confirmation with the address, parking and who they'll meet, then a reminder the day before.
3. After the viewing: a thank-you the same day with the proposal or quote attached, and the offer of a provisional hold.
4. Provisional hold: the date is marked as held in your diary with an end date. The client gets that date in writing and a reminder a few days before it ends. If they don't confirm, you're asked to approve releasing it.
5. Second enquiry for a held date: the second enquirer is told the date is provisionally held and offered a waiting list, and the first client gets a message asking them to confirm or release by a set date.
6. Booking confirmed: the contract goes out for e-signature with the deposit payment link. If it isn't signed within a week, a reminder follows, then a task for someone to call.
7. Payment schedule: each instalment and the balance is reminded before its due date, with the same terms every time. Late payers are handled like any [overdue invoice](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/).
8. Final details: a form for final numbers, dietary needs, timings and suppliers goes out on the date in your contract, with reminders until it's complete. The florist dressing the room needs the same answers by a similar date, as set out in [final details for wedding and event flower orders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/florist-wedding-and-event-orders/).

### A hold and payment timeline you can copy
For illustration. Change the timings and amounts to match your own contract.
| When | What the client gets | What your team checks |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Within minutes of the enquiry | Availability, prices that fit, viewing link | The date and room are right |
| Day of the viewing | Thank-you, proposal, offer of a hold | The proposal matches what was discussed |
| Hold placed | Hold confirmed in writing with its end date | Date marked as held in the diary |
| 3 days before the hold ends | Reminder: confirm or release | Any second enquiries for the date |
| Hold ends, no reply | Note that the date is released | You approve the release first |
| On confirmation | Contract for e-signature and deposit link | Contract signed and deposit received |
| Each instalment date | Reminder 7 days before and on the day | Payment received |
| Final details date | Form for numbers, dietary needs, timings | Form complete, kitchen and staff told |

### A hold reminder email you can copy
Sent 3 days before a provisional hold ends (edit the words in brackets):
```
Hi [first name],

Thank you again for coming to see [venue name]. We're holding [date] for your [event type] until [hold end date].

If you'd like to go ahead, just reply to this email or sign the booking form here: [link]. The [deposit amount] deposit secures the date, and the rest of the payment schedule is set out in the form.

If you've decided not to go ahead, or would like a different date, let us know and we'll release this one. If we don't hear from you by [hold end date], we'll release the date so others can book it.

Any questions, call me on [phone].

[your name]
[venue name]
```

### Deposits, cancellations and contracts: what to check
In the UK, regulation 28(1)(h) of the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 takes accommodation, catering and services related to leisure activities with a specific date out of the usual 14-day right to cancel a distance contract. Whether your bookings fall inside that exclusion depends on what you sell, so take advice. The CMA's unfair contract terms guidance (CMA37, updated 22 July 2026) says a deposit can be kept in full if it works as a binding reservation with clear, narrow conditions, but "will not normally be more than a small percentage of the price". More in our [salon cancellation policy guide](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/salon-cancellation-policy-and-deposits/) and [how to ask for a deposit](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/how-to-ask-for-a-deposit-on-a-quote/). Signing online is fine for most contracts: in the UK, section 7 of the Electronic Communications Act 2000 makes electronic signatures admissible in evidence, and in the US the federal ESIGN Act (15 U.S.C. 7001) says a contract can't be denied legal effect just because it's electronic. US state rules on deposits vary, so check with your attorney. The workflow sends your terms; the wording comes from you and your adviser.

### What stays with you
Your prices, packages and contract terms. Every viewing, every conversation about the day, and every decision to hold, release or move a date. The workflow keeps the enquiry list, sends each message on its date and records replies, signatures and payments. It never releases a held date or offers it to someone else without your approval, and it never quotes a price you haven't set. If AI drafts a reply to an unusual enquiry, a person approves it before it's sent. If you also plan events for clients, the [wedding planner payment schedule](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/wedding-planner-supplier-and-payment-schedules/) covers the supplier side, and [photographers](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/photographer-booking-contracts-and-deposits/) use a similar contract and deposit routine.

It's built on the tools you already use: your website form, email, diary or booking system, a spreadsheet, your e-signature tool and your payment links, so your team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it. To see the steps for your venue first, [build your plan here](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=event-venue-enquiry-follow-up), or [try the demo](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/try/).

### How fast should a venue reply to an enquiry?
As fast as you can. The workflow can send the first reply within minutes, at any hour, with availability and prices, and a person picks up from there.

### Can it check whether the date is free?
Yes, if your availability lives in a calendar, a spreadsheet or a booking system it can read. The first reply says the date looks free, and a person confirms it before any hold.

## Body shop repair updates that go out on their own, plus insurer paperwork chasing
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/body-shop-repair-updates/

Body shop repair updates are short messages that tell the vehicle owner which stage their collision repair has reached (estimate, insurer approval, parts, repair, paint, ready) and when to expect the car back. An automated workflow sends each update when the job's stage changes in your shop system or job board, asks the customer to approve any extra work in writing, and chases the insurer for authorisations and supplements on a fixed schedule. A person in the shop still sets every date, price and repair decision.

Body shop repair updates are the messages your customers want most and your front desk has the least time to send. A collision repair can sit for days waiting for an insurer's approval, a parts delivery or a supplement after teardown, and the customer has no idea why. So they ring, the estimator stops to look up the job, and someone still has to chase the insurer. Below: the stages worth messaging, texts you can copy, an insurer chasing schedule and the approval rules in California and the UK.

### Where repair updates break down
- Updates depend on whoever answers the phone, so customers hear nothing until they call
- The job board shows the stage, but nobody turns that into a message
- Hidden damage found at teardown is approved over the phone and never written down; bike shops avoid this by [texting the mechanic's quote for approval](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/bike-shop-service-bookings-and-repair-updates/) before any chargeable work
- Insurer authorisations and supplements wait in an inbox with no follow-up date
- Calls come in while the estimator is with a customer, and missed callers try another shop: a [missed-call text-back](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/missed-call-text-back-contractors/) helps there

### The stages worth a message
Use the stages your shop already tracks. Each change of stage sends one message. Nothing is sent for steps the customer doesn't care about. Phone repair shops use the same idea, with one message per stage [from check-in to collection](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/phone-repair-shop-job-updates/).
| Stage | Who gets a message | What it says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Vehicle dropped off or towed in | Customer | We have your car, your job number, who to contact and what happens next |
| Estimate sent to insurer | Customer, and the insurer or adjuster | Estimate sent on [date], we'll update you when it's approved |
| Waiting on insurer approval | Insurer (chaser), customer (status) | Polite chase to the insurer; the customer is told the job is waiting on approval, not on the shop |
| Supplement or extra work found | Customer and insurer | What was found, photos, the price and a link to approve in writing |
| Parts ordered or delayed | Customer | Parts ordered, expected on [date]; a new message only if that date moves |
| In repair, then paint | Customer | One short update per stage, no promises beyond your current target date |
| Ready for collection | Customer | Ready, opening hours, what to bring, any balance or excess to pay |
| A few days after collection | Customer | One check-in and a review link, sent once |

### Status texts you can copy
Four updates (edit the words in brackets):
```
Drop-off: Hi [first name], we have your [make model, reg/plate] in. Your job number is [job no]. [Estimator name] is looking after it. Next step: we send the estimate to [insurer] and let you know when they approve it. Questions: reply here or call [phone].

Waiting on insurer: Hi [first name], quick update on job [job no]. The estimate went to [insurer] on [date] and we're waiting for their approval. We chased them today and will update you as soon as we hear.

Date change: Hi [first name], the target date for your car has moved from [old date] to [new date] because [reason, e.g. a part is delayed]. Sorry about that. We'll text you again when it's ready.

Ready: Hi [first name], your [make model] is ready to collect. We're open [hours]. Please bring [ID / keys / excess payment]. [Shop name], [phone]
```

### Why extra work needs a written yes first
Rules differ by state and country, so take advice for your own shop. In California, the Bureau of Automotive Repair (BAR) says a shop must give the customer a paper or electronic estimate and get the customer's authorisation before work starts. If more work is needed than the original estimate, BAR says the shop must prepare a revised work order and get and record the customer's authorisation first. BAR's spring 2022 newsletter lists what a recorded oral or electronic authorisation includes: the date, the time and the name of the person who authorised it, plus the phone number or email address used. In the UK, the Consumer Rights Act 2015 says a service must be carried out with reasonable care and skill (section 49), and that what you say or write to the customer about the service can become part of the contract if they rely on it (section 50). So send dates as targets, with the reason when one moves, not as promises. With a workflow, the approval is a reply or a tap on a link, and the date, time, name and number are saved on the job.

### Chasing insurer paperwork on a schedule
1. When the estimate or supplement goes to the insurer, the job gets a chase date (for example two working days later, or whatever suits your insurers). Brokers chase insurers on a similar schedule when they [keep clients updated on a claim](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/insurance-broker-claims-updates/).
2. On the chase date, if nothing has come back, a polite email goes to the adjuster or claims handler with the claim number, the job number and what you are waiting for.
3. If there is still no reply, a second chase goes out and the job lands on the estimator's call list for that day.
4. When the authorisation arrives, the job moves to the next stage, the customer gets their update and the chasing stops.
5. Each morning the office gets one list: jobs waiting on insurers, how long each has waited and the next chase date.

### What stays with you
The estimate, the repair method, every price and every decision about the car stay with your estimator and technicians. The workflow doesn't write estimates or discuss the claim with insurers. It sends the messages you have approved, records replies and keeps the chase dates. If AI drafts an update or a reply, a person always approves it before it's sent. If your messages go beyond the repair (offers, servicing, marketing), check the marketing consent rules where you are first. When the car is paid for, the [payment reminder workflow](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) can cover any balance left unpaid.

### How Mike Automations would build this
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how jobs move through your shop today and where customers and insurers get stuck. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your shop management system or job board, a spreadsheet, email, texts or WhatsApp), so your team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it, under a [pay-when-happy agreement](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agreement/). To see the steps for your shop first, [build your plan here](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=body-shop-repair-updates), or [try the demo](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/try/).

### Does this replace our shop management system?
No. It reads the job stage from your system, a job board or a spreadsheet and sends the right message when the stage changes. Your system stays the record of the job.

### Can customers approve extra work by text?
Yes. They get what was found, a photo and the price, and approve or decline with a reply or a link. The date, time, name and number are saved on the job, and the technician waits for a yes.

### Will it message the insurer for us?
It sends the chase emails you have written, on the dates you set, with the claim and job numbers. Anything about the claim itself stays with your estimator.

### How much does it cost?

## Interior design client approvals, purchase orders and delivery tracking
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/interior-designer-client-approvals-and-orders/

Interior design client approvals are the client's written yes to each item before you order it: the fabric, the finish, the sofa, the price and the lead time. A workflow can send each selection with its sample photo and cost, record the client's approval, raise the purchase order to the supplier only once the approval and deposit are in, and keep one tracker of what's ordered, confirmed, delayed and delivered. The designer still makes every design choice and decides what gets ordered.

Interior design client approvals tend to live in a mix of WhatsApp messages, email threads and "yes, love it" on a site visit. That works until a custom sofa arrives in the wrong velvet, or nobody can say which of forty items has actually been ordered. This page is for small interior design studios in the UK and the US that buy furniture and finishes on the client's behalf. Architects have a similar stage sign-off routine: see [fee proposals and stage approvals for architects](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/architect-fee-proposals-and-approvals/).

### Why every item needs a written approval
Made-to-order upholstery, cut fabric, custom joinery and special-order lighting are usually non-returnable once the supplier starts work, so the moment to be sure is before the purchase order goes out. A written approval per item, with the exact finish, quantity, price and lead time, gives you and the client the same record. The same idea runs through a [change order approval workflow](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/change-order-approval-workflow/) for builders.

### The rules to check before you order
Checked on the official sources in November 2026. They decide when an order is safe to place. Ask your adviser how they apply to your contracts.
- UK: under the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 (legislation.gov.uk), a consumer who signs a distance or off-premises contract, such as one agreed by email or at their home, has a 14-day cancellation period. For a service it ends 14 days after the contract is made. For goods it ends 14 days after the goods arrive.
- UK: regulation 28 of the same regulations says the right to cancel does not apply to goods made to the consumer's specifications or clearly personalised. Made-to-measure curtains or a sofa in the client's chosen fabric may fall here; a stock lamp does not.
- US: the FTC's Cooling-Off Rule (16 CFR Part 429) covers sales of $25 or more made at the buyer's home and $130 or more at other temporary locations. The buyer can cancel within three business days, and the seller must give a written cancellation notice. It doesn't cover deals negotiated at your studio or showroom. Some states add their own rules.
- If a cancellation period applies, the safe default is to place non-refundable orders only after it ends, or after the client has asked in writing for work to start sooner.

### From selection to delivery, step by step
1. You finish a selection (one room or one batch of items) in your usual spec sheet. If a decorator is painting the rooms, the paint colours can go through [a written colour and finish sign-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/painters-decorators-quotes-and-colour-sign-off/) in the same way.
2. The workflow sends the client a selection sheet: photo or sample image, supplier, finish, quantity, price, lead time and whether the item can be returned. Each line has approve, change or remove.
3. If no reply comes in 3 working days, one reminder goes out. After 7, the item goes on your call list.
4. Approved items wait until the deposit or full payment for them is received. The client gets an invoice or payment link for exactly the approved lines, and the [payment reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) cover anyone who forgets.
5. Once approval and payment are both in, the workflow drafts the purchase order to the supplier. You check it and release it. Nothing is ordered without your click.
6. Supplier order confirmations are matched to the purchase order. If the finish, price or lead time differs from what the client approved, it is flagged to you before anything else happens.
7. Delivery dates feed the tracker. The client gets a short weekly update and a message the day before any home delivery.

### A selection approval message you can copy
Selection sent for approval (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: [Room] selections ready for your approval

Hi [client name],

The selections for the [room] are ready. For each item you'll see the photo, finish, price and lead time, and whether it can be returned once ordered.

[link to selection sheet]

Please mark each item approve, change or remove. I'll order approved items once the deposit of [amount] for them is received, and not before. Made-to-order pieces can't usually be returned, so please check the fabric and finish codes carefully.

If it's easier to talk it through, book a short call here: [booking link].

Thanks,
[designer name]
[studio name]
```

### The order and delivery tracker
One row per item. The client sees a simple version, you see all of it:
| Item | Supplier | Client approved | Paid | PO sent | Supplier confirmed | Due | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [Sofa, fabric code] | [supplier] | [date] | Deposit [date] | [PO number, date] | [date, lead time] | [week] | In production |
| [Pendant light x2] | [supplier] | [date] | [date] | [PO number, date] | [date] | [date] | Delivered, checked |
| [Curtains, made to measure] | [workroom] | Waiting, reminder sent [date] |  |  |  |  | Waiting for client |
| [Rug] | [supplier] | [date] | [date] | [PO number, date] | Price changed |  | Flagged to designer |

### What stays with you
Every design choice, every supplier, your trade prices and your mark-up, and the decision to order. You decide what goes on a selection sheet and when it's ready to send. The workflow sends, reminds, records, drafts purchase orders and keeps the tracker. It never orders anything on its own or tells a client an item is approved on your behalf. If AI drafts an update or a reply, a person approves it before it's sent. The same approach works for [client approvals at an agency](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/agency-client-approvals/).

## Construction daily site reports, from the phone to the office and client automatically
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/construction-daily-site-reports/

A construction daily site report (or site diary) is a short daily record of who was on site, what work was done, deliveries, weather, delays, instructions and any incidents, with photos. Automating it means the site lead fills in one phone form before leaving, and the report is saved to the job folder, sent to the office and turned into a weekly client update without anyone retyping it. Incidents go straight to a named person, because reporting rules such as RIDDOR in Great Britain and OSHA's in the US run on short deadlines.

Construction daily site reports are the record you reach for when something goes wrong: a dispute over a delay, a missing delivery, a variation nobody wrote down or an accident. Yet on most small and mid-sized jobs the site diary is a paper book in the van, a WhatsApp thread, or a form someone fills in on Friday from memory. The office only finds out what happened when the client rings to ask. This page gives you a daily report form you can copy, the steps to get it from the phone to the office and the client automatically, and the incident rules that mean some entries can't wait until the end of the day.

### What a daily site report should record
Keep it short enough to fill in on a phone in a couple of minutes, or it won't get done. These are the fields that answer most questions later:
| Field | What to write | Why it matters later |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Job, date and who filled it in | Site address or job number, today's date, the site lead's name | Ties every entry to one job and one person |
| Labour on site | Your crew and each subcontractor, with headcount and hours | Backs up labour costs, subcontractor invoices and day-work sheets |
| Work done today | Plain words per area or stage, with 3 to 6 photos | Shows progress against the programme |
| Deliveries and plant | What arrived, what was short or damaged, plant on and off hire | Settles supplier and hire disputes |
| Weather | Conditions and any hours lost | Supports a claim for weather delays |
| Delays and problems | What stopped work, how long, who caused it | The evidence for an extension of time |
| Instructions and changes | Who asked for what, on site or by phone | Starts a change order before the work is done |
| Visitors and inspections | Client, architect, building control, inspectors | Records who saw what and when |
| Health and safety | Near misses, injuries, toolbox talks, anything reportable | Triggers an immediate alert, not a daily one |

### A daily site report form you can copy
Daily site report (paste into Google Forms, Microsoft Forms or your job app; edit the words in brackets):
```
DAILY SITE REPORT
Job: [job number / site address]
Date: [date]   Filled in by: [name]

1. Labour on site: [own crew, number and hours] / [subcontractor, trade, number and hours]
2. Work done today: [area or stage: what was done]
3. Photos: [3 to 6 photos of today's work]
4. Deliveries: [supplier, what arrived, anything short or damaged]
5. Plant on or off hire: [item, on or off]
6. Weather: [conditions] Hours lost: [0 / number]
7. Delays or problems: [what, how long, cause] or NONE
8. Instructions or changes requested: [who asked, what, how] or NONE
9. Visitors and inspections: [name, company, purpose] or NONE
10. Accident, injury or near miss: YES / NO (if YES, call [name] now as well)
11. Plan for tomorrow: [what's next, anything needed from the office]
```

### How the automated version works
1. The site lead opens the form on their phone before leaving site. The job list is filled in for them, so they pick the job rather than type it.
2. On submit, the report is saved as a PDF with its photos in the job's folder (Google Drive, OneDrive or SharePoint), named by job and date, and added as a row in a job log spreadsheet.
3. The office gets one email or chat message per site with the day's reports, and anything flagged (delays, shortages, changes) at the top.
4. If question 8 has an instruction or change, the office gets a task to raise a [change order](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/change-order-approval-workflow/) before the work goes ahead. A question for the architect or engineer goes into the [RFI log](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/construction-rfi-and-submittal-tracking/) instead.
5. If question 10 is YES, a named person gets a text and an email at once with the details, so the incident is handled and, if it's reportable, reported in time.
6. If no report has arrived for a live job by a set time, the site lead gets one reminder, then the office is told.
7. Once a week, the reports for each job are turned into a short client update: progress, photos, anything the client needs to decide. A person reads and approves it before it's sent.

### Incidents can't wait for the end of the day
In Great Britain, HSE's RIDDOR guidance (checked November 2026) says deaths, specified injuries to workers and dangerous occurrences must be reported to the enforcing authority without delay, and a report must be received within 10 days of the incident. Injuries that keep a worker off their normal duties for more than seven days must be reported within 15 days. In the US, OSHA says an employer must report a work-related fatality within 8 hours, and an in-patient hospitalization, amputation or loss of an eye within 24 hours (29 CFR 1904.39). That's why the incident question sends an alert at once rather than waiting for the evening summary. The workflow doesn't decide whether something is reportable or file the report: a competent person on your side does that.

### Where site diaries usually break
- The form is too long, so it gets skipped on busy days and filled in from memory on Friday
- Photos sit on the site lead's phone and never reach the job folder
- Reports arrive, but nobody in the office reads them until there's a dispute
- Instructions given on site never become a written change order, so the extra work is hard to invoice
- Subcontractor headcounts aren't recorded, so day-work sheets and invoices can't be checked
- Clients ring for updates because the only record is internal

### What stays with you
The site lead writes what happened, in their own words. You decide what goes to the client, whether a delay is worth a claim, and what to do about an incident. The workflow collects, files, sends and reminds. If AI is used to draft the weekly client summary from the reports, a person always reads and approves it before it goes out. The same job folder can feed your [job sign-off and completion photos](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/job-sign-off-and-completion-photos/), and your subcontractor records can sit alongside [insurance certificate tracking](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/subcontractor-coi-tracking/) on US jobs or [CIS invoice chasing](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/cis-monthly-return-subcontractor-invoices/) on UK jobs.

A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how your site reports work today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (a phone form, Google Drive or OneDrive, a spreadsheet, email, WhatsApp or your job software), so your crews don't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it, as set out in the [pay-when-happy agreement](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agreement/). To see the steps for your jobs first, [build your plan here](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=construction-daily-site-reports). More ideas for building firms are on the [contractors page](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/contractors/).

### Is a daily site report the same as a site diary?
Mostly, yes. Both are a daily record of labour, work done, deliveries, weather, delays, instructions and incidents. Some firms keep a site diary for internal use and send a shorter report to the client: the same form can feed both.

### Do we need special construction software?
No. A phone form, a shared drive and a spreadsheet are enough to start. If you already use job management software with a form, the workflow can start from that instead.

### What if there's no signal on site?
Some phone form and job apps can save a form offline and send it when the phone is back in signal. Check this in the app you choose before rolling it out.

### Can the client see the reports?
Only what you choose to send. The full reports stay in your job folder; the client gets a weekly summary that a person approves first.

## Immigration document checklist automation for law firms
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/immigration-law-firm-document-checklists/

Immigration document checklist automation sends each client the list of documents their case type needs, records what has arrived, reminds them about what is still missing and warns the fee earner before a deadline gets close. It doesn't judge whether evidence is good enough: a solicitor, attorney or registered adviser checks every document and decides when the case is ready to file.

An immigration document checklist is the first thing every case needs and the thing that holds most cases up. A spouse visa, a Skilled Worker application, a family petition or a response to a request for evidence all start with the same job: tell the client exactly what to send, then keep asking until it's all in. This page is for small immigration practices in the UK and the US. It sets out the deadlines your reminders should work back from, a checklist you can adapt, a chasing message you can copy, and what should never be automated.

### Where immigration cases get stuck
- The client gets a long list in one email, sends half of it and thinks they're done
- Documents arrive by email, WhatsApp and post, and nobody has one view of what's missing
- Foreign-language documents come in without a translation, or with one that isn't certified
- A dependant's passport, a payslip or a bank statement is out of date by the time the bundle is ready
- A deadline sits in one fee earner's diary and nobody else sees it coming

### The deadlines your reminders should work back from
These come from gov.uk and USCIS, checked in November 2026. They are the dates a checklist workflow can count down to. Your own case deadlines, set by the fee earner, sit on top of them.
| Country | Rule | Source |
| --- | --- | --- |
| UK | A Skilled Worker must apply within 3 months of getting their certificate of sponsorship, and can apply up to 3 months before their job start date | gov.uk, Skilled Worker visa |
| UK | After submitting an application, the applicant must book and attend a visa application centre appointment within 240 days, or start a new application | gov.uk, Apply to come to the UK |
| UK | Documents not in English or Welsh need a certified translation | gov.uk, Apply to come to the UK |
| UK | Most partner or spouse applicants need a combined income of at least £29,000 a year (different rules apply to some extensions and benefit cases) | gov.uk, Family visas |
| US | The maximum response time for a Request for Evidence is 12 weeks (84 days), and 3 days are added when USCIS serves it by mail | USCIS Policy Manual, Vol. 1, Part E, Ch. 6 |
| US | The maximum response time for a Notice of Intent to Deny is 30 days, plus 3 days if served by mail | USCIS Policy Manual, Vol. 1, Part E, Ch. 6 |
| US | Foreign-language documents need a full English translation with the translator's certification that it is complete and accurate and that they are competent to translate | USCIS, Form I-130 page, and 8 CFR 103.2(b)(3) |
| US | A noncitizen in the US must report a change of address to USCIS within 10 days of moving (A and G visa holders and visa waiver visitors are exempt) | USCIS, Form AR-11 page |

### A document checklist you can adapt
Every case type gets its own list, written by your fee earners. The workflow only sends it and tracks it. As an example, a UK Skilled Worker list, based on what gov.uk asks for, might start like this:
- Valid passport or other document showing identity and nationality
- Certificate of sponsorship reference number, from the employer
- Job title, occupation code and annual salary, as shown on the certificate
- Evidence of English language ability, if needed
- Bank statements showing personal savings, unless the certificate says the employer will support the applicant
- Tuberculosis test result, if the applicant is from a listed country
- Certified translation of anything not in English or Welsh
- For each dependant: passport, and evidence of the relationship such as a marriage or birth certificate

### How the checklist workflow runs
1. The fee earner opens the case and picks the case type. The workflow creates the matching checklist for that client, with any deadline the fee earner sets.
2. The client gets one message with their list, a secure upload link (your case software's portal, or a shared folder) and a plain-English note on translations and copies.
3. Each file that arrives is saved to the case folder and ticked off. A person confirms each tick, because only a person can tell a clear bank statement from a cropped one.
4. The client gets a short reminder listing only what's still missing, on the schedule you set, for example every 4 days, then every 2 days in the last fortnight.
5. The fee earner gets an alert when a deadline is close and items are still outstanding, and another when everything is in and ready for review.
6. When a Request for Evidence or a Home Office request for more information arrives, the fee earner writes the new list and the same reminders run against the response date.
7. Passports, visas and other documents that expire go onto one list, so clients are told in good time.

### A chasing message you can copy
Reminder listing only the missing documents (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: [Case reference]: [number] documents still needed

Dear [first name],

Thank you for the documents you've sent so far. We have received: [list received].

We still need:
- [missing item 1]
- [missing item 2]

Please upload them here: [secure link]. If any document is not in English, please also send a certified translation.

We need everything by [internal date] so we have time to check it before [deadline]. If something is hard to get, reply to this email and tell us, and we'll talk it through.

Kind regards,
[name]
[firm name]
```

### What stays with your lawyers
Everything that is advice. In the UK, gov.uk says immigration advisers must be registered with the Immigration Advice Authority (IAA) or be members of an approved professional body, so the advice itself stays with your solicitors and registered advisers. In the US, an attorney or accredited representative files Form G-28 to represent a client before USCIS. The workflow never decides which route fits, whether evidence meets the rules or when to file. Immigration files are also full of sensitive data: the ICO lists health data and data revealing racial or ethnic origin as special category data under UK GDPR, so documents should go to your case system or a secure folder, never sit in a group chat. Our [GDPR checklist for automating client data](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gdpr-checklist-automating-client-data/) covers the questions to ask. If AI drafts a message to a client, a person always approves it before it's sent.

### The same approach elsewhere in a law firm
Document checklists start once a client has signed up, so the step before is [client intake for law firms](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/law-firm-client-intake/). Conveyancing teams run the same pattern for [source of funds documents](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/conveyancing-source-of-funds-document-chasing/). For reminder wording that gets replies, see our [document chasing email templates](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/document-chasing-email-templates/), and for clients who send part of a list and go quiet, read [what to do when clients send some documents but not all](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/clients-who-send-some-documents-but-not-all/).

### How Mike Automations would build this
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how documents reach your firm today and where cases wait. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your email, case management software where it allows a connection, a shared drive and a spreadsheet), so nobody learns a new system. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it, under our [pay-when-happy agreement](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agreement/). To see the steps for your firm first, [build your plan here](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=immigration-law-firm-document-checklists).

### Can the workflow check whether a document is good enough?
No. It records that a file arrived and who confirmed it. Whether it meets the rules is a judgement for your solicitor, attorney or registered adviser.

### How long do we have to answer a USCIS Request for Evidence?
The USCIS Policy Manual says the maximum response time for an RFE is 12 weeks (84 days), with 3 days added if it was served by mail. The notice itself gives the actual due date, and that is the date the reminders count down to.

### Do documents need translating for a UK visa?
Gov.uk says applicants need certified translations of any documents that are not in English or Welsh. The checklist can show translation as its own item so it isn't forgotten.

## Probate document collection: get papers and answers from executors without the chasing
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/probate-document-collection/

Probate document collection is the work a solicitor or probate firm does to gather the original will, the asset and debt details and the executors' decisions needed to value the estate and apply for the grant. Gov.uk says the estate must be valued for Inheritance Tax before anyone applies for probate in England and Wales, so one missing bank letter can hold up the whole file. An automated workflow sends executors one clear checklist, records what has arrived and gently chases what is still missing, while the fee earner keeps every legal decision.

Probate document collection often takes longer than the legal work. Executors are grieving, may live far apart, and are handed a list of papers they have never seen before. Someone in the firm has to remember which bank has replied and which executor still hasn't signed. This page is for solicitors and probate practitioners in England and Wales (Scotland and Northern Ireland have different rules): what gov.uk says you need, a checklist and email to send executors, and the chasing that can run on its own.

### What gov.uk says has to be in place before you apply
These points come from gov.uk's probate and estate valuation guides, checked in November 2026. They decide what you need to collect and when.
- The estate must be valued for Inheritance Tax before applying, even when there's no tax to pay. The application needs the estate values.
- The original will goes with the application: gov.uk says a photocopy can't be used. If the original is lost, form PA13 may apply.
- If full details of the estate are needed, form IHT400 must go to HMRC within 12 months of the death and before applying. HMRC then sends a unique code, usually within 20 working days of receiving the IHT400 or the payment, whichever is later.
- Inheritance Tax must be paid by the end of the sixth month after the death to avoid interest, according to gov.uk.
- Up to 4 executors can be named on the application. An executor who steps aside can hold power reserved (in writing), renounce with form PA15 or appoint someone with form PA11.
- Gov.uk's practitioner guidance (updated July 2026) says practitioners must apply through MyHMCTS, apart from a listed set of cases that need the paper form.
- Gov.uk says the fee is £526 if the estate is worth over £5,000, and grants usually arrive within 12 weeks.

### Probate documents checklist for executors
A starting point to adapt to your firm's own file opening. Send it as a short online form or a tracked list rather than a long letter, and let executors mark an item "don't know" so they don't stop at the first gap.
| Item | Who usually has it | Why you need it |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Original will and any codicils | Executor, the firm that stored it, or the probate registry | Sent with the application; no photocopies |
| Death certificate (or interim certificate from the coroner) | Executor | Needed for letters to banks and other holders; also for the application if the death was outside England and Wales or the certificate is interim |
| Bank, building society, ISA and Premium Bond details | Executor, from statements and post | Each holder is asked for the balance at the date of death |
| Pensions, employer and life insurance details | Executor or family | Lump sums and wages owed can count towards the estate |
| Property address, mortgage lender and how it was owned | Executor or HM Land Registry | Property owned as joint tenants passes to the surviving owner; a valuation is needed |
| Shares, investments and share certificates | Executor or the person's papers | Number held and company details for valuation |
| Debts: credit cards, loans, utility bills, funeral invoice | Executor | Deducted to reach the net estate |
| Gifts made in the 7 years before death | Family, bank statements | Included in the Inheritance Tax estimate |
| Each executor's contact details and decision to act, hold power reserved or renounce | Each executor | Up to 4 can apply; the others need a written note or form |
| ID for each executor | Each executor | Your firm's own identity and AML checks |

### A request email to executors you can copy
First request, sent once you are instructed (edit the words in brackets):
```
Dear [executor name],

Thank you for asking us to help with [deceased's name]'s estate. We're sorry for your loss.

To value the estate and apply for probate, we need some papers and information from you. There's no need to send everything at once. Please use this link to see the list, upload what you have and tick anything you don't know: [secure link].

The most useful things to start with are:
1. The original will, if you have it (please post it to us by recorded delivery rather than scanning it)
2. A copy of the death certificate
3. Any recent bank, pension or insurance letters addressed to [deceased's name]

We'll write to the banks and other organisations ourselves once we have their details. If anything on the list is hard to find, reply to this email or call [name] on [phone] and we'll help.

Kind regards,
[name], [firm]
```

### How the collection workflow runs
1. When the matter is opened, the executors get the checklist and the request email, with a secure upload link.
2. Each upload or reply is filed to the matter and ticked off the list, so the whole team can see what's missing. Family teams use the same pattern for [Form E financial disclosure papers](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/form-e-financial-disclosure-document-collection/).
3. Reminders go only for items still outstanding, kind in tone: for example after 10 days, then 3 weeks, then a note to the fee earner to ring. Executors marked "call only" get no automated messages.
4. When an executor sends a bank's name, the workflow drafts the valuation letter for a person to check and send, and tracks the reply.
5. Each Friday the fee earner gets one list: matters waiting on executors, letters waiting on banks and when each was last chased.
6. Key dates sit on the matter: 6 months from the death for Inheritance Tax payment, 12 months for an IHT400, and the 2-month creditor period after a notice in The Gazette, which gov.uk says must pass before assets are distributed.

### Where probate files usually stall
- One executor answers quickly and the other never does, so the file waits on a signature or a renunciation form
- Executors send scans of the will and keep the original in a drawer
- Banks reply to the executor, not the firm, and the letter sits unopened
- Several people in the firm chase the same executor, or nobody does
- Executors send some documents but not all, and nobody spots the gap until the figures are drafted: our post on [clients who send some documents but not all](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/clients-who-send-some-documents-but-not-all/) covers that pattern, and the [document chasing email templates](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/document-chasing-email-templates/) help with wording

### What stays with you
Every legal judgement: who can apply, whether the estate is excepted, the Inheritance Tax figures and anything said to a family in dispute. The workflow keeps the list, sends reminders and files what comes back. It never gives advice and never sends anything to HMRC or the probate registry. The papers hold sensitive personal and financial data, so read our [GDPR checklist for automating client data](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gdpr-checklist-automating-client-data/) and keep files in the systems you already control. Identity checks follow your own [AML process](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/aml-client-id-checks-workflow/). If AI drafts a reminder or a letter, a person always approves it before it's sent.

### What documents do executors need to provide for probate?
Gov.uk says the application needs the original will (no photocopies) and the estate values, plus a copy of the death certificate if the death was outside England and Wales or there's an interim certificate from the coroner. To reach those values you also need details of bank accounts, property, pensions, shares, debts and gifts made in the 7 years before death.

### How long do we have to report the estate to HMRC?
If full details are needed, gov.uk says form IHT400 must be sent within 12 months of the death and before applying for probate. Inheritance Tax must be paid by the end of the sixth month after the death to avoid interest.

### Will automated reminders upset grieving executors?
Not if they are few, kind and only about what's missing. You set the wording and the gaps between messages, and any executor can be marked as call-only so they never get an automated message.

## Tax return approval chasing: get clients to approve and sign before the deadline
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/tax-return-approval-chasing/

Tax return approval chasing is the follow-up an accountant or tax preparer sends after a return is prepared, until the client has checked it and given written approval to file. In the UK, gov.uk says that if an agent submits your tax return, you must check the information and tell them it's correct before they submit it. In the US, the IRS Form 8879 instructions say the preparer must receive the completed and signed Form 8879 before the e-filed return is transmitted.

Tax return approval chasing is the most frustrating stage of the season. The return is done, and it sits in a queue because the client hasn't opened the email, can't find the e-signature link or has a question they never asked. You can't file without their sign-off, so the deadline risk moves back to you. This page covers what the UK and US rules say, a reminder schedule and an approval email to copy, and how the chasing can run on its own.

### What the rules say about client approval
Checked on gov.uk and irs.gov in November 2026.
- UK: gov.uk's guidance on authorising an agent says the client is still legally responsible for their own tax, and must check the return and tell the agent it's correct before it's submitted.
- UK: for the 2025 to 2026 tax year, gov.uk says online Self Assessment returns are due by 11:59pm on 31 January 2027, and the tax owed must be paid by the same time.
- UK: gov.uk says a late return gets a £100 penalty, then £10 a day (up to £900) after 3 months, with more at 6 and 12 months.
- US: the IRS Form 8879 (Rev. January 2021) instructions say the ERO must receive the signed form before the return is transmitted. Clients may sign by hand, or electronically if the software supports it.
- US: the same instructions say the ERO keeps Form 8879 for 3 years from the return due date or the IRS received date, whichever is later, and doesn't send it to the IRS unless asked.
- US: the IRS says Form 4868 gives individuals until October 15 to file, not more time to pay. The failure-to-file penalty is 5% of the unpaid tax for each month or part of a month late, up to 25%.

### Why approvals stall
- The return goes out as a long PDF with no summary, so the client puts it aside to read later
- On a US joint return both spouses need to sign, and one of them doesn't
- The client has a question about a figure and doesn't want to look silly asking it
- The tax due comes as a shock, so the client avoids the email

### An approval reminder schedule you can copy
Day 0 is the day the return is ready for the client. Shorten the gaps as the deadline gets closer:
| When | Channel | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Day 0 | Email | Return summary (tax due or refund, payment date), the full return attached or in the portal, and the approval or e-signature link |
| Day 3, not opened | Text or WhatsApp | Short nudge: your return is ready to approve, with the link |
| Day 7, not approved | Email | Reminder with the summary again and a "reply with any question" line |
| Day 10, not approved | Office task | A named person calls the client. The workflow stops chasing until they update the status |
| Approved | Automatic | Approval saved to the client file, return marked ready to file |

### An approval request email you can copy
Return ready to approve (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: Your [tax year] tax return is ready to approve

Hi [first name],

Your tax return is ready. In short:
- [Tax to pay: amount, by date] or [Refund due: amount]
- [One line on anything that changed from last year]

Please check the full return here: [link]. If everything is correct, approve it here: [approval or e-signature link]. We can't file until you do.

If anything looks wrong or you have a question, reply to this email and we'll go through it with you.

Thanks,
[name], [firm]
```

### How the workflow runs
1. When the preparer marks a return ready in your practice software or tracking sheet, the workflow sends the approval email with the summary and the link.
2. It sends reminders on your schedule until it sees an approval (e-signature, portal approval or a written reply a person confirms), or a question.
3. A question goes to the preparer. Nothing is answered automatically.
4. When approval comes in, the signed document or the client's written confirmation is saved to their folder with the date, and the return is marked ready to file.
5. A daily list shows the team every return waiting for approval, how many days it has waited, and which clients need a call.

### What stays with you
The return itself, any answer to a client's question, the decision to file, and the call to a client who won't respond. If AI drafts a summary or a reply, a person checks it before it goes. US preparers: check [Section 7216 consent](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/section-7216-consent-before-automation-or-ai/) before return information passes through a new tool. Missing records are a different job: see [Self Assessment document chasing](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/self-assessment-document-chasing/) and the [tax season client email calendar](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/tax-season-client-email-calendar/). US clients heading for an extension need the [tax extension email templates](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/tax-extension-client-email-templates/).

Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your practice software, e-signature tool, email and a spreadsheet), so your team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it, under the [pay-when-happy agreement](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agreement/). To see the steps for your practice first, [build your plan here](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=tax-return-approval-chasing).

### Do UK clients have to approve their Self Assessment return?
Gov.uk says that when an agent submits the return, the client must check the information and confirm it's correct before it's submitted. An e-signature or portal approval gives you a dated record of it.

### Can US clients sign Form 8879 electronically?
The Form 8879 instructions say taxpayers can sign by handwritten signature, or electronic signature if supported by computer software. The preparer must have the signed form before transmitting the return.

The Form 8879 instructions say to give the client a corrected copy. In both countries, send the changed return for approval again as a new request.
