## Tutoring centre enrolment, termly invoices and parent updates, without the evening admin
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/tutoring-centre-enrolment-and-termly-invoices/

Tutoring centre enrolment is the path from a parent's first enquiry to a pupil on the register: a trial lesson, an enrolment form, then a termly invoice and regular updates. A workflow can reply to each enquiry with trial times, send the enrolment form, issue each term's invoices from the register, remind only the parents who haven't paid, and send attendance and progress notes the tutors have approved. The centre still decides who enrols, what is charged and what is said about each child.

Tutoring centre enrolment runs in waves. A parent enquires on Sunday night, a trial gets booked by text on Tuesday, the enrolment form is a PDF that comes back half filled in, and at the start of every term someone spends two evenings building invoices from the register. Then come the reminders, the parents who say they never got the invoice, and the ones who ask how their child is doing. Every one of those steps is the same for every family, so it can run as one workflow while your tutors teach. This page is for tutoring and education centres in the UK and the US (tutoring center, semester or term, the process is the same).

### Where families drop out or payments slip
- An enquiry waits a day or two for a reply, and the parent books with someone who answered first
- A trial lesson happens, but nobody follows up with the enrolment form while the parent is still keen
- The enrolment form comes back without emergency contacts, consent answers or the subjects needed
- Termly invoices are built by hand from the register, so they go out late and some are wrong
- Parents only hear from you when an invoice is due, never about attendance or progress

### The enrolment and billing workflow
1. A parent enquires by form, email or phone message. Within minutes they get a reply with trial lesson times for the subject and year group, and a link to book one. [Driving instructors](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/driving-instructor-lesson-bookings-and-test-reminders/) run the same booking and payment steps for one-to-one pupils.
2. The day before the trial, the parent gets a reminder with the address, what to bring and the tutor's name.
3. After the trial, the tutor adds a short note. You decide whether to offer a place, and the parent gets the enrolment form and your terms.
4. The enrolment form checks that required answers are there before it can be sent, then adds the pupil to the register and the class list. Swim schools do the same each term, asking current families to [re-enrol before the term ends](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/swim-school-term-bookings-and-waiting-list/).
5. At the start of each term, an invoice for every family is drafted from the register: the classes, the number of weeks and any sibling discount you set. You check the batch and send it. Music schools build [term fee invoices from the lesson timetable](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/music-school-lesson-scheduling-and-term-fees/) in the same way.
6. Parents who haven't paid by your due date get a polite reminder, then a second one. Anyone still unpaid goes on your list for a call. See [automated invoice payment reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) for a schedule.
7. Attendance is logged in the register, and missed lessons trigger a short message to the parent the same day.
8. Halfway through and at the end of each term, tutors write a few lines on each pupil. A person checks each note before it goes to the parent.

### What the enrolment form should ask
| Section | What to ask | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Pupil | Name, date of birth, school year, subjects and current level | Puts them in the right group |
| Parent or guardian | Name, email, phone, who pays the invoices | Invoices and messages go to the right person |
| Emergency contacts | At least one other adult and their phone number | Needed if the parent can't be reached during a lesson |
| Collection | Who may collect the child, and whether they may leave alone | Safety at the end of each lesson |
| Medical and learning needs | Only what tutors need to know to teach safely | This is health data, so ask only what you need (see below) |
| Consents | Separate yes or no answers, for example to photos or to progress updates by text | One clear answer per use, recorded with the date |
| Terms | Fees, notice period, missed lesson policy, a tick to confirm they've read them | Avoids disputes about what was agreed |

### Children's data needs extra care
Most of the people on your register are children. Recital 38 of the UK GDPR says children merit specific protection with regard to their personal data, because they may be less aware of the risks involved. Information about a child's health, which can include medical conditions and some learning needs, falls under Article 9 of the UK GDPR as special category data, with stricter conditions for using it. In practice: collect only what tutors need, keep it in one place with restricted access rather than in email threads, tell parents in plain words how you use it, and delete it when a pupil leaves and you no longer need it. Check the ICO's guidance on children's information before you change how you collect it. Our [GDPR checklist before automating client data](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gdpr-checklist-automating-client-data/) covers the setup. US centres should follow their own state's rules; the same care makes sense everywhere. Nurseries hold even younger children's details; see [nursery enrolment and waiting lists](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/nursery-enrolment-and-waiting-list/).

### A termly invoice message you can copy
Email to parents with each term's invoice:
```
Subject: [Child's name]: invoice for [term name]

Hi [parent name],

Please find attached the invoice for [child's name]'s lessons this term: [classes], [number] weeks from [start date] to [end date], [amount] in total.

Payment is due by [due date]. You can pay by [payment method or link].

If anything on the invoice doesn't look right, for example a week you told us [child's name] would miss, just reply and we'll check it.

Thank you,
[your name]
[centre name]
```

### What stays with you
You decide who is offered a place, what each family pays, any discount or payment plan, and what happens when a family falls behind. Tutors write every progress note, and a person approves it before a parent sees it. The workflow never makes a decision about a child. If AI helps draft a message or summarise a tutor's notes, a person checks it first, and children's details are never pasted into tools you haven't checked.

## Driving instructor bookings: lesson reminders, block payments and test dates
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/driving-instructor-lesson-bookings-and-test-reminders/

Driving instructor bookings can run largely on their own: each pupil gets a reminder before every lesson, a payment link when their block of lessons is nearly used up, and the cancellation policy in writing when they book. A simple tracker also holds each pupil's theory pass date and practical test date, so the instructor is reminded in time to talk about readiness. The pupil still books, moves and cancels their own driving test, because DVSA rules say the instructor can't.

Driving instructor bookings fill your evenings. Pupils text to move a lesson, forget the one tomorrow morning, ask how many lessons are left on their block, and mention their test date in passing so you write it on the back of the diary. None of it is hard, but it's the same messages every week, typed between lessons in a car park. This page is for independent instructors and small driving schools in Great Britain, with the DVSA rules that shape what you can and can't do for the pupil.

### What eats an instructor's admin time
- Confirming next week's lessons one pupil at a time by text or WhatsApp
- Pupils who forget an early lesson and aren't at home when you pull up
- Working out who has paid for a block, how many lessons are left and who owes for last week
- Late cancellations, and the awkward conversation about whether to charge
- Test dates and theory pass dates kept in your head or on scraps of paper

### The DVSA rules that shape test reminders
The test itself belongs to the pupil, so the workflow reminds and records; it never books. Gov.uk says you must book your driving test yourself, that your driving instructor is not allowed to do it for you, and that it's against the law to book a car driving test for someone else. The same applies to changing and cancelling. For car tests, gov.uk (checked November 2026) says the pupil needs to give 10 full working days' notice to change or cancel without paying again, counting Monday to Saturday but not Sundays or public holidays, and a car test can only be changed 2 times. A theory test pass certificate number lasts 2 years, and if the pupil hasn't passed the practical test in that time they have to take the theory test again. These rules cover England, Scotland and Wales, and DVSA changes them from time to time, so check gov.uk first. Music schools have a similar date to watch: [exam entry closing dates set by the exam board](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/music-school-lesson-scheduling-and-term-fees/).

### A reminder schedule you can copy
For illustration. Change the timings to suit how you work. Every lesson message stops if the lesson is cancelled or moved.
| When | Who gets it | What it says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| When a pupil books | Pupil | Lesson times, pick-up point, your cancellation policy, and how to pay |
| Day before each lesson | Pupil | Time and pick-up point, with a reply option if something has changed |
| 2 lessons left on a block | Pupil | How many lessons are left, and a link to pay for the next block |
| Pupil tells you their test date | You | A note in the tracker, plus a reminder 3 weeks before the test |
| About 3 weeks before the test | You | A prompt to talk about readiness while the pupil can still move the test without paying again |
| Day before the test | Pupil | What gov.uk says to bring: their UK driving licence, plus the theory certificate if they took the theory test in Northern Ireland |
| Theory pass is 21 months old, no test passed | You and the pupil | A reminder that the certificate runs out at 2 years |

### Lesson reminder message
Text or WhatsApp, the day before:
```
Hi [Pupil name], just a reminder of your driving lesson tomorrow, [day] at [time], picking up from [pick-up point].

If you need to change it, please let me know by [cut-off time]. Lessons cancelled with less notice than that are charged, as in my cancellation policy: [link].

See you tomorrow,
[Instructor name]
```

### Block bookings and payments
1. Each pupil's record holds the block they bought and the lessons used, updated after every lesson. Swim schools keep a similar record for each swimmer, with [their stage, class and term payment](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/swim-school-term-bookings-and-waiting-list/).
2. When two lessons are left, the pupil gets a payment link for the next block.
3. When the payment arrives, the block resets and you get a one-line note.
4. Pay-as-you-go pupils get a payment link after each lesson.
5. Once a week you get a list of who owes what.

### A cancellation policy pupils read
Most disputes come from a policy the pupil never saw. Put yours in the first message, in plain words: how much notice you need and what happens if they cancel late or aren't there. Repeat the cut-off in every lesson reminder. Whether you charge in full, charge half or let a first late cancellation go is your decision; the workflow only makes sure the pupil was told. The same approach works for [salon deposits and late cancellations](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/salon-cancellation-policy-and-deposits/), and the wider tactics in [reducing no-shows](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reduce-appointment-no-shows/) apply to lessons too. Tutoring centres handle the same lesson bookings and payments for whole families: see [tutoring centre enrolment and termly invoices](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/tutoring-centre-enrolment-and-termly-invoices/).

### What stays with you
Whether a pupil is ready for their test, what each lesson covers, and any money decision such as waiving a late cancellation charge. The workflow never books, moves or cancels a driving test. If AI drafts a message, you approve it before it goes out.

Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". ### Can the workflow book or move my pupils' driving tests?
No. Gov.uk says the learner must book, change and cancel their own test, and that it's against the law to book a car driving test for someone else. The workflow only records the date the pupil tells you and reminds you both.

### How much notice does a pupil need to give to move a car test?
Gov.uk says 10 full working days for car tests, counting Monday to Saturday, to change or cancel without paying again. A car test can be changed 2 times. Check gov.uk for the current rules before advising a pupil.

## Vet vaccination reminders: boosters, flea and worm treatment and follow-ups
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/vet-practice-vaccination-reminders/

Vet vaccination reminders tell a pet owner that their animal is due a booster and ask them to book. Most practice management systems send the first reminder; the pets that go overdue belong to owners who ignore it. A short follow-up sequence closes the gap: a second reminder on another channel, a weekly list of overdue pets for reception to call, and simple follow-ups after appointments, with the vet setting every due date.

Vet vaccination reminders mostly reach the owners who were going to book anyway. The rest read the text on the school run and forget. A few months later the dog is well past its booster, the cat's flea treatment ran out in spring, and nobody at the practice noticed because the system sent one reminder and moved on. This page is for small vet practices in the UK and the US. It doesn't tell you which vaccines a pet needs or how often: that's the vet's decision for each animal.

### Where vaccination reminders lose pets
- The system sends one reminder, then stops. Nobody owns the owners who didn't reply.
- The reminder goes to an old mobile number or an email nobody reads, and the bounce is never checked.
- Multi-pet households get separate messages on different days, so they book one pet and forget the others.
- A pet has died or been rehomed, and the reminders keep coming, which upsets the owner.

### The vet sets the dates, the system follows them
Which vaccines a pet gets, how often boosters are due and which parasite treatment suits it are clinical decisions made by the vet for that animal. The automation only reads the due dates the vet recorded in your practice management system and works from those. For flea and worm products there is one more point in the UK: veterinary medicines are sold in legal categories set by the Veterinary Medicines Regulations 2013, from prescription-only (POM-V) to the general sales list (AVM-GSL). The RCVS Code says a vet must carry out a clinical assessment of an animal under their care before prescribing a POM-V medicine. So a reminder for a prescription product should invite the owner to book a check or ask the practice, not promise a repeat supply.

### A reminder sequence for boosters
For illustration. The timings count from the due date your vet recorded. Change them to suit your practice. Every step stops the moment the owner books.
| When | Channel | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 2 to 4 weeks before due | Text or email (your system's usual reminder) | Your pet is due their booster, here's how to book. |
| Due date, not booked | The other channel | A short second reminder with a booking link or phone number. All the household's pets that are due go in one message. |
| 2 weeks after due | Text | A friendly nudge offering two or three real appointment times. |
| 4 weeks after due | Reception call list | The pet goes on this week's call list, oldest overdue first, with the owner's other pets shown. |
| After the call | Recorded by a person | Booked, call back on a date, pet has died, rehomed, moved away, now registered elsewhere, or please don't contact. The list updates. |

### Second reminder for an owner who hasn't booked
Text or email (edit the wording to suit your practice):
```
Hi [Owner first name], this is [Practice name]. Our records show [Pet name] is due their [vaccination or booster] and we haven't got them booked in yet.

You can book here: [booking link], or call us on [phone number].

If [Pet name] is no longer with you, or you've moved to another practice, just reply and let us know so we can update our records.

Thanks,
[Practice name]
```

### Flea, worm and after-appointment follow-ups
1. Flea and worm reminders follow the interval the vet or nurse recorded for that pet and product, sent with the booster reminder when they fall close together.
2. For a prescription product, the reminder asks the owner to book a check or contact the practice, so the vet can decide on the next supply.
3. After a procedure or a new prescription, a check-in message goes out on the day the vet chose, asking how the pet is doing, with the practice number for any concerns.
4. Any reply that mentions symptoms, pain or worry goes straight to a person, never to an automatic answer.
5. After a pet has died, every reminder for that pet stops at once.

### Keep messages short and confidential
Reminders can be read by anyone who picks up the owner's phone. Keep them to the practice name, the pet's name, what's due and how to book. Leave out clinical details and outstanding balances. In the UK, the RCVS Code says vets should not disclose information about a client or their animal to any third party, that the duty extends to support staff, and that clients' personal data must be handled in line with the GDPR, while data about the animal falls outside it. US practices should check their own state rules. This isn't legal advice.

### If your practice system already sends reminders
Most veterinary practice management systems have vaccination reminders built in. Switch them on and use them first. The gap is what happens after the first reminder: the overdue list, replies that land nowhere and bounced contact details. That's the part worth building, the same way [eye test recall for opticians](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/optician-eye-test-recall/) and [physio rebooking reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/physio-rebooking-reminders/) work best when the system does the sending and a person handles the exceptions. Groomers and kennels keep the same vaccination dates from the other side: see [dog groomer bookings and vaccination records](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/dog-groomer-bookings-and-vaccination-records/).

### How Mike Automations would build it
A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how reminders run at your practice today and where pets slip through. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example "every pet past its booster date gets two follow-ups, and reception gets one call list every Monday". It's built on the tools you already use (your practice management system where it allows a connection, your email and text service, Google Sheets or Excel), so your team has nothing new to learn. It goes live in 2-3 days, costs [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it. A person at the practice approves the wording of every message before anything is sent. To see the steps first, [build a plan for this workflow](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=vet-practice-vaccination-reminders).

### How often should pets have boosters?
That's the vet's decision for each animal. The reminders don't set any schedule; they follow the due dates the vet records in your practice management system.

### What happens when a pet has died?
As soon as the practice records it, or the owner replies to say so, every reminder for that pet stops. A person decides whether anything else is sent.

### Can it send repeat flea and worm treatments automatically?
It can remind owners when treatment is due. For prescription-only products, the RCVS Code says the vet must carry out a clinical assessment before prescribing, so the reminder asks the owner to book or contact the practice instead of promising a supply.

## Eye test recall reminders: following up patients who don't book
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/optician-eye-test-recall/

Eye test recall reminders tell a patient their next sight test is due and ask them to book. Most optical practice software sends the first reminder, but patients who ignore it drift for months, and contact lens wearers miss aftercare checks without anyone noticing. A short follow-up sequence fixes that: a second reminder by a different channel, a separate aftercare track for lens wearers, and a weekly call list for a person at the practice to work through.

Eye test recall reminders work well for the patients who were going to book anyway. The rest mean to call, forget, and turn up two years later with a headache and an expired contact lens prescription. This page is for small independent opticians in the UK and US: a recall follow-up sequence, a separate aftercare track for lens wearers, messages to copy, and what to keep with your team. It never sets how often anyone should be seen: that is the optometrist's call for each patient.

### Where recall patients slip through
- The practice system sends one reminder and stops. Nobody owns the patients who didn't reply.
- Recall dates are set in the test room but never reach the reminder list, or the recall type is wrong.
- Contact lens wearers keep buying lenses and skip their aftercare appointment.
- Messages go to an old mobile number and the failed text is never checked.
- One parent books for the whole family, and a child's recall is quietly missed.

### Who sets the recall interval
The interval is a clinical decision, made for each patient. For England, the NHS says people who are eligible for a free NHS sight test can have one every 2 years, and more often if their optometrist recommends it (nhs.uk, page last reviewed April 2023). Eligibility includes people under 16, 16 to 18 year olds in full-time education, people aged 60 or over, and people with diabetes or glaucoma, among others listed on the same NHS page. Private patients, US patients and contact lens aftercare follow whatever the optometrist or prescriber records. So the automation never decides when someone is due. It reads the recall date and recall type set in your practice system and works from those.

### A recall and aftercare sequence
For illustration. The gaps count from the date your optometrist set, and every step stops the moment the patient books.
| When | Sight test recall | Contact lens aftercare |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 4 weeks before due | Your software's usual reminder | Reminder that aftercare is due, with a booking link |
| Due date, not booked | Second reminder by the other channel | Second reminder, mentioning the prescription end date the prescriber set |
| 2 weeks after due | Text offering two or three real slots | Text offering slots, plus a note to the team if the patient is still ordering lenses |
| 4 weeks after due | Patient goes on this week's call list | Patient goes on the call list, flagged as a lens wearer |
| After the call | A person records the outcome | A person records the outcome and any change to the lens order |
| 3 months after due, no answer | One last letter or email, then a person marks them lapsed | One last message, then the dispensing team decides what happens to lens orders |

### Second reminder for a patient who hasn't booked
Text or email (edit the wording to suit your practice):
```
Hi [First name], this is [Practice name]. Our records show your [eye test / contact lens check] is due and we haven't got you booked in yet.

You can book here: [booking link], or call us on [phone number].

If you've moved or now go to another optician, just reply and let us know so we can update your record.

Thanks,
[Practice name]
```

### What to automate and what to keep with a person
1. Read recall dates and recall types from your practice system each week, so sight test and aftercare patients get the right message. Audiology practices run the same weekly read for [hearing checks and hearing aid services](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/hearing-care-recall-reminders/).
2. Send the second and third reminders on the other channel, and stop them as soon as a booking appears.
3. Move failed texts and bounced emails straight to the call list with a note to update the details.
4. Build one weekly call list, oldest overdue first, with family members grouped and lens wearers flagged.
5. Record every call outcome in one place, so nobody is called twice and "please don't contact" is respected everywhere.
6. Keep these with a person: anything clinical, symptoms a patient mentions in a reply, lens supply decisions, complaints, and marking anyone lapsed.

### Replies that need a person straight away
Some patients answer a recall message with a symptom: sudden blurred vision, flashes, a painful red eye. A reminder system should never answer those. Every reply goes to a shared inbox a person reads every day, and replies that mention pain, sudden changes or injury go to the top of the list with a note to call the patient back that day. Keep the messages themselves short: the practice name, that a check is due, and how to book, with no clinical details. Check your own data protection and patient privacy obligations before changing how patients are contacted; this isn't legal advice. The [GDPR checklist before automating client data](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gdpr-checklist-automating-client-data/) is a good starting point for UK practices.

### If your practice software already does recalls
Most optical practice systems send recall letters, texts or emails. Use them first. The gap is what happens after: the overdue list nobody works through, replies to a no-reply address, and lens wearers who never come back. That's the part worth building, the same way [dental recall follow-up](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/dental-recall-follow-up/) and [vet vaccination reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/vet-practice-vaccination-reminders/) work best when the system sends and a person handles the exceptions. To see the steps laid out for your own practice, [build a plan for eye test recalls](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=optician-eye-test-recall).

A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how recalls run at your practice today and where patients slip through. ### How often should patients have an eye test?
The optometrist decides for each patient. For England, the NHS says eligible patients can have a free NHS sight test every 2 years, or more often if the optometrist recommends it. The reminders simply follow the recall date recorded in your practice system.

### Can contact lens aftercare reminders run separately from sight test recalls?
Yes. Lens wearers get their own track, based on the aftercare date and prescription end date the prescriber records, so a patient who is up to date on their sight test still hears about aftercare.

### Can AI reply to patients?
AI can help draft reminder wording or sort replies into booked, call back and needs a person, but a person approves every message and reads anything that mentions symptoms.

## Carer compliance for home care agencies: chasing documents and tracking expiries
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/home-care-agency-carer-compliance/

Carer compliance for a home care agency means holding the right checks and documents for every carer before they work, such as identity, right to work, a DBS certificate, references and training certificates, and keeping them current afterwards. In England, CQC's Regulation 19 asks providers to run robust recruitment checks and to monitor staff on an ongoing basis. A small agency can run it from one checklist per carer: automatic requests for what's missing, reminders before training or right to work dates run out, and a weekly list for the registered manager to act on.

Carer compliance is the paperwork that decides who can go out on a visit tomorrow. A new carer is ready to start, but one reference hasn't come back. A long-serving carer's moving and handling certificate ran out last month and nobody noticed. This page is for small home care agencies in England: what the rules ask for, a document checklist, an expiry and chase sequence, messages to copy and rota change notices. It sits next to our guide on [chasing candidate compliance documents](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/candidate-compliance-document-chasing/) for recruitment agencies, which works the same way, and agencies that also chase weekly hours can use [timesheet chasing](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/recruitment-timesheet-chasing/).

### What CQC and gov.uk ask for
CQC's guidance on Regulation 19 (fit and proper persons employed, updated May 2025) says providers must run robust recruitment procedures, including the relevant checks, and have a way of monitoring staff on an ongoing basis. It counts agency and bank staff as "persons employed". The information in Schedule 3 of the 2014 Regulations must be confirmed before someone is employed: proof of identity with a recent photograph, a DBS certificate where required, evidence of conduct in previous care work and why it ended, relevant qualifications, a full employment history with gaps explained, and relevant health information. CQC also expects providers employing social care support workers to follow the Care Certificate standards. On DBS, gov.uk says a check has no official expiry date and you decide when a new one is needed; if a carer is on the DBS Update Service, you can check their certificate's status online for free, with their permission. On right to work, gov.uk says you must check before you employ someone, and again when time-limited permission is due to expire. This is a summary, not legal advice.

### A carer document checklist
For illustration. Your own list depends on your policies, your commissioners' contracts and the care you provide. Agree it with your registered manager, then let the system chase against it.
| Document | When it's needed | Does it run out? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Proof of identity with a recent photo | Before the carer starts | Only if your policy says so |
| Right to work | Before the carer starts | Follow-up check if permission is time-limited |
| Enhanced DBS (with barred list where eligible) | Before the carer starts | No official expiry; your policy sets re-checks, or use the Update Service |
| Two references and reason previous care work ended | Before the carer starts | No |
| Full employment history, gaps explained | Before the carer starts | No |
| Care Certificate or equivalent | Within the time your induction policy sets | No, but keep evidence on file |
| Mandatory training (moving and handling, medication, safeguarding, first aid) | As your training policy sets | Yes: refresher dates from your training policy |
| Driving licence, business car insurance, MOT | Before driving to visits | Yes: each has its own date |

### An expiry and chase sequence
| When | Who gets it | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| On offer | New carer | One message listing only the documents still missing, with a secure upload link. |
| Every 2 days until complete | New carer | A reminder listing only what's still outstanding. |
| Day 5 | Registered manager | A note naming any carer still waiting on references or DBS, so a person can chase. |
| 60 days before an expiry | Carer | Reminder that a certificate, licence or right to work date is coming up. |
| 30 days before | Carer and coordinator | Second reminder; training is booked if needed. |
| 7 days before | Registered manager | The carer is flagged on the weekly list. A person decides what happens to their visits. |

### Reminder to a carer
Text or email (edit the wording to suit your agency):
```
Hi [First name], it's [Your name] at [Agency].

Your [document, e.g. moving and handling certificate] runs out on [date]. Please [book the refresher here: link / upload the new one here: link] before then.

If you've already done it, just upload the certificate and this reminder will stop.

Thanks,
[Your name]
```

### Rota change notifications
When a coordinator changes a visit in your rota system, the change can go out as one clear message to the carer, with the visit time, client first name and area, and a reply to confirm. Anyone who hasn't confirmed within the time you choose goes on a short list for the coordinator to ring. Keep care notes, key safe codes and health details out of these messages: those stay in your care system.
Rota change text:
```
Rota change for [day, date]: [visit time] with [client first name] in [area] is now [new time / given to another carer / added]. Please reply YES to confirm. Questions: call [office number].
```

### What to automate and what to keep with a person
1. Keep one checklist per carer, with the date each item arrived and any expiry date, in your care system or a shared sheet.
2. Send requests for missing documents and expiry reminders automatically, listing only what's due.
3. Check DBS Update Service status on your schedule where the carer has given permission, and log the date checked.
4. Send rota changes as one message per carer and list anyone who hasn't confirmed. A [security company](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/security-company-licence-and-shift-confirmations/) confirms guard shifts the same way.
5. Give the registered manager one weekly list: who's cleared, who's waiting, what runs out in the next 60 days.
6. Keep with a person: checking documents are genuine, the right to work check itself, reading DBS results and references, deciding whether someone can work, and any concern about a carer's fitness.

A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how carer documents and rota changes are handled today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working", for example "every carer has one checklist, reminders go out before anything runs out, and the registered manager gets one list every Monday". Carer documents are personal data, so keep them in tools you control. Charities chasing volunteer references and DBS checks can use the same steps: see [volunteer onboarding for charities](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/charity-gift-aid-declarations/). To map the steps for your own agency, [build a plan for carer compliance](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=home-care-agency-carer-compliance).

### Do DBS checks for carers expire?
Gov.uk says a DBS check has no official expiry date, and it's up to the employer to decide when a new check is needed. If a carer subscribes to the DBS Update Service, you can check their certificate's status online for free with their permission. Your own policy should say how often you do this.

### Does CQC say how often training must be refreshed?
Regulation 19 asks for ongoing monitoring and expects providers employing social care support workers to follow the Care Certificate standards. Refresher dates come from your own training policy and your training provider; the system just reminds you before they run out.

### Can automation clear a carer to work?
No. Automation requests documents, records dates and reminds people. A person checks every document, reads DBS results and references, and decides whether a carer can start or keep working.

## Removals company automation, from the survey to move day
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/removals-company-surveys-and-move-day/

Removals company automation means letting software send the repeat messages around every move: booking the home or video survey, following up the quote, taking the booking deposit, sending the customer a pre-move checklist, confirming the crew and timings before move day, and asking for a review afterwards. A person still prices every job, agrees the date and handles anything that changes on the day.

Removals company automation is for owners of small removal firms (moving companies in the US) who spend evenings chasing quotes, re-confirming dates and answering "what time are you coming?". Every move goes through the same stages, with the same messages at each one. Below: the stages, a timeline for one move, a pre-move checklist and a quote follow-up you can copy. It works with the email, calendar, phone and accounting tool you already use. Move dates often hang on the property chain, which estate agents track through [sales progression](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/estate-agent-sales-progression-updates/).

### The six stages every move goes through
- Survey booking: the enquiry gets an instant reply with a link to book a home survey or a video survey, plus the questions you need answered first (from and to addresses, property size, access, rough date).
- Quote follow-up: the quote goes out, then a short follow-up a few days later and one more before you'd need to release the date. Our [estimate follow-up email templates](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/estimate-follow-up-email-templates-contractors/) give you more wording.
- Booking deposit: when the customer says yes, they get your terms and a payment link for the deposit, and the date is only held once it's paid.
- Pre-move checklist: a week or two before, the customer gets a checklist (parking, keys, what to pack, what you won't move) and confirms the access details.
- Move-day confirmations: two days before, the customer gets the crew arrival window and the foreman's name; the crew gets the job sheet the evening before.
- After the move: the balance invoice, then one review request to every customer.

### One move, start to finish
For illustration: a three-bedroom house move booked about five weeks ahead. The timings are a suggested schedule; you set your own.
| When | What happens | Automatic or a person? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enquiry arrives | Reply with the survey booking link and the pre-survey questions | Automatic |
| Survey day | Surveyor walks the home or does the video call and records the inventory and access notes | A person |
| Same or next day | Quote prepared from the survey notes and checked | A person prices, the draft is automatic |
| Quote + 3 days | Short follow-up asking if they have questions | Automatic, stops on a reply |
| Quote + 7 days | Last follow-up: the date is not held until the deposit is paid | Automatic, stops on a reply |
| Customer accepts | Terms and deposit payment link sent; date held once paid | Automatic, a person confirms the date |
| Move date - 14 days | Pre-move checklist; customer confirms parking and access | Automatic |
| Move date - 2 days | Arrival window, foreman's name, balance due and how to pay | Automatic |
| Evening before | Crew job sheet: addresses, access, inventory, special items | Automatic |
| Day after the move | Balance invoice if unpaid, then a review request | Automatic |

### Home survey or video survey
Some customers would rather show you round on a video call than book a visit, and it saves your surveyor a drive. For US interstate moves, FMCSA's 2022 rule (in force from 27 June 2022) counts a live or pre-recorded video survey as a physical survey, requires movers to offer a survey for every household goods shipment, and says the customer can only waive it in writing. The same rule says the "Your Rights and Responsibilities When You Move" booklet goes to the customer with the estimate. If you do interstate moves, the workflow can attach the FMCSA link to every estimate and store the signed waiver when a customer declines a survey. Rules for local moves are set by each state, so check yours.

### Deposits, cancellations and your terms
Hold a date only when the deposit is paid, and say so in the quote follow-up. Put your deposit, cancellation and date-change terms in the same message as the payment link, so the customer reads them before paying. In the UK, the Consumer Contracts Regulations 2013 normally give consumers 14 days to cancel a service bought at a distance or off your premises, but regulation 28(1)(h) excludes "transport of goods" where the contract gives a specific date. Whether a particular removal falls inside that exclusion depends on the job (packing and storage are not transport), so take advice from your trade association or a solicitor on your own terms rather than relying on a rule of thumb.

### Pre-move checklist to send the customer
Email or text 14 days before the move:
```
Hi [name], your move with [company] is booked for [date]. To make the day go smoothly, please check these and reply to confirm:

1. Parking: can we park a [van size] at both addresses? If permits or a suspended bay are needed, tell us now.
2. Keys: when can you collect the keys to the new home? We can't unload before that.
3. Access: stairs, lifts, narrow gates or low beams at either address?
4. Packing: [we pack everything / please have everything packed and boxes sealed by the evening before].
5. Not moving: items we can't take, such as [paint, gas bottles, fuel, chemicals].
6. Valuables, documents and medicines: please keep these with you.
7. Anything new since the survey: extra furniture, a shed or a loft we didn't see?

Your arrival window and foreman's name will follow two days before. [Owner name], [company]
```

### Quote follow-up you can copy
Follow-up 3 days after the quote:
```
Hi [name], just checking you received our quote for your move on [date] from [area] to [area]. Happy to answer any questions or adjust anything we missed on the survey. We can't hold the date until the deposit is paid, so if you'd like to go ahead, here's the link: [deposit link]. [Owner name], [company]
```

### Move-day confirmations and the crew
1. Two days before, the customer gets the arrival window, the foreman's first name and phone number, and the balance due with how to pay.
2. If they reply with a change (a new key time, a parking problem), it goes to you, not to the crew.
3. The evening before, each crew gets one job sheet: both addresses, access notes, the survey inventory, items needing special handling and the customer's number.
4. On the day, the foreman ticks "loaded" and "delivered" on their phone, so the office knows where each job is without phoning. Couriers use the same tick, with a photo, as [proof of delivery](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/courier-proof-of-delivery-and-failed-delivery-messages/) for the customer.
5. Any damage or a missing item is recorded with a photo at the time and sent to you.

### Reviews: ask every customer
The day after the move, send the same review request to every customer. Google's review policy says businesses must not selectively ask happy customers for reviews or offer anything in return, so the message goes to everyone and offers nothing. A customer who replies with a problem gets a call from you first. Our guide on [asking for Google reviews](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/ask-for-google-reviews-automatically/) has the wording.

A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how enquiries, surveys and bookings work in your firm today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price. It's built on the email, calendar, phone and accounting tool you already use, so your surveyors and crews don't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. You can [build a draft plan for this workflow](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=removals-company-surveys-and-move-day) first. You approve every message, and a person stays in charge of prices, dates and anything that goes wrong on the day.

### What should a small removals company automate first?
Usually the quote follow-up and the deposit link, because quotes that are never followed up are lost work. Then the pre-move checklist and the move-day confirmation, which cut the "what time are you coming?" calls.

### Can the survey be done by video?
Yes, you can offer a video survey as well as a home visit. For US interstate moves, FMCSA counts a live or pre-recorded video survey as a physical survey, and the customer can only waive the survey in writing.

### Should I take a deposit before holding a moving date?
Holding a date only once a deposit is paid protects you from no-shows and double bookings. Put your deposit, cancellation and date-change terms in writing with the payment link, and take advice on how consumer cancellation rules apply to your terms.

## Pest control contract visits and reports, without the paperwork evenings
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pest-control-contract-visits-and-reports/

Automating pest control contract visits means the recurring visits for each commercial contract are scheduled on their own, the client's site contact is told before each visit, the technician's findings become a visit report sent the same day, follow-up treatments are booked from the report, and renewal reminders go out before each contract ends. The technician still inspects, treats and recommends, and a person checks every report before it goes out.

Pest control contract visits are the steady income of a pest control business: restaurants, warehouses, offices and schools paying for routine visits through the year, much like a [commercial cleaning round](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/cleaning-business-automation/). They're also where the admin piles up. Each visit needs booking with a site contact, a report the client can file for their own audits, any follow-up treatment booked, and the contract renewed on time. This page is for small pest control firms in the UK and the US. It covers the flow for one contract, what a visit report should hold, and a report email you can copy.

### Where contract admin goes wrong
- Routine visits are booked from memory or a spreadsheet, so one slips and the client's audit file has a gap.
- The site contact isn't told you're coming, and the technician waits at reception or can't get into the bin store.
- Reports are written up in the evening or at the weekend, and reach the client days later.
- A follow-up treatment is agreed on site but never booked.
- The contract end date passes without anyone noticing, and the client drifts or shops around.
- Technician certificates expire and nobody is watching the dates.

### One commercial contract through the year
For illustration: a restaurant on a contract with routine visits every eight weeks and call-outs as needed. Your own visit frequency is whatever the contract says.
| When | What happens | Automatic or a person? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Contract signed | Every routine visit for the contract year is put in the diary, spread across your technicians' routes | Automatic, a person checks the routes |
| Visit - 3 working days | Site contact told the date, time window and technician, asked about access and any sightings | Automatic |
| Evening before | Technician gets the site notes, bait point map and last visit's findings | Automatic |
| On site | Technician fills in the visit form on their phone: points checked, activity, treatment, recommendations, photos | Technician |
| Same day | Draft visit report built from the form; office checks it, then it's sent to the client and filed | Draft automatic, a person approves |
| Follow-up needed | Follow-up visit booked within the time the technician set, client told the date | Automatic, technician sets the timing |
| Recommendation open | Client reminded of proofing or hygiene actions still open at the next visit notice | Automatic |
| Contract end - 60 days | Renewal reminder with the year's visit summary and the new price | Automatic, a person sets the price |

### What a visit report should include
Commercial clients usually keep your reports in their own pest control file for audits and inspections, so make every report complete and in the same layout. Check your contract and your trade body or state rules for anything they require you to record; this list is a practical starting point, not a legal definition. A [pool service visit report](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pool-service-visit-reports/) follows the same idea, with water readings and photos sent after every visit.
1. Client, site address, date, time in and out, and the technician's name.
2. Type of visit: routine, follow-up or call-out.
3. Each monitoring or bait point checked, with its number and what was found.
4. Pest activity seen, where, and how much.
5. Treatment carried out: product, where it was used and how much, as your records require.
6. Recommendations for the client: proofing, hygiene, storage, with photos.
7. Follow-up planned, with its date.
8. Technician's signature and, where the client wants it, the site contact's.

### A visit report email you can copy
Sent once the report is approved:
```
Hi [site contact name],

[Technician name] visited [site name] today, [date], for your [routine / follow-up / call-out] visit. The full report is attached.

Summary:
- Points checked: [number]
- Activity found: [none / details]
- Treatment: [none / what and where]
- Your actions: [proofing or hygiene recommendations, or "none this visit"]

[If needed: We'll be back on [date] for a follow-up visit.]

Your next routine visit is due in [month]. If you see any activity before then, reply to this email or call [number].

[Owner name], [company]
```

### Follow-up treatments and open recommendations
Two things get lost most often: follow-up visits agreed on site, and the recommendations the client is meant to act on. The visit form has a field for each. A follow-up with a date becomes a booking straight away, and the client gets the date in the report email. An open recommendation, such as a gap under a door that needs proofing, stays on the site record and is repeated in the next visit notice until the technician marks it done. That gives the client a clear list and gives you a written record that you raised it.

### Renewals and technician certificates
Every contract has an end date, and the renewal reminder should go out well before it with a summary of the year's visits, so the client sees what they're paying for. A person sets the new price and approves the message. The same date tracking works for your team's certificates. In the UK, CRRU UK says that from 1 January 2026 buyers of professional rodenticides must show proof of competence at the point of sale: a CRRU UK approved course in the past five years or membership of a recognised CPD scheme. In the US, EPA says anyone who applies or supervises the use of restricted use pesticides must be certified, with programmes run by states, territories and tribes and a maximum recertification interval of five years. Many states also require certification for commercial use of other pesticides, so check your state lead agency. The workflow can remind you before each technician's date comes up.

### What stays with you
The technician decides what is found, what is used and what is recommended. A person approves every report before it goes to a client, sets every renewal price and handles any complaint. If AI drafts the report summary from the technician's notes, a person checks it against the form first. Site photos and contact details are client data, so keep them in your own records and tell clients how you use them.

It's built on the tools you already use: your calendar, email, a shared drive, phones for the visit form, and your job software or accounting tool where it allows a connection. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/) ($1,500 for the first 3 clients), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it. You can [build a draft plan for this workflow](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=pest-control-contract-visits-and-reports) first, or compare it with [HVAC maintenance agreement renewals](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/hvac-maintenance-agreement-renewals/) and [lawn care seasonal renewals](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/lawn-care-seasonal-renewals/), which work the same way.

### Can the visit report be written on site?
Yes. The technician fills in a form on their phone, with photos, and the report is built from it. A person checks the draft before it goes to the client, usually the same day.

### How do I stop routine visits being missed?
Put every routine visit for the contract year in the diary when the contract is signed, and have the workflow warn you about any visit not completed by its due date.

### What regulations apply to pest control records?
It depends on where you work and what you use. Check your contract, your trade body and, in the US, your state lead agency. This page names only the certification points it could check on CRRU UK and EPA sources.

## Estate agent sales progression updates, automated
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/estate-agent-sales-progression-updates/

Estate agent sales progression is the work an agent does between an offer being accepted and completion: sending the memorandum of sale, chasing both solicitors and the buyer's mortgage, and keeping buyer and seller informed. An automated sales progression workflow keeps one milestone table per sale, sends the chase emails and the buyer and seller updates on a schedule, and flags any sale that has gone quiet so a negotiator can pick up the phone.

Estate agent sales progression updates are where a sale is held together or quietly lost. Once an offer is accepted, the seller wants to know when to book [the removals](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/removals-company-surveys-and-move-day/), the buyer wants to know where their mortgage is, and both solicitors are waiting on someone else. Most of a progressor's day is the same emails and calls: "any news on searches?", "has the mortgage offer arrived?". Those can run as a workflow, so your progressor spends their time on the sales that are actually stuck. This guide is the agent's side of the chain. The solicitor's side, keeping their own client informed, is covered in [conveyancing client updates](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/conveyancing-client-progress-updates/).

### Why sales go quiet after the board says sold
- The memorandum of sale goes out, then nobody hears anything for weeks
- Chasing both solicitors depends on one progressor remembering every file
- The buyer's mortgage valuation or [survey](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/surveyor-booking-and-report-delivery/) is booked, but nobody tells the agent the result
- Sellers ring the branch for news the branch doesn't have
- A problem further up the chain only surfaces when exchange is supposed to happen

### A milestone table for every sale
This is the heart of the workflow: one row per milestone, per sale, with who you need it from and when to chase. The chase timings below are suggestions; change the rows and timings to match how your office works. A milestone counts as done only when your team ticks it, never just because a date has passed. The stage before an offer, from portal enquiry to viewing, is covered for US and Australian agents in [real estate agent lead follow-up](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/real-estate-agent-lead-follow-up/).
| Milestone | Who it comes from | First chase (suggested) | Who is updated when it's done |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Offer accepted, memorandum of sale sent | Your office | Same day | Buyer, seller, both solicitors |
| Both solicitors instructed, ID checks done | Buyer and seller | After 3 working days | The other agents in the chain |
| Draft contract pack sent | Seller's solicitor | After 7 working days | Seller and buyer |
| Searches ordered | Buyer's solicitor | After 7 working days | Buyer |
| Mortgage valuation done | Buyer or their broker | After 5 working days | Seller (just that it's done) |
| Survey done, any renegotiation settled | Buyer | After the survey date | Seller, if anything changes |
| Mortgage offer issued | Buyer or their broker | Weekly | Seller |
| Enquiries raised and answered | Both solicitors | Weekly | Seller, with what is outstanding |
| Ready to exchange, dates agreed | Both solicitors | Daily in the last week | Buyer, seller, the chain |
| Exchanged, then completed | Both solicitors | Not chased | Buyer and seller, then keys arranged |

### What the workflow does
1. When a sale is agreed in your CRM or sales spreadsheet, it sends the memorandum of sale to both solicitors and both clients, and creates the milestone table for that sale.
2. On each chase date, it emails the right person a short, polite request for the next milestone only, not a list of everything outstanding.
3. When your progressor ticks a milestone, it sends the matching update to the seller and the buyer, written and approved by your office in advance.
4. For the mortgage, it reminds the buyer (or their broker, if the buyer has agreed) to confirm the valuation and the offer.
5. Every Monday, the progressor gets a list of sales where nothing has moved for a set number of days, longest first.
6. Anything that needs judgement, such as a down-valuation, a survey problem or a chain break, goes straight to a person. The workflow doesn't write those messages.

### A chase email you can copy
Weekly chase to the buyer's solicitor:
```
Subject: [property address]: sale agreed [date], searches

Dear [solicitor name],

I'm the agent on the sale of [property address] to your client [buyer name].

Could you let me know whether the searches have been ordered and, if so, roughly when you expect them back? Our seller is keen to understand the timescale.

If you're waiting for anything from the seller's side, tell me and I'll chase it from here.

Many thanks,
[your name]
[branch name] | [direct line]
```

### Material information at the point of sale
Gaps in the listing often come back as enquiries during conveyancing, so it helps to pass what you already know to both solicitors with the memorandum of sale. The rules here have changed. National Trading Standards published material information guidance for property listings in three parts (Part A in 2022, Parts B and C in November 2023), but withdrew it in 2025 after Part 4 of the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act 2024 replaced the Consumer Protection from Unfair Trading Regulations from 6 April 2025. Section 227 of that Act treats leaving out information the average consumer needs to make an informed decision as a misleading omission. In June 2026 the government's home buying and selling reform roadmap said it would publish non-statutory guidance on the information in property listings, and later legislate for upfront sales packs. Until that guidance is out, check your obligations with your redress scheme or trade body. The workflow only attaches the information your office already holds for the property; it never decides what counts as material.

### What stays with you
Negotiation, renegotiation after a survey, managing the chain and every conversation that needs a human. The workflow sends the routine chases and updates your office has approved, and tells you which sales need you. If AI drafts an update, a person always approves it before it goes out.

## Client onboarding for coaches and consultants
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/coach-consultant-client-onboarding/

Client onboarding for coaches and consultants is everything between a good discovery call and the first session: the proposal, the contract and invoice, an intake questionnaire, booking the sessions and tracking how many are left. An automated onboarding workflow sends each of these in order once the client says yes, reminds them about anything unsigned or unpaid, and tells you when a package is nearly used up so you can talk about renewal.

Client onboarding for coaches and consultants is usually done by hand, one email at a time, by the same person who does the coaching. After a discovery call you write a proposal, then send a contract, then an invoice, then a questionnaire, then a booking link, and then you try to remember how many sessions each client has left. None of it is hard, but it eats the hours you could be working with clients, and a slow start is the moment a new client can cool off. The steps are the same for every client, so they can run as a workflow while you keep the conversations.

### Where onboarding stalls for a solo practice
- The proposal goes out days after the discovery call, when the client's enthusiasm has dipped
- The contract is signed but the invoice isn't paid, or the other way round
- The intake questionnaire comes back the night before the first session, or not at all
- Clients book sessions by email back and forth instead of a link
- Nobody tracks how many sessions are left, so renewal conversations happen too late

### What an automated onboarding workflow does
1. After the discovery call you choose the package in a short form. The workflow fills your proposal template with the client's name, goals and package, and you check it before it's sent.
2. When the client accepts, it sends the contract for e-signature and the invoice with a payment link, and chases either one if it's still open after a few days. Unpaid invoices get polite reminders on a schedule until they're paid.
3. Once both are done, it sends the welcome email with the intake questionnaire and your booking link, limited to the number of sessions in their package. If you're still choosing a booking tool, compare [Calendly with Google Calendar booking pages](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/google-calendar-appointment-schedules-vs-calendly/).
4. It reminds the client if the questionnaire isn't in a couple of days before the first session, and sends you the answers as a one-page summary to read beforehand.
5. After each session it updates the package tracker, so you can see sessions used and sessions left for every client. Personal trainers track packages the same way, with [weekly client check-ins](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/personal-trainer-client-check-ins/) between sessions.
6. When a client has a set number of sessions left, it reminds you to raise renewal. You decide whether to offer it and what to say. The general version, for any service business, is in our post on [automating client onboarding](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/client-onboarding-automation-service-business/).

### A package tracker you can copy
One row per client is enough. Keep it in a spreadsheet you already use; the workflow fills in the columns, and you only read it.
| Client | Package | Contract | Invoice | Intake | Sessions used | Sessions left | Next step |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| [client name] | [package name] | Signed [date] | Paid [date] | Received | [used] | [left] | Book next session |
| [client name] | [package name] | Sent, reminded once | Not yet sent | Not yet sent | None | All | Waiting for signature |
| [client name] | [package name] | Signed | Paid | Received | [used] | Two | You: raise renewal |

### A welcome email you can copy
Welcome email sent once the contract is signed and paid:
```
Subject: Welcome, [first name]: two things before our first session

Hi [first name],

Thank you for signing up for [package name]. I'm looking forward to working with you.

Before we start, two quick things:

1. The intake questionnaire (about 10 minutes): [questionnaire link]. It helps me make our first session about you, not about background questions.
2. Book your first session here: [booking link]. You can book the rest the same way, whenever suits you.

Your package includes [number] sessions. I'll keep track, so you don't have to.

If anything comes up before then, just reply to this email.

[your name]
```

### Intake questionnaires and personal data
Coaching intake forms sometimes ask about stress, health or personal circumstances. Under Article 9 of the UK GDPR, data concerning health is special category data, which needs extra care and a specific condition for processing on top of a lawful basis. If you coach in the US, check the rules that apply in your state. The simplest approach is to ask only what you actually use, store answers in one place you control, and never send the full answers around by email. The workflow sends you a summary inside your own account, not to anyone else.

### Consultants: the same flow with a statement of work
For an independent consultant, the proposal is usually a statement of work and the package is a set of days or deliverables rather than sessions. The workflow is the same: proposal checked by you, contract and invoice, a kickoff questionnaire, then a tracker of days used. It works much like [onboarding for a marketing agency](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agency-client-onboarding-automation/), without the account access requests. Firms that quote from files a client sends, such as a [translation agency](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/translation-agency-quotes-and-file-intake/), run a similar intake, and tutoring centres sell termly packages of sessions the same way: see [tutoring centre enrolment](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/tutoring-centre-enrolment-and-termly-invoices/).

### What stays with you
The discovery call, the coaching or advice, the price and every renewal conversation. You approve each proposal before it goes, and you decide what to do when a client goes quiet. If AI drafts a proposal or summarises an intake form, you always read and approve it before it's used.

## Translation quote requests and file intake for agencies
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/translation-agency-quotes-and-file-intake/

Translation quote request automation is a workflow that collects every request through one form (the files, source and target languages, deadline, purpose and whether a certified translation is needed), saves the files to a job folder and prepares a draft quote from the word count for a project manager to approve. Once the client accepts, it offers the job to suitable translators, tracks the deadline, sends the delivery and raises the invoice. A person still checks the word count, sets the price and decides who translates.

Translation quote requests arrive in every shape: an email with three attachments and no deadline, a scanned PDF of a birth certificate, a link to a shared folder that needs permission. Before you can price anything, someone has to download the files, work out the languages, get a word count and ask the questions the client left out. That routine is the same every time, so it can run as a workflow while your project managers spend their time on pricing and quality. Consultants and coaches run a similar enquiry-to-kickoff flow: see [client onboarding for coaches and consultants](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/coach-consultant-client-onboarding/).

### Where quoting and intake slow down
- Requests come by email, website form, phone and shared folders, so nothing is in one list
- Clients forget the target language variant, the deadline or what the translation is for
- Scanned PDFs and images can't be counted automatically, so they sit until someone looks
- Quotes go out late, and nobody follows up the ones that went quiet
- Accepted jobs are offered to translators one email at a time, and invoices go out when someone remembers

### A quote request form you can copy
Ask everything you need to price the job on the first contact. Each row below is one field on the form. Show the certified translation questions only when the client ticks that box.
| Field | Why you need it |
| --- | --- |
| Files (upload) | Saved straight to a job folder, never left in an inbox |
| Source language | Confirms the pair, especially for documents in more than one language |
| Target language and variant | For example UK or US English, European or Latin American Spanish |
| Deadline | Drives the price and which translators you can offer it to |
| What it's for | Publication, internal use, a court or an immigration application changes the work |
| Certified translation needed? (yes or no) | Changes the deliverable and who signs it |
| Who will receive it | For certified work, that organisation's own rules come first |
| Format back | Editable file, PDF, or the same layout as the original |
| Billing details and PO number | So the invoice is right the first time |

### What an automated intake and quote workflow does
1. Receives the request from the form, or from a shared inbox, and creates a job with a reference number.
2. Saves the files to a job folder in Google Drive, Dropbox or SharePoint, and confirms to the client what arrived. Sign and print shops confirm files the same way, then [send a proof for the customer to approve](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/sign-and-print-shop-artwork-approvals/).
3. Counts words in editable files, or reads your CAT tool's analysis export, and flags scanned PDFs and images for a person to count or estimate.
4. Builds a draft quote from your own rates for that language pair, deadline and service, for a project manager to check and send.
5. Follows up quotes that get no reply, then marks them lost after the last reminder.
6. When the client accepts, offers the job to translators who cover that pair and subject, and a project manager confirms who gets it.
7. Tracks the translator's due date and the client's deadline, and warns you when either is at risk.
8. Sends the finished files to the client and raises the invoice in Xero or QuickBooks, with [automatic payment reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) if it goes unpaid.

### Certified translations: what to collect
If you offer certified translations, the workflow can make sure each one carries the right statement, but the wording and the signature stay with you. In the UK, the gov.uk page "Certifying a document" (checked November 2026) says that to certify a translation, the translator confirms in writing on it that it's a "true and accurate translation of the original document", with the date of the translation and their full name and contact details. In the US, the USCIS rule at 8 CFR 103.2(b)(3) (checked on eCFR in November 2026) says a foreign-language document must come with a full English translation that the translator has certified as complete and accurate, plus the translator's certification that they're competent to translate from that language into English. Courts, universities and other receiving organisations can set their own requirements, so the form asks who the translation is for, and a project manager checks that organisation's rules before quoting.

### A quote email you can copy
Sent once a project manager approves the draft quote:
```
Subject: Your translation quote [job reference]: [source language] to [target language]

Hi [first name],

Thanks for sending [number] file(s). Here's your quote:

Words: [word count] ([counted from your files / estimated from scanned pages])
Service: [translation / translation and proofreading / certified translation]
Delivery: by [date and time]
Price: [price] [VAT or sales tax note]

To go ahead, reply "yes" or accept here: [link]. Once you accept, we'll confirm your delivery date.

[If certified: please confirm who the translation is for, so we can match their requirements.]

This quote is valid until [date].

[your name]
[agency name]
```

### What stays with you
The pricing, the choice of translator and the quality. The workflow never sends a quote, assigns a job or signs a certification without a person approving it. Client files often contain personal data, so access to job folders is limited to the people working on the job, and our [GDPR checklist for automating client data](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gdpr-checklist-automating-client-data/) applies to UK and EU clients. If AI is used to draft a quote email or summarise a brief, a person reads and approves it first.
