## Gift Aid declarations: collect, store and claim on time
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/charity-gift-aid-declarations/

A Gift Aid declaration is the donor's permission for a UK charity to claim back basic rate tax on their donation, 25p for every £1 according to HMRC. It must give the donor's name and home address, name the charity, say which donations it covers and confirm they're Gift Aid donations, and the charity must explain that the donor has to pay enough Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax to cover it. Automating it means every declaration is captured with the donation, stored as evidence HMRC accepts, confirmed to the donor and ready for the next claim.

Gift Aid declarations are easy to lose. They arrive on paper forms, online tick boxes, phone calls and collection envelopes, and someone types them into a spreadsheet weeks later. HMRC can audit any claim, and a declaration you can't produce means repaying the tax with interest. The steps are the same for every donor, so they can run as a workflow.

### What a valid Gift Aid declaration must contain
HMRC doesn't publish an official form, but it does publish model declarations and the rules. These fields come from HMRC's Chapter 3: Gift Aid guidance (updated October 2026, checked 11 November 2026) and its "Claim Gift Aid" pages on gov.uk. Use them to check your online form, paper form and phone script.
| Field | Required? | What HMRC says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Donor's name | Yes | A full name is recommended. No company names or joint names |
| Home address | Yes | For UK addresses, the house name or number and postcode are accepted. Donors outside the UK give a full address, and Channel Islands and Isle of Man donors don't give a postcode |
| Name of the charity | Yes | Full name, or a working name, logo or appeal that identifies you beyond doubt |
| Which donations it covers | Yes | For example "the enclosed donation" or "all donations I make from this date until further notice" |
| Confirmation they're Gift Aid donations | Yes | For example "I want to Gift Aid my donation" |
| Tax explanation | Yes, on the form or given separately | That the donor must pay enough Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax to cover the Gift Aid, and pay any difference. "I am a UK taxpayer" alone is not enough |
| Date | When the wording doesn't fix the period | Needed so the period the declaration covers is clear |
| Signature | No | Optional |

### Phone and in-person declarations
HMRC accepts declarations in writing (including email and text message) and orally. An oral declaration only takes effect once you've sent the donor a written record, unless you keep an audible recording. That record must include the details the donor gave, the tax explanation, their right to cancel within 30 days with retrospective effect, the date they made the declaration and the date you sent the record. HMRC also says that typing declarations into a database is not, on its own, an auditable record. So the workflow keeps the evidence itself: the online form submission, the scanned paper form, the email, or a copy of the written record it sent.

### A donor thank-you email you can copy
Sent after a phone or in-person declaration (it also serves as the written record):
```
Subject: Thank you for your donation to [charity name]

Dear [first name],

Thank you for your donation of £[amount] on [date of donation]. It will help us [one line on what it pays for].

On [date of call or event] you told us you'd like us to claim Gift Aid. These are the details you gave us:
Name: [full name]
Home address: [address and postcode]
Donations covered: [this donation / this donation and all future donations until you tell us otherwise]

Gift Aid lets us claim 25p from HMRC for every £1 you give. To qualify, you must pay at least as much Income Tax or Capital Gains Tax in the tax year as the Gift Aid claimed on all your donations to charities. If you pay less, it's your responsibility to pay any difference.

If you'd rather we didn't claim Gift Aid, reply to this email within 30 days and it will be treated as if you never made the declaration. You can also cancel at any time in the future. Please tell us if you change your name or address, or no longer pay enough tax.

This record was sent on [date sent].

With thanks,
[your name]
[charity name], registered charity number [number]
```

### Claim timing and record keeping
You can claim Gift Aid online through HMRC's Charities Online service, with a spreadsheet or with recognised software, and HMRC says claims of over 1,000 donations must use software. Each donation must be claimed within 4 years of the end of the financial period it was received in: the tax year for a trust, the accounting period for a CIO or charitable company. Small cash and contactless donations of £30 or less can go through the Gift Aid Small Donations Scheme without a declaration, claimed within 2 years of the end of the tax year. Declarations that cover ongoing donations must be kept for as long as the donations continue, then for at least 6 years after the period of the last donation (a charitable company counts from the end of its accounting period, a trust from the end of the tax year). HMRC also recommends checking active donors' details every two years, for example with a newsletter asking them to tell you if their tax status has changed.

### What an automated Gift Aid workflow does
1. Captures each declaration with the donation, from your online form, payment page, scanned paper forms and phone notes.
2. Saves the evidence (form submission, scan, email or written record) and links it to the donor and every donation it covers.
3. Sends the written record and thank-you email for phone and in-person declarations, and logs the date sent.
4. Records cancellations, changes of name or address, and returned mail with the date, and stops claiming where it should.
5. Builds the claim list for each period in the format your Charities Online upload or software needs, for your treasurer to check.
6. Flags any donation getting close to the 4-year limit, and emails donors whose details haven't been confirmed for two years.
7. Optionally, follows up [failed regular donations](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/gym-failed-payment-follow-up/) the way a membership business would.

### Volunteer onboarding, briefly
The same approach works for new volunteers: one form for contact and emergency details, a welcome email with the role description, a checklist of what the role needs (such as references or a DBS check where the role is eligible), and a reminder to the coordinator when something is missing. Home care agencies run the same kind of checklist for carers: see [carer compliance for home care agencies](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/home-care-agency-carer-compliance/). Donor and volunteer records hold personal data, so UK GDPR applies.

### What stays with you
The claim itself, and the judgement calls. Your treasurer or finance lead checks and submits every claim to HMRC, decides on unclear declarations and handles donor benefits, sponsored events and charity shop sales, which have their own HMRC rules. If AI is used to read scanned forms or draft a thank-you note, a person checks it before anything is claimed or sent. This is a summary of HMRC guidance, not tax advice. Charities funded by grants have another set of dates to watch, covered in [grant reporting deadline reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/grant-reporting-deadline-reminders/).

It's built on the tools you already use (your donation forms, email, spreadsheet or [donor database](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/spreadsheet-vs-crm-small-service-business/), and shared drive, where they allow a connection). Live in 2-3 days. [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it. To see the steps for your charity first, [build a plan for Gift Aid declarations](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/?g=charity-gift-aid-declarations).

### Does a Gift Aid declaration need a signature?
No. HMRC's guidance says a signature isn't required. What you need is the required details, the tax explanation and evidence that the donor made the declaration.

### Is a spreadsheet of donor names enough evidence for HMRC?
Not on its own. HMRC says transcribing declarations into a database doesn't show the donor made them. Keep the original evidence: the online submission, the scanned form, the email, or the written record you sent.

### How long do we have to claim Gift Aid?
HMRC says within 4 years of the end of the financial period you received the donation in. Claiming regularly, for example monthly or quarterly, keeps each claim small and easy to check.

## MOT reminders for garages, plus bookings, approvals and car-ready messages
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/garage-mot-reminders/

MOT reminders for garages are messages that tell each customer their vehicle's MOT is due and invite them to book, sent from one list of every vehicle and its MOT expiry date. Gov.uk says you can get an MOT up to a month (minus a day) before it runs out and keep the same renewal date, so a good reminder gives the customer the earliest date they can book without losing any days. The same workflow can confirm bookings, ask for approval of extra work and text the customer when the car is ready.

MOT reminders for garages are the simplest repeat work there is: every car on your books needs a test once a year, on a date you already know. Yet most garages still remind customers from a diary, a card index or a garage system's report that someone has to remember to run. When the workshop is busy, the reminders stop, and the customer books wherever comes up first in a search. This page sets out the MOT dates as gov.uk states them, a reminder schedule and message you can copy, and the other messages a garage sends every day that can run the same way.

### The MOT rules your reminders should follow
These are the gov.uk rules for Great Britain, checked in November 2026. Northern Ireland has its own rules and process.
- A vehicle's first MOT is due by the third anniversary of its registration. Gov.uk says some vehicles must be tested at one year old, so check the MOT fees table for those.
- You can get an MOT up to a month (minus a day) before it runs out and keep the same renewal date. Test earlier than that and the new expiry is a year (minus a day) from the pass date.
- Gov.uk says drivers can be fined up to £1,000 for driving without a valid MOT.
- The maximum fee for a car MOT is £54.85, according to the gov.uk fees table.
- If the car stays with you for repair and is retested within 10 working days, the partial retest is free. If the customer takes it away, the retest is free only for a listed set of items (lamps, wipers, tyres and others) and only if it comes back before the end of the next working day.
- Gov.uk runs its own free MOT reminder by text or email, sent one month before a car's MOT is due. Your reminder should arrive first, so the customer books with you rather than searching.

### A reminder schedule you can copy
Set the timing to suit your workshop. This assumes you hold each vehicle's MOT expiry date:
| When | Channel | What it says |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5 weeks before expiry | Email and text | Your MOT runs out on [date]. Book any day from [earliest date] and keep your renewal date. Booking link or reply to book |
| 2 weeks before | Text | Short reminder with the booking link and your phone number |
| 3 days before | Text | Last reminder, plus the expiry date |
| On expiry, not booked | Office list | Customer goes on a call list, or is marked as sold or moved on |
| Once booked | Text | Booking confirmation, then a reminder the day before |

### An MOT reminder text you can copy
First reminder, 5 weeks before expiry (edit the words in brackets):
```
Hi [first name], the MOT on your [make model, reg] runs out on [expiry date]. You can book any day from [expiry date minus one month plus one day] and keep the same renewal date. Book here: [link] or reply with a day that suits you. [garage name], [phone]
```

### The other messages a garage sends every day
1. Booking confirmation: date, time, what's booked (MOT, service or both), drop-off time and how to cancel, sent as soon as the booking is made, then a reminder the day before.
2. Service reminders: due by date or mileage from your last service record, sent with the MOT reminder when the dates are close so the customer books both in one visit. Bike shops do the same with [a reminder when each bike's next service is due](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/bike-shop-service-bookings-and-repair-updates/), and heating engineers with [yearly boiler service reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/boiler-service-reminders-heating-engineers/).
3. Extra work found: the technician's note, a photo and the price go to the customer by text or email with a link to approve or decline. Nothing is done until the customer says yes, and the reply is saved on the job. Collision repairers send a longer run of updates, covered in [body shop repair status messages](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/body-shop-repair-updates/). Phone repair shops send [the diagnosis and price to approve by text](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/phone-repair-shop-job-updates/) in the same way.
4. Car ready: a text when the job is marked complete, with the total, how to pay and your closing time. If you take payment by link, the [payment reminder workflow](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) covers anyone who forgets.
5. Review request: one message a day or two after collection, asking how it went and linking to your review page. Sent once, never chased.

### Where garage reminders usually break
- MOT expiry dates are typed in wrong or missing, so reminders go out late or not at all
- The car has been sold, and the old owner keeps getting texts
- Extra-work approvals happen over the phone and nobody writes down what was agreed
- Customers ring to ask if the car is ready because nobody told them
- Calls come in while everyone is under a car, and missed callers book elsewhere: a [missed-call text-back](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/missed-call-text-back-contractors/) helps there

### What stays with you
The test itself, your prices and every decision about the car. The workflow keeps the list, sends messages on time and records replies. It doesn't diagnose anything or approve work. If your messages promote services beyond the reminder, check the ICO's direct marketing guidance and keep a record of each customer's permission. If AI drafts a message or a reply, a person always approves it before it's sent.

Gov.uk says up to a month (minus a day) before the current MOT runs out, and they keep the same renewal date. Your reminder can work that date out and state it.

## Solar installer paperwork, from first enquiry to handover pack
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/solar-installer-paperwork-and-handover/

Automating solar installer paperwork means one record per job that moves from enquiry to survey, quote, signed contract, customer documents, installation and handover, with each message and reminder sent at the right step. For MCS installations in the UK, MCS says the installation must be registered no later than 10 working days after commissioning and the MCS certificate goes in the customer's handover pack, so a workflow that starts that clock on commissioning day keeps the deadline in view. The same approach works for heat pump installers and for US installers working to their utility's steps.

Solar installer paperwork grows with every job you win. A solar PV or heat pump job starts as an enquiry, needs a survey, a quote that gets chased, a contract, documents from the customer, often a grant or network application, and ends with a handover pack, a certificate and warranty registrations. Most of that lives in inboxes and on a whiteboard. This page sets out the steps where the dates matter, what MCS says about them, and a handover checklist you can copy.

### The job, step by step, and what each step needs
| Step | What you need | What can run on its own |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enquiry | Address, roof or property type, energy bills, photos | A reply within minutes with a short form for the details and photos |
| Survey | A booked visit and the customer's access details | Booking link, confirmation and a reminder the day before |
| Quote | Your design and price | Follow-ups on day 3, day 7 and day 14 until a yes or no |
| Contract | Signed contract and deposit, if you take one | E-signature request and a payment link |
| Customer documents | Bills, meter details, proof of ownership, grant forms | One checklist per job, reminders listing only what's missing |
| Installation | Booked dates, scaffold, materials | Date confirmations to the customer and your team |
| Handover | Certificate, manuals, warranties, test results | Pack assembled from the job folder and sent, warranty reminders logged |

### UK dates that come from MCS and gov.uk
Check these against the current MCS standard for your technology, since they can change.
- DNO notification: MCS's guidance for homeowners says the Distribution Network Operator needs notifying before the installer begins work, and that in some cases the installer can do this on the homeowner's behalf. Your workflow can hold the job's start date until you've marked the notification done.
- MCS certificate: MCS says registration on the MCS Installation Database must be completed no later than 10 working days after commissioning, and only by the MCS certified contractor who signed the contract with the customer. The certificate is included in the handover pack.
- Heat pump handover pack: MCS tells homeowners to expect a list of the system's key parts, health and safety guidance, a recommended servicing and maintenance schedule, the manufacturer's manuals, all relevant guarantees and warranties, and a copy of the MCS Customer Commitment.
- Boiler Upgrade Scheme: gov.uk says the scheme is open to people in England and Wales, the installer applies on the homeowner's behalf on the Ofgem website, and Ofgem contacts the homeowner to confirm the installer is acting for them. The grant is £7,500 towards an air source or ground source heat pump.

### For US installers
The paperwork is different but the shape is the same: a building permit, your utility's interconnection application and approval to switch the system on, plus any incentive paperwork. Each utility and local building department sets its own forms and order, so the workflow follows the steps you give it rather than a national rule. It still gives you a document checklist per job, reminders for anything missing and a date on every step.

### A handover checklist you can copy
1. Commissioning day: record the date and start the 10-working-day MCS registration countdown (UK MCS jobs).
2. Register the installation and save the MCS certificate to the job folder.
3. Add the commissioning and test results, the list of key parts with serial numbers, and the manufacturers' manuals.
4. Add the servicing and maintenance schedule and your workmanship warranty.
5. Register product warranties with each manufacturer, using their own process and deadline, and save each confirmation.
6. Send the pack to the customer as one link or one PDF, with a short note on what each document is for.
7. Set reminders for the first service visit and any warranty check dates, and ask for a review. Garages do the same with [MOT and service reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/garage-mot-reminders/).

### A document request you can copy
Customer document request after the contract is signed (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: [address]: what we need from you before installation

Hi [first name],

Thanks for going ahead with your [solar PV / heat pump] installation. Before we can book your installation date, we need:

1. [A recent electricity bill showing your MPAN]
2. [Photos of your consumer unit and meter]
3. [Proof of ownership, if needed for your grant]

You can upload them here: [upload link]. We'll remind you only about anything still missing.

Any questions, reply to this email or call [phone].

[your name], [company]
```

### Where installer paperwork stalls
- Quotes go out and nobody follows up, so they go cold: the [quote follow-up workflow](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/whatsapp-quote-follow-up-tradespeople/) fixes that
- The customer sends half the documents and the rest are forgotten
- Commissioning happens on a Friday and the certificate isn't registered until someone notices
- Warranty registrations sit undone because the serial numbers are on a photo in someone's phone
- The handover pack is built by hand for every job from five different folders

System design, pricing, every technical and safety decision, and every submission to MCS, a network operator, Ofgem or a utility. ## Surveyor booking and report delivery, from instruction to follow-up questions
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/surveyor-booking-and-report-delivery/

Surveyor booking and report delivery is the admin around a home survey: taking the instruction, getting terms of engagement signed, booking access with the estate agent or vendor, collecting what the buyer knows about the property, then sending the report and handling questions. RICS's Home survey standard says terms of engagement should be issued and returned before the inspection, and that the surveyor should offer to discuss the report after delivery. A workflow can run the chasing and the records, while the surveyor does the inspection and writes the report.

Surveyor booking and report delivery takes more time than most residential surveyors expect. A buyer calls in a hurry, the terms go out by email and wait unsigned, the agent takes two days to confirm a key collection, and the buyer's questions after the report arrive by phone, text and email. This page is for UK firms and sole surveyors doing RICS home surveys. Architects run a similar proposal-and-sign-off routine: see [architect fee proposals and stage approvals](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/architect-fee-proposals-and-approvals/).

### What the RICS Home survey standard asks for
RICS names its home survey products as the RICS Home Survey Level 1, Level 2 (survey only), Level 2 (survey and valuation) and Level 3. The Home survey standard, 1st edition, has been effective since 1 March 2021, and RICS's update of 28 September 2026 says members should keep working to it until the 2nd edition is officially announced. A few parts of the standard shape the admin directly:
- Before a contract is formed, the client should understand the levels, know the fee, agree the report format and method of delivery, and explain the intended future use of the property, for example buy to let (section 2.4).
- Terms of engagement should be issued and returned by the client before the inspection. Where that isn't possible, they must be agreed before the service is delivered, ideally before any advice on the property is given (section 2.6).
- The surveyor should offer to discuss the report's findings after delivery, keep a written record of that exchange and not go beyond the agreed terms (sections 4.10 and 4.13).
- Records must be stored securely, and the standard says the file is kept for up to 15 years (sections 4.11 and 4.13).

### A booking sequence you can adapt
For illustration: the order most instructions follow. The timings are yours to set.
| Stage | What happens | Who it goes to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Instruction | Enquiry form captures the address, property type, level wanted and intended use | Buyer |
| Quote and terms | Fee and terms of engagement sent for signature, with the level explained in plain words | Buyer |
| Terms chase | One reminder if unsigned, then a call from a person | Buyer |
| Access | Request for an inspection slot and key arrangements | Estate agent or vendor |
| Pre-survey questions | Short form on what the buyer has noticed and wants checked | Buyer |
| Confirmation | Date, time and access details confirmed to everyone | Buyer, agent, surveyor |
| Report delivery | Report sent in the agreed format, with an offer to discuss | Buyer |
| Follow-up | Questions logged and a written summary of each call kept on file | Buyer, file |

### Where it usually slips
- Terms of engagement sit unsigned, so the inspection date arrives without them.
- The buyer's worries (a crack, a damp patch, a planned extension) never reach the surveyor before the visit.
- Follow-up questions arrive scattered, and the written record the standard asks for isn't kept.
- The fee isn't paid before the report is due, and [chasing the invoice](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/invoice-payment-reminders/) becomes awkward.

### What an automated workflow does
1. Takes each new instruction from your website form or email into one list with its address, level and status.
2. Sends the fee and terms of engagement for e-signature, and reminds once if they come back unsigned.
3. Emails the [estate agent](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/estate-agent-sales-progression-updates/) or vendor with two or three times from the surveyor's diary and asks for access details.
4. Sends the buyer a short pre-survey form and puts the answers in the job file for the surveyor.
5. Confirms the date to the buyer, the agent and the surveyor, and reminds them the day before.
6. When the surveyor marks the report final, sends it in the format the buyer chose, with a link to book a call about it.
7. Logs every follow-up question and drafts a summary of each call for the surveyor to check before it is filed.

### Access request to the estate agent
Email to the agent or vendor to book access:
```
Subject: Survey access for [property address], instructed by [buyer name]

Hi [agent name],

We've been instructed by [buyer name] to carry out an RICS Home Survey Level [level] at [property address].

Could you let us know which of these times works for access?
- [option 1]
- [option 2]
- [option 3]

Please also confirm:
- Whether the vendor will be there, or where we collect the keys
- Any parking, alarm or pet details we should know
- Access to the loft, and to any garage or outbuildings

The inspection usually takes [length]. Thank you,
[surveyor name]
[firm name]
```

### Pre-survey questions for the buyer
Short form sent once the terms are signed:
```
1. Is the property freehold or leasehold, if you know?
2. What do you plan to use it for: your home, a let, or something else?
3. Have you noticed anything that worries you (cracks, damp, roof, trees, extensions)?
4. Are you planning any alterations or major work?
5. Has the vendor or agent told you about any past work or problems?
6. How would you like the report: PDF by email, or something else?
7. Anything else you want the surveyor to know before the visit?
```

### What stays with the surveyor
The surveyor advises on the right level, does the inspection, writes and signs off every report and answers the technical questions. If AI drafts a call summary or a message, a person reads and approves it before it goes out or into the file. Client files stay in the system you already use, stored as the standard and data protection law require.

RICS's Home survey standard says they should be issued and returned before the inspection. Where that isn't possible, they must be agreed before the service is delivered, ideally before any advice on the property is given.

### What are the RICS home survey levels called?
RICS Home Survey Level 1, Level 2 (survey only), Level 2 (survey and valuation) and Level 3.

## Dog groomer bookings and vaccination records, without the paper folder
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/dog-groomer-bookings-and-vaccination-records/

Dog groomer bookings and vaccination records are the routine of taking each booking, reminding the owner, rebooking the next groom and keeping each dog's vaccination record and consent form current. In England, licensed kennels and dog day care must see an up-to-date vet vaccination record for every dog and keep a register that includes consent forms, under GOV.UK statutory guidance. A workflow can send the reminders, ask for an updated record before it expires and flag gaps, while a person decides which dogs are accepted.

Dog groomer bookings and vaccination records sound like two jobs, but they collide at the door. A dog arrives for a groom or a day at daycare, and the vaccination card on file ran out last month. Or the owner forgot the appointment, and the six-week rebook never got made. This page is for dog groomers, daycare and kennels in the UK and the US.

### What the rules say about vaccination records
In England, the Animal Welfare (Licensing of Activities Involving Animals) (England) Regulations 2018 license boarding for cats or dogs, which covers kennels, home boarding and daytime care for dogs. Grooming on its own isn't one of the licensable activities in Schedule 1, so a groomer's vaccination policy is their own choice. The GOV.UK statutory guidance for dog kennel boarding and for dog day care (both updated 1 June 2026) says:
- An up-to-date vet vaccination record must be seen for every dog, covering canine parvovirus, distemper, infectious canine hepatitis (adenovirus), leptospirosis and other relevant diseases. Kennel cough vaccination may be required.
- A vet certificate of a recent protective titre test may be accepted instead of a booster, at the licence holder's discretion.
- Primary vaccination courses must be finished at least 2 weeks before the dog is accepted.
- The register for each dog includes vaccination, worming and flea treatment dates and consent forms, and records are kept for at least 3 years.
- Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland have their own rules, so check with your local council there.
- In the US, rabies vaccination is set by state and local law. The CDC's guidance for vets says to vaccinate dogs for rabies according to local laws. Any other vaccines you ask for are your own policy, so agree them with your vet and check your state and county rules.

### A booking and rebooking cycle
For illustration: a pattern you could start from. Set the timings to suit your services.
| When | What happens | Who it goes to |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At booking | Confirmation with date, time, prep notes and your no-show policy | Owner |
| New dog | Form for vet details, behaviour, health and consent, plus a vaccination record upload | Owner |
| 30 days before a record expires | Request for the updated vaccination record | Owner |
| 2 days before | Reminder with a link to move or cancel | Owner |
| Day before | List of dogs booked tomorrow with any missing or expired records | You |
| After the groom | Thank you and a link to book the next groom, on that dog's usual cycle | Owner |
| No rebook after the usual cycle | One friendly nudge, then stop | Owner |

### What an automated workflow does
1. Keeps one list of every dog with its owner, usual groom cycle and vaccination expiry dates.
2. Sends new owners an intake form with consent wording you approve, and files the answers and record upload against the dog.
3. Asks for an updated vaccination record before the current one expires, and reminds once if nothing arrives.
4. Sends booking confirmations and reminders by text, WhatsApp or email, with a link to move the appointment.
5. The day before, gives you a list of tomorrow's dogs with any record that's missing or out of date, so a person can call.
6. After each visit, sends a rebooking link timed to that dog's usual cycle.
7. Lists no-shows for you to review, and logs what you decided about any fee.

### Vaccination record request
Message before a record expires:
```
Hi [owner name], [dog name]'s [vaccine] on our records runs out on [date]. Before [his/her] next visit on [booking date], could you upload the updated vaccination record from your vet here: [link]. A photo of the card is fine. If [dog name] has a titre test certificate instead, you can upload that and we'll check it. Thanks, [business name]
```

### A simple no-show policy
A short policy, shown at booking and in every reminder, stops most arguments. The CMA's guidance on deposits and cancellation charges is explained in our [salon cancellation policy and deposits guide](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/salon-cancellation-policy-and-deposits/), and the same UK consumer law points are worth checking for grooming and daycare bookings. More ideas in [how to reduce no-shows](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reduce-appointment-no-shows/).
No-show and cancellation policy:
```
Changing or cancelling
You can move or cancel for free up to [48] hours before your appointment, using the link in your reminder.

No-shows and late cancellations
If you cancel with less than [48] hours' notice or don't come, we may keep your deposit of [amount] or charge a fee of [amount].

Vaccinations
We need an up-to-date vaccination record before [dog name] can be [groomed / stay with us]. If the record is out of date on the day, we'll have to rebook.

If we cancel
If we need to cancel, you get any deposit back in full.
```

### What stays with you
You decide which vaccinations you require, whether a titre certificate is accepted and whether a dog is turned away. Vet practices chase the same boosters from their side: see [vet vaccination reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/vet-practice-vaccination-reminders/). A person checks each uploaded record before it counts as current, and decides any no-show fee. If AI drafts a message, you approve the wording first. Owner details and records stay in the booking app or files you already use.

### Do dog groomers legally need vaccination records?
In England, grooming on its own isn't a licensable activity under the 2018 regulations, so it's your policy. Licensed kennels, home boarders and dog day care must see an up-to-date vet vaccination record for every dog, under GOV.UK statutory guidance.

## A supplier invoice approval workflow for small firms
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/supplier-invoice-approval-workflow/

A supplier invoice approval workflow collects every supplier invoice in one place, sends each one to the right approver by rules you set, reminds them until they answer, and records who approved what and when. It never approves or pays anything on its own: a person makes every decision and every payment.

In a small firm, supplier invoices arrive in three inboxes and get approved in a corridor. Someone forwards a PDF with "OK to pay?", the answer comes a week later or not at all, and at month end nobody is sure what was agreed. Getting each invoice in front of the right person and recording their answer is the same few steps every time, so it can run as a workflow.

### Where invoice approvals get stuck
- Invoices arrive by email to different people, and some never reach whoever pays the bills
- Approval is a forwarded email that sits unanswered while the approver is busy or away
- The same invoice is sent twice and nobody notices until it has been paid twice
- There is no record of who approved an invoice, or when
- Suppliers chase for payment before anyone knows the invoice exists

### What an automated approval workflow does
- Collects supplier invoices into one place, from a shared inbox or an upload form, with the supplier, amount and due date [read from the PDF](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/automate-data-entry-from-emails-and-pdfs/) for a person to check
- Sends each invoice to the right approver, by rules you set, such as supplier, project or amount
- Lets the approver approve, reject or ask a question from the email itself
- Reminds the approver if there is no answer, and tells you when an invoice has waited too long
- Flags an invoice that looks like one already received, so a person can check it
- Keeps a log of who approved what and when, and passes approved invoices to your accounting software where it allows a connection

### What stays with you
Every approval and every payment. The workflow moves invoices to the right person and records the answer; it never approves or pays anything on its own. You set the rules for who approves what, and you can change them. If AI reads the details from an invoice, a person always checks them before the invoice is approved.

## HMRC agent authorisation codes: getting them from new clients before they expire
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/hmrc-agent-authorisation-code-chasing/

An HMRC agent authorisation code is posted to your client after you request authorisation through Online Agent Authorisation. GOV.UK says the letter is sent within 7 working days and the client should tell you the code within 30 days, after which it expires and you start again. A short chasing sequence, counted from the day you made the request, gets the code back while it still works.

You take on a new client in December, request authorisation, and wait. The letter from HMRC lands on their doormat, looks like every other brown envelope, and goes in a drawer. By the time you ask about it, the code has expired, you request a new one, and the January deadline is two weeks closer. The request itself takes minutes. The time goes on the waiting and the chasing, and that is the same few messages every time, so it can run on its own.

### What GOV.UK says about the code and the link
Checked on gov.uk in November 2026. HMRC changes these services from time to time, so check the guidance for the service you need.
- Online Agent Authorisation: after you complete the request, HMRC posts a letter with an authorisation code to your client within 7 working days.
- The client should tell you the code within 30 days. GOV.UK says this is usually 30 days from the letter being issued, and the exact date is in the letter.
- After that date the code expires, and you have to start the authorisation process again.
- You make one request for each tax service, so a client can get several letters, each with its own code. If a code is entered incorrectly 3 times, the process starts again.
- GOV.UK says Online Agent Authorisation has not been available for VAT authorisations since 16 February 2024.
- Digital handshake (through your agent services account): you send the client a link, and they respond within 21 days. The link expires after 21 days, and then you start again.

### Why codes expire unused
- The client doesn't know a letter is coming, so they don't look for it or don't open it
- They read it, mean to send the code, and forget
- Two letters arrive for two tax services, and the client sends one code without saying which service it is for
- The letter goes to an old address because HMRC's record was never updated
- Nobody at the practice counts the days, so the first reminder goes out after the code has already expired
- A handshake link sits in the client's inbox because they don't have, or can't find, their sign-in details

### A chasing schedule you can copy
Day 0 is the day you submit the request in your HMRC account. The gaps here are for a posted code, which leaves about 30 days. For a digital handshake link, which expires after 21 days, bring every step forward by about a week.
| When | Channel | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Day 0 | Email | Tells the client a letter from HMRC is on its way, what it looks like, and to send you the code and the tax service named on it |
| Day 8 | Text or WhatsApp | "Your HMRC letter should have arrived. Please send us the code." With a way to reply or upload a photo |
| Day 14 | Email | Reminder, with the expiry explained: if the code runs out, the letter has to be sent again |
| Day 20 | Office task | A named person phones the client and checks the address HMRC holds for them |
| Day 26 | Alert to the team | The code is close to expiry. Decide whether to chase once more or plan a new request |
| Code received | Automatic | Reminders stop. A person gets a task to enter the code in the HMRC account |

### A message to send on day 0
Email to a new client (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: A letter from HMRC is on its way to you. We need the code in it

Hi [first name],

So that we can deal with HMRC for you, we have asked them to authorise us as your agent for [tax service].

HMRC will post you a letter in the next week or so. It contains an authorisation code. Please send us:
- the code, exactly as printed
- the tax service the letter names
- the date the letter says the code must be used by

You can reply to this email, or send a photo of the letter here: [upload link].

The code runs out about 30 days after HMRC issues the letter. If it does, we have to ask for a new one and wait for the post again, so please send it as soon as it arrives.

If nothing has arrived in two weeks, tell us and we will check the address HMRC has for you.

Thanks,
[name], [practice]
```

### How the workflow runs
1. When a person at the practice submits a request, they add a row to the tracker: client, tax service, route (posted code or handshake link) and the date.
2. The workflow sends the day 0 message and counts the days from that date. Each tax service is tracked on its own row, because each has its own code.
3. Reminders go out on your schedule until the client replies. A reply or an uploaded photo stops the reminders and creates a task for a person.
4. If AI reads the code from a photo of the letter, a person checks it against the photo before it is entered. Three wrong entries mean starting again.
5. A weekly list shows every open request, the days left, and which ones need a phone call or a new request.

### What stays with you
Everything inside HMRC. A person at your practice submits the request, enters the code and confirms the client appears on your list. The workflow never signs in to HMRC, never holds your Government Gateway details and never asks for the client's own sign-in details. It only sends the messages, counts the days and tells you who to call. Authorisation is one step of taking on a client: the rest is in the [accounting client onboarding checklist](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/accounting-client-onboarding-checklist/). Once you are authorised, the next wait is usually for records, covered in [Self Assessment document chasing](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/self-assessment-document-chasing/).

GOV.UK says the client should tell you the code within 30 days, usually counted from the letter being issued, and that the exact date is in the letter. After that the code expires and you start the process again.

### Is the digital handshake quicker than a posted code?

## Lien waiver tracking for general contractors: every sub, every pay period
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/lien-waiver-tracking-subcontractors/

Lien waiver tracking means knowing, for every subcontractor and every pay period, which waiver you asked for, whether it came back signed, and whether it matches the payment. A simple workflow can request the right waiver with each pay application, remind subs until it arrives, and give whoever writes the checks a list of what is still missing. A person still decides which form to use and when to release payment.

Lien waiver tracking falls apart at the end of the month. Pay applications come in, the owner wants waivers from every sub before releasing the draw, and someone in the office is searching email for a signed PDF from the electrician. One missing waiver holds up a payment, or the check goes out without it and nobody notices until closeout. Requesting, collecting and filing waivers is the same routine every pay period, so it can run on its own while you keep the decisions.

### The waivers you're tracking
Most contractors work with four kinds of waiver: conditional or unconditional, for a progress payment or the final payment. The names, the wording and the rules depend on the state. California is one example: its Contractors State License Board says a waiver must substantially follow one of four forms set out in the Civil Code, that a conditional waiver is only effective if the claimant is actually paid, and that in an unconditional waiver the claimant asserts they have received the payment. Ask your attorney which forms apply in the states where you build. This page is about keeping track of them, not about the law.
| Waiver | Usually requested | What to track |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Conditional, progress payment | With the sub's pay application, before you pay | Amount and through date match the pay application |
| Unconditional, progress payment | After the earlier payment has been received | It covers the previous period's payment |
| Conditional, final payment | With the final pay application | Amount matches the final balance, including approved change orders |
| Unconditional, final payment | After the final payment has been received | On file before the job is closed out |

### Why waivers go missing
- Waivers are requested by email, one sub at a time, by whoever remembers
- Signed waivers come back as phone photos and attachments, and get saved in different places
- The amount or the through date on the waiver doesn't match the pay application, and nobody compares them
- A sub's own suppliers and lower-tier subs owe waivers too, and nobody keeps that list
- The unconditional waiver for last month's payment is never requested, because this month's paperwork has already started
- At closeout, someone rebuilds the whole history from old emails

### A lien waiver tracker you can copy
Keep one row per sub per pay period. For illustration, as it might look a few days before a draw:
| Subcontractor | Pay period | Waiver needed | Status | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Electrical sub | October | Conditional, progress | Received, amount matches | Cleared for payment review |
| Electrical sub | September | Unconditional, progress | Requested, not received | Second reminder sent |
| Framing sub | October | Conditional, progress | Received, amount differs | Office to check against pay application |
| Plumbing sub | October | Conditional, progress | Not received | Call the sub today |
| Drywall sub | Final | Conditional, final | Received | Waiting for final change order to be approved |

### A waiver request you can copy
Email to a sub with a pay application (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: Lien waiver needed for [project], [pay period]

Hi [first name],

We have your pay application for [pay period] on [project] for [amount].

To process it, we need a signed [waiver type] for [amount], through [through date]. The form is attached. Please sign it and upload it here: [upload link].

[If you were paid for the previous period, please also send the signed unconditional waiver for that payment.]

We review payments on [date]. Waivers received after that move to the next review.

Thanks,
[your name], [company]
```

### How the workflow runs
1. When a pay application is logged, the workflow emails the sub a request with the form your attorney approved and one upload link.
2. It saves each signed waiver in the job folder under the sub and the pay period, and marks the tracker row as received.
3. AI can read the amount and the through date from the signed waiver and compare them with the pay application. Anything that differs goes to a person, and a person confirms every match before it counts.
4. It reminds subs who haven't sent a waiver, on a schedule you choose, and stops as soon as the waiver arrives.
5. After a payment is recorded as made, it requests the unconditional waiver for that payment, if your process uses one.
6. Before each payment review, it sends a list: which subs are complete, which are missing a waiver and which have a mismatch.

### What stays with you
Which waiver form to use, whether a signed waiver is good enough, and when to release a payment. The workflow doesn't write legal forms, doesn't hold or release money and doesn't decide whether a waiver is valid. It asks, files, compares and reports. Waivers sit next to the other paperwork you collect from subs: [certificates of insurance](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/subcontractor-coi-tracking/) before they start, and signed [change orders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/change-order-approval-workflow/) before the final numbers are agreed.

Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your email, shared drive, a spreadsheet and your accounting software where it allows a connection), so your team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. If you run many large projects with several tiers of subs, dedicated construction payment software may fit better, and we'll say so on the call.

### Does the workflow tell us which lien waiver form to use?
No. The forms and the rules depend on the state, so that is a question for your attorney. The workflow sends the forms you give it and tracks what comes back.

### Can it hold a payment until the waiver arrives?
It doesn't touch payments. It gives the person who releases them a list of what is complete and what is missing, and they decide.

## Dental treatment plan follow-up: patients who leave without booking
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/dental-treatment-plan-follow-up/

Dental treatment plan follow-up is the contact a practice makes after a dentist recommends treatment and the patient leaves without an appointment for it. A simple sequence works from the list of open treatment plans in your practice software: a short message a few days later, a second one by another channel, then a weekly call list for a person at the front desk. It never gives clinical advice and never discusses the treatment in a text.

The dentist explains the treatment, the patient nods, says they need to check their calendar, and leaves. Nobody is being difficult. They want to think about the cost, talk to their partner or find a free afternoon. Then a week passes, the front desk is busy with today's patients, and the plan sits in the software with no appointment against it. This page gives a follow-up sequence and a message to copy, and shows which parts can run on their own and which belong to your team.

### Why recommended treatment goes unbooked
- The patient needs time to think about the cost and nobody arranges a moment to come back to it
- They had a question they didn't ask in the chair, about pain, time off work or alternatives
- The front desk was busy when they left, so no appointment was offered
- The unscheduled treatment report exists, but it's long, and nobody owns it
- Follow-up depends on one team member's memory, and stops when they're away
- By the time someone calls, weeks have passed and the conversation starts from the beginning

### What a follow-up message should and shouldn't say
Keep it short and keep clinical detail out of it. A text or email can be seen by someone else, so it shouldn't name the treatment, the tooth or the price. In the UK, the ICO treats appointment details that reveal something about a person's health as health data. In the US, HHS says providers emailing patients without encryption should limit the amount or type of information they send (both checked November 2026). It says that the dentist recommended some treatment, that you'd like to help the patient book or answer their questions, and how to reach you. Questions about the treatment go to the clinical team, and questions about paying go to whoever handles that at your practice. Follow your own rules on patient consent for texts and emails, and stop as soon as a patient asks you to.

### A follow-up sequence you can copy
Day 0 is the appointment where the treatment was recommended. Change the gaps to suit your practice. Every step stops the moment the patient books, declines or asks not to be contacted. If the dentist marks the treatment as urgent, skip the sequence: a person calls.
| When | Channel | What happens |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Day 0 | At the front desk | The patient is offered an appointment before they leave. If they don't book, the plan is marked as open |
| Day 3 | Text or email | A short message: we'd like to help you book, or answer any questions |
| Day 10 | The other channel | A second message with a booking link or the phone number |
| Day 21 | Front desk call list | The patient goes on this week's list, with the dentist's notes for the person calling |
| After the call | Recorded by a person | Booked, thinking about it until a date, declined, gone elsewhere or asked not to be contacted |
| Day 60, no answer | One last message | A short note that the offer to book stands. Then the plan leaves the active list until the next visit |

### A first follow-up message you can copy
Text or email on day 3 (edit the words in brackets):
```
Hi [first name], this is [practice name]. At your visit on [date], [dentist name] recommended some treatment, and we haven't booked it in yet.

If you'd like to go ahead, you can book here: [booking link], or call us on [phone number].

If you have questions first, about the treatment or about paying for it, reply to this message and one of the team will call you.

If you'd rather we didn't follow up, just let us know.

Thanks,
[practice name]
```

### How the workflow runs
1. Each day it reads the list of treatment plans with no appointment from your practice software, by a report or a connection where the software allows one.
2. It sends the messages on your schedule, using wording your team has approved, and never includes the treatment details.
3. A reply stops the sequence and goes to a person. Nothing is answered automatically.
4. When an appointment is booked for the plan, or a team member records an outcome, the patient leaves the list.
5. Once a week the front desk gets a short call list: who to ring, when they were seen and what the dentist asked to be passed on.
6. The practice manager gets a monthly count of plans opened, booked, declined and still open.

### What stays with you
Every clinical decision and every conversation about the treatment or the cost. The dentist decides what is urgent and what can wait. A person at the practice makes the calls and records the outcome. If AI drafts a reply to a patient's question, a person checks it before it's sent. The workflow only keeps the list moving so that nobody is forgotten. Routine check-ups are a separate list, covered in [dental recall reminders](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/dental-recall-follow-up/), and missed appointments are covered in [how to reduce appointment no-shows](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/reduce-appointment-no-shows/).

A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how open treatment plans are followed up today and what your practice software can export. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your practice software where it allows a connection, your text and email service and a spreadsheet), so your team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it, under the [pay-when-happy agreement](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agreement/). If your practice software already has a follow-up feature that does this, we'll tell you to switch it on instead.

### Our practice software already sends reminders. Is this different?
Most software reminds patients about appointments that exist and check-ups that are due. This follows up treatment that was recommended and never booked. If your software already does that well, you don't need us.

### Will patients feel pressured?
The messages are short, offer help and give an easy way to say no. Every step stops when a patient books, declines or asks not to be contacted, and your team approves the wording.

No. Messages say only that the dentist recommended some treatment. Details are discussed by a person, by phone or at the practice.

## Boiler service reminders for heating engineers: every customer, every year
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/boiler-service-reminders-heating-engineers/

Boiler service reminders work when every job you finish leaves a due date behind it. A simple workflow can keep one list of customers and landlords with the date their next service or gas safety check is due, message them a few weeks before, let them pick a slot, and show you who hasn't replied. You still decide the diary, the price and anything about the appliance.

Boiler service reminders are easy to promise and hard to keep up. You fit or service a boiler in October, tell the customer you'll be in touch next year, and by next October the date is in a notebook, an old invoice or nowhere. The customer books whoever sends them a text first. Landlords are stricter: their gas safety check has a date, and they want it done before that date, not after. The list of who is due this month is the same job every month, so it can run on its own while you stay on the tools.

### Why the yearly service gets missed
- The due date lives on last year's invoice or certificate, not in a list anyone looks at
- Reminders go out in a quiet week, and then not at all from October to February
- A reminder goes out once, the customer means to reply, and nobody follows up
- Landlords with several properties get separate messages on different dates, or none
- Customers reply by text, WhatsApp, email and voicemail, and some replies are never answered
- Summer is quiet and winter is full, because nobody was asked to book early

### What landlords need, and what the workflow tracks
For rented homes there is a date to hit. The Health and Safety Executive says landlords must have gas appliances and flues checked every 12 months by a Gas Safe registered engineer, give existing tenants a copy of the record within 28 days of the check, and give it to new tenants before they move in. HSE also says a check can be done up to 2 months before the due date and keep the original date, which is the reason to remind landlords early. Homeowners are different: for them the annual service is a recommendation, and a boiler warranty may ask for one, so point them to their manufacturer's terms. This page is about keeping the dates, not about the regulations.
| Customer | What is due | When to remind | What to track |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homeowner | Annual boiler service | A few weeks before last year's date | Date of last service, appliance, how they like to be contacted |
| Landlord, one property | Gas safety check, with a service if they want one | Early enough to book inside the 2 months before the due date | Due date, tenant contact for access, where the record is sent |
| Landlord or agent, several properties | Checks on different dates | One message a month listing every property due soon | Each property's due date and access details |

### A service list you can copy
Keep one row per appliance, not per customer. For illustration, as it might look in early October:
| Customer | Address | Type | Due | Status | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Homeowner | 14 Hill Road | Annual service | 28 October | Booked for 21 October | Reminder the day before |
| Landlord | Flat 2, 9 Park Street | Gas safety check | 12 November | First message sent, no reply | Second message on Monday |
| Landlord | Flat 3, 9 Park Street | Gas safety check | 12 November | First message sent, no reply | Second message on Monday |
| Homeowner | 3 Mill Lane | Annual service | 5 November | Replied: call me after 5pm | You call today |
| Homeowner | 27 Bridge Street | Annual service | 30 October | Two messages, no reply | On Friday's call list |

### A reminder you can copy
Text or email to a homeowner (edit the words in brackets):
```
Hi [first name], it's [your name] from [business]. Your boiler at [address] was last serviced on [date], so it's due again this month.

You can pick a time here: [booking link]. Or reply with a day that suits you and I'll confirm.

The price is [price]. If you'd rather not get these reminders, reply STOP.
```

### How the workflow runs
1. When you finish a service or a gas safety check, the job is logged with the date, the address and the appliance. The next due date is set from it.
2. A few weeks before the due date, the customer gets a message with your wording and a link to book, or an invitation to reply with a day.
3. If they book, the slot goes in your calendar and they get a confirmation and a reminder the day before.
4. If they don't reply, a second message goes out on the schedule you choose. After that they go on a short call list, and the messages stop.
5. Landlords and agents with several properties get one message listing every property due soon, with the access contact for each.
6. Any reply that isn't a booking goes straight to you. If AI drafts an answer to a question, you read and approve it before it is sent.
7. Once a month you get a list: due this month, booked, no reply, and overdue.

### What stays with you
The work, the record and every judgement about the appliance. The workflow doesn't issue gas safety records, doesn't give advice about a boiler and doesn't change a price. It keeps dates, sends the messages you approved and tells you who needs a call. If a landlord's agent sends the reminders themselves, that side is covered in [compliance certificate reminders for letting agents](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/letting-agent-compliance-certificate-reminders/). For breakdowns that arrive while you're on a job, see [emergency call-out triage](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/emergency-call-out-triage-plumbers/).

## Medical records request tracking for personal injury firms
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/medical-records-request-tracking-personal-injury/

Medical records request tracking means knowing, for every client and every provider, what you asked for, when you asked, and what has come back. A simple workflow can keep one log, send follow-ups to providers on a schedule you set, file what arrives and give each case manager a weekly list of open requests. A person still reviews every authorization, every request and every record.

Medical records request tracking is where a personal injury case slows down. A client treated with six providers, and each one needs a request for records and a request for bills. Some take a portal upload, some want a fax, some use a records vendor, and one says the request never arrived. The case manager is supposed to follow up, but there are forty other files. The demand can't go out until the last record is in. Sending the request, checking on it and filing the result is the same routine for every provider, so it can run on a schedule while your team does the legal work.

### Where requests stall
- Requests are sent from individual inboxes and fax lines, and the only record is a note in the file
- Records and billing are separate departments at many providers, and only one of them was asked
- A provider rejects the authorization or asks for a fee, and the letter sits unopened
- Follow-up happens when someone remembers, not on a date
- The client mentions a new provider on a call, and it never reaches the list
- Records arrive, but nobody checks that the dates of treatment are all there

### A request log you can copy
Keep one row per provider per request type. For illustration, as it might look for one client:
| Provider | Request | Sent | How | Status | Next action |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Hospital emergency department | Records | 3 March | Provider portal | Received | Case manager to review dates of treatment |
| Hospital emergency department | Bills | 3 March | Fax to billing office | No response | Second follow-up due Monday |
| Orthopedic clinic | Records and bills | 5 March | Records vendor | Fee invoice received | Approve and pay the fee |
| Physical therapy | Records and bills | 5 March | Fax | Rejected: authorization incomplete | Paralegal to get a new signed authorization |
| Imaging center | Records and films | Not sent |  | Waiting for provider address | Ask the client |

### The authorization comes first
Every request rides on the client's signed authorization, and providers send requests back when it is incomplete. The federal privacy rule lists the core elements of a valid authorization: a description of the information, who may disclose it, who may receive it, the purpose, an expiration date or event, and the individual's signature and date. An authorization that has expired or is not fully filled out is not valid. Your attorneys decide the form your firm uses and whether a state needs something more. The workflow can check that a signed copy is on file and not past its expiration before a request goes out, and stop if it isn't. How long a provider has to respond and what it can charge depend on the state and the type of request, so the follow-up schedule is one you set.

### A follow-up you can copy
Follow-up to a provider's records department (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: Follow-up on records request for [patient name], date of birth [date]

To the records department,

On [date sent] we sent a request for [records / itemized bills] for the patient above, for treatment from [start date] to [end date]. A signed authorization was included. We sent it by [fax / portal / mail] to [number or address].

We have not received the records or a response. Please let us know:
1. Whether you have the request.
2. Whether anything else is needed, including any fee.
3. When we can expect the records.

You can reply to this email or call [name] at [phone].

Thank you,
[name], [firm]
```

### How the workflow runs
1. When a provider is added to a case, a row is created for records and a row for bills, with the provider's request method and contact details.
2. A person prepares and approves each request. The workflow sends it by email where the provider accepts that, or creates a task for the fax, portal or vendor.
3. It logs the date sent and sets the first follow-up date from your schedule.
4. On each follow-up date, it sends the follow-up you approved or puts a call on the case manager's list, and logs the attempt.
5. Letters back from providers, such as a rejection or a fee invoice, are logged against the right row and sent to the person who handles them.
6. When records arrive they are filed under the client and the provider. AI can list the dates of treatment it finds and point out gaps against the dates you asked for, and a person checks that list before anything is marked complete.
7. Each week, every case manager gets one list: requests sent, received, overdue and blocked.

### What stays with you
Which providers to request from, what the request says, whether an authorization is good, and what the records mean for the case. The workflow doesn't review medical records for you, doesn't write a demand and doesn't decide anything about a claim. It keeps the log, follows up and tells you what is still missing. Client records are sensitive, so the build keeps them in the systems your firm already uses and limits who can see them. If you want the start of the file tidier too, see [client intake for small law firms](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/law-firm-client-intake/).

A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how requests go out and get followed up at your firm today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your email, your document storage, a spreadsheet and your case management software where it allows a connection), so your team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. If your volume is high enough that a records retrieval service makes more sense, we'll say so on the call.

### Does the workflow send requests without a person seeing them?
No. A person prepares and approves each request and each follow-up template. The workflow sends what was approved, on the dates you set, and logs it.

### Many providers only take fax or a portal. Does it still help?
Yes. Where a request can't be sent by email, the workflow creates the task, logs the date it was done and still runs the follow-up schedule and the weekly list.

That is a different job and not part of this workflow. Here AI only helps check that the records received cover the dates requested, and a person confirms it.

## Form E document collection for family solicitors: one checklist, fewer chasing emails
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/form-e-financial-disclosure-document-collection/

Form E document collection means getting a full set of financial papers from a client before the date for exchange. A simple workflow can send each client one checklist built from your own list, give them one place to upload, remind them about what is still missing and show the fee earner where every file stands. A solicitor still reviews every document and decides what goes into the form.

Form E documents arrive in pieces. The client sends three months of statements for one account, a photo of a payslip and a promise to find the pension paperwork. The paralegal writes back, the client sends two more things, and the list of what is still missing lives in someone's head. The date for exchange gets closer. Clients are going through a divorce and paperwork is the last thing they want to do, so they need short, kind, specific reminders. That part is routine, and it can run on its own while the solicitor does the advising.

### Why disclosure takes so long to collect
- The first email lists everything at once, and the client doesn't know where to start
- Statements arrive for part of the period, as screenshots or as dozens of separate files
- Some papers have to be requested from someone else, such as a pension provider or a lender, and the client hasn't asked yet
- Documents come by email, WhatsApp, post and in person, and get saved in different places
- Chasing depends on a paralegal who is also preparing three other files
- Nobody can say in one line what is missing for each client

### A Form E checklist you can copy
The form itself lists the documents to attach, so build your checklist from the current version on GOV.UK. For each bank account listed, it asks for statements covering the last 12 months. The other rows below are what firms commonly ask for; check each against the form and the client's circumstances. Form E1 and Form E2 are separate forms with their own lists.
| Document | Who the client gets it from | What to track |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Bank and savings statements, last 12 months, every account | Online banking or the bank | Each account separately, with the first and last date covered |
| Mortgage statement and property valuation | The lender and an estate agent | Requested, received |
| Payslips and the latest P60 | Their employer | Received, and whether the period matches your list |
| Pension valuation | Each pension provider | Date the client requested it, date it arrived |
| Business accounts, if self-employed or a company owner | Their accountant | Requested, received |
| Loan, credit card and other debt statements | Each lender | Each account separately |

### A reminder you can copy
Email to a client with items outstanding (edit the words in brackets):
```
Subject: Your financial documents: [number] items still to send

Dear [first name],

Thank you for what you have sent so far. We now have [list of items received].

We still need:
1. [Item, for example: statements for your savings account ending 1234, from [date] to [date]]
2. [Item]
3. [Item]

You can upload them here: [upload link]. Photos are fine if they are clear and show the whole page.

If you have asked your pension provider for a valuation, please tell us the date you asked, so we know when to expect it.

We need everything by [date] so that we can prepare your Form E in time. If anything on this list is hard to get, reply to this email or call [name] on [phone] and we will help.

Kind regards,
[name], [firm]
```

### How the workflow runs
1. When a matter reaches the disclosure stage, the fee earner ticks the items that apply to this client. The checklist is built from your firm's own list.
2. The client gets one email with the checklist in plain words and one secure upload link. Items they must request from someone else are marked, so they start those first.
3. Each upload is saved in the matter folder under the right item, and the checklist updates.
4. AI can read a statement's account and dates and say which months seem to be missing. A person checks that before the client is asked for anything.
5. Reminders go out on the schedule you choose and list only what is still missing. They stop when the item arrives or when a person pauses them.
6. Any reply from the client goes to the fee earner or paralegal. Nothing is answered automatically.
7. Each week the team gets one list: every disclosure file, what is missing and the date it is needed by.

### What stays with you
The advice, the form and every judgement about what a document shows. The workflow doesn't fill in Form E, doesn't decide what must be disclosed and doesn't talk to the other side. A solicitor approves the checklist, the wording and the timing, and can pause reminders for any client at any time, which matters when a client is struggling. The papers are sensitive, so they stay in the storage your firm already uses, with access limited to the people on the matter. The same routine works for other files that wait on a client: [source of funds in conveyancing](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/conveyancing-source-of-funds-document-chasing/) and [probate document collection](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/probate-document-collection/).

A [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) about how disclosure is collected at your firm today. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price and a clear definition of "working". It's built on the tools you already use (your email, your document storage and your case management software where it allows a connection), so the team doesn't learn a new system. Live in 2-3 days. [Workflow automation is a fixed $2,000](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/), and you pay once it's running and you're happy with it, under the [pay-when-happy agreement](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/agreement/). If your case management system already has a client portal that does this well, we'll say so on the call.

### Does the workflow fill in Form E?
No. It collects and organises the supporting documents. The form is completed by the client with their solicitor, and a solicitor reviews everything before it is used.
