Book a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) and we'll look at where email eats your week. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price. It's built on the tools you already use, in your own Google Workspace account, goes live in 2-3 days, and costs [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/) ($1,500 for the first 3 clients). You pay once it's running and you're happy with it. Anything AI drafts is approved by a person before it reaches a client.

### Can Gmail send an automatic reply to certain emails only?
Yes. Turn on templates under Settings, See all settings, Advanced, save your reply as a template, then create a filter with your criteria and tick Send template. Google's Gmail Help describes these steps (checked 11 November 2026).

### How many emails can I schedule in Gmail?
Google's Gmail Help says you can have up to 100 scheduled emails at once (checked 11 November 2026).

### Is Gemini in Gmail included in Google Workspace?
Google's help page lists Help me write and thread summaries for eligible Google Workspace plans, with some features, such as AI Inbox, US-only for now. Check your own plan, since availability varies by edition and country.

### Can Gmail chase clients who haven't sent their documents?
Not on its own. Filters act on email as it arrives, and nothing in Gmail tracks which client still owes you what. A workflow connected to your client list can send each client their own reminders and stop when the item arrives.

## Outlook automation for accountants: what Microsoft 365 already does
Source: https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/outlook-automation-for-accountants/ (2026-11-11)

Outlook automation for accountants covers rules that file, flag and forward email as it arrives, Quick Steps that do several actions in one click, saved templates and schedule send. Power Automate, which most Microsoft 365 business plans already include for standard connectors, can go further: save attachments to SharePoint or OneDrive, log requests in Excel and send reminders. What Outlook can't do alone is know which client still owes you which document.

Outlook automation for accountants is mostly about switching on what you already pay for. If the practice runs on Microsoft 365, Outlook has rules, Quick Steps, templates and schedule send, and Power Automate sits in the same account.
This post is for small accounting and bookkeeping practices in the UK and the US. Each feature was checked on Microsoft's support and Learn pages on 11 November 2026. Microsoft is moving people from classic Outlook to new Outlook, and some features work differently in each, so the differences are noted where they matter.

### What Outlook can do on its own
- Rules. Microsoft's support page says a rule needs a name, a condition and an action, for example moving mail from a sender to a folder or changing its importance. In new Outlook a rule runs on incoming mail; to apply it to mail already in a folder, use Run rule now in Settings, Mail, Rules.
- Quick Steps. One click, several actions: move to a client folder, mark as read and flag for follow-up, say. Microsoft's comparison page (updated 23 September 2026) lists Quick Steps as partially available in new Outlook and fully available in classic. Microsoft also notes that a Quick Step can't be undone with Ctrl+Z.
- Templates. New Outlook has two kinds. Mail Templates save a whole email, attachments included. The My Templates add-in stores short text snippets. Microsoft says both need a qualifying Microsoft 365 subscription.
- Schedule send. In new Outlook, pick Schedule send from the Send button. In classic Outlook, the Delay Delivery option holds the email in the Outbox, and Microsoft says Outlook has to be online and connected for it to go.
- Automatic replies. The out-of-office message, available in both versions.

### Classic vs new Outlook: what changes for a practice
Microsoft's feature comparison lists rules as partially available in new Outlook. Two details catch practices out. Some rules made in classic Outlook are client-side rules that new Outlook can't process, so you recreate them. And Microsoft says new Outlook doesn't support rules for third-party accounts such as Gmail, Yahoo and iCloud. COM add-ins and VBA macros aren't supported in new Outlook either, so an old macro that filed attachments will stop when you switch.
Before anyone moves to new Outlook, list your rules and any add-ins the practice relies on. It takes ten minutes and avoids a surprise in January.

### Copilot in Outlook
Microsoft's support pages describe Summarize, which summarises an email thread, and Draft with Copilot for writing replies. Which of these your users get depends on your licence. Microsoft offers both Copilot Chat and a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licence, and when we checked, its own pages weren't consistent about which Outlook features need the paid one. Check with whoever manages your Microsoft 365 account. Either way, it helps with the email in front of you, and a person should read any draft before it reaches a client.

### Power Automate: the part most practices haven't opened
Microsoft Learn (updated 22 September 2026) says basic Power Automate is included at no cost for work or school accounts, covering cloud flows with standard connectors only. The Office 365 Outlook connector is a standard connector. Its triggers include When a new email arrives (V3) and When a new email arrives in a shared mailbox (V2), and its actions include Send an email (V2), Send an email from a shared mailbox (V2) and Flag email (V2).
That covers the jobs Outlook rules can't do: save each attachment to the right SharePoint or OneDrive folder, add a row to an Excel tracker, or send a reminder on a schedule. Premium connectors, such as some accounting or CRM apps, need a paid licence. [Power Automate vs Zapier](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/power-automate-vs-zapier-small-business/) explains the licences, and who owns a flow when someone leaves. If you'd rather hand the build over, see [hiring a Power Automate expert](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/power-automate-consultant-small-business/). If your practice runs on Google Workspace instead, see [Gmail automation for accountants](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/gmail-automation-for-accountants/).

### Outlook on its own vs a workflow
| Practice task | Outlook on its own | Where a workflow adds value |
| --- | --- | --- |
| File client email | A rule moves it by sender or subject | Matches it to the client and the job, and logs it |
| Handle a document email in one go | A Quick Step: move, mark read, flag | Saves the attachment to the client's folder and ticks it off the list |
| Reply to common questions | Mail Templates or My Templates | Drafts with the client's name, deadline and missing items, for a person to approve |
| Send a request at the right time | Schedule send, one email at a time | Sends every client their own request on the date you set |
| Chase missing records | Not built in: a flag reminds you, not the client | Reminders that stop the moment the item arrives |
| Shared inbox (info@ or docs@) | Shared mailbox and rules | A flow on the shared mailbox that sorts, saves and reports what's still open |
| See who's outstanding | Search and flags | One daily list of clients with open items, from Excel or your practice software |

### Rules and Quick Steps worth setting up today
1. A rule for client documents: messages with attachments from outside the practice go to a To file folder, so nothing with an attachment gets buried in the inbox.
2. A rule for HMRC, IRS or software notices: move them to a Notices folder and mark them important, so they're read but don't crowd client email. Check the exact sender addresses on mail you've actually received.
3. A Quick Step called Filed: move to the client's folder, mark as read and clear the flag.
4. A Quick Step called Waiting on client: flag for follow-up next week and move to a Waiting folder.
5. A Mail Template for your standard records request, so the wording is the same every time.
6. A list of your rules and add-ins, kept somewhere the whole practice can see, before anyone moves to new Outlook.

### A records request template you can copy
The template keeps your wording consistent, but you still type each client's list by hand and remember to chase. For follow-up wording, see these [document chasing email templates](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/blog/document-chasing-email-templates/). To see which of these steps could run on their own in your practice, try the [plan builder](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/plan/).
Mail Template: records request:
```
Subject: Records for your [tax year] return

Hi [first name],

It's time to start your [tax year] return. Could you send us the following by [date]:

- [item 1]
- [item 2]
- [item 3]

You can reply to this email with the documents attached, or upload them here: [link].

If anything has changed this year, such as a new job, a property or a pension, just let us know in your reply.

Thanks,
[name]
[practice name]
```

### How Mike Automations would build it
Book a [free 15-minute call](https://mikeautomations.github.io/call/) and we'll look at where email eats your week. Within 48 hours you get a written plan with a fixed price that says which parts run in Outlook, which in Power Automate, and which licences, if any, you'd need. It's built on the tools you already use, in your own Microsoft 365 account, goes live in 2-3 days, and costs [$2,000 one-off](https://mikeautomations.github.io/en/pricing/) ($1,500 for the first 3 clients). You pay once it's running and you're happy with it.

### Do Outlook rules work in new Outlook?
Yes, but Microsoft lists rules as partially available in new Outlook (checked 11 November 2026). Some client-side rules from classic Outlook can't be processed and need recreating, and new Outlook doesn't support rules for third-party accounts such as Gmail.

### Is Power Automate included with Microsoft 365?
Basic Power Automate is. Microsoft Learn says work or school accounts can create and run cloud flows with standard connectors at no cost. The Office 365 Outlook, SharePoint and Excel Online (Business) connectors are standard. Premium connectors need a paid licence.

### Can Outlook chase clients automatically?
Not on its own. Rules act on email as it arrives and flags remind you, not the client. A Power Automate flow, or another workflow tool, can send each client reminders and stop when the documents arrive.

### Can I share Outlook templates with colleagues?
Microsoft's support page says templates saved in a shared mailbox that has been added as a full account in new Outlook can be viewed and edited by others who open that mailbox the same way. Templates in your own mailbox are only yours.
